job.title: Maintenance Technician - Olympus Alameda
job.description:
Maintenance work at a residential property demands a broad skill set used every single day. Plumbing one hour, HVAC diagnostics the next, then a lock change, then an appliance swap. At Olympus Alameda in Albuquerque, that's the actual rhythm of the role. If you like variety and can move between trades without losing your place, this position fits that way of working.

What the Work Requires

The core of this role is hands-on repair across multiple systems. You'll handle minor to moderate plumbing, electrical fixture and switch replacements, appliance repairs (refrigerators, stoves, washers, dryers, ovens, microwaves), lock systems, door hardware, and painting. Preventative maintenance on HVAC units is a regular responsibility, including filter changes and coil cleaning, so an EPA/HVAC certification is required before you start. A CPO certification is also required, since pool maintenance falls within your scope.

Beyond the unit work, you'll help maintain common areas and grounds, track service requests through property management software, and keep the maintenance shop organized and inventoried. You'll coordinate daily and weekly priorities with the Lead Maintenance Technician rather than setting your own schedule in isolation. That kind of structured communication keeps the team from doubling up or dropping tasks during busy stretches.

Full-time hours run Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, with some flexibility built in. Emergency on-call availability is part of the job. That part's worth naming plainly: after-hours calls happen, and this role expects you to respond when they do.

Experience and Credentials

  • Minimum 2 years of maintenance experience in commercial, residential, or apartment settings
  • EPA/HVAC certification (required)
  • CPO certification (required)
  • Familiarity with hand tools, power tools, and the range of repairs listed above
  • Comfort using software systems to log and track work orders

What Separates Strong Candidates

The technicians who do well in roles like this one tend to be self-directed once priorities are set, and they don't need to be walked through every repair. Two years of experience is the floor, but the quality of that experience matters more than the number. Someone who's done real make-ready work, turned units under time pressure, and handled HVAC diagnostics independently will move faster and more confidently than someone who's logged time without much variety.

Olympus Property has earned recognition from the National Apartment Association as a top employer in 2023, 2024, and 2025. The company places real weight on internal culture, team recognition, and career development. Eligible team members receive monthly and quarterly bonuses, and the benefits package includes medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer matching, an apartment rental allowance, tuition reimbursement, and a sabbatical program, among others. For a maintenance technician who wants to grow into a lead or supervisor role over time, those internal pathways are worth considering seriously.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
Apartment maintenance leadership works best when the supervisor carries real trade depth and still shows up with a wrench. That's the balance Weinstein Properties has refined across more than 70 years of family ownership and 60-plus communities in Virginia, Texas, and several other states. At Bexley Central Park in Grand Prairie, they're looking for a Maintenance Supervisor who can run a service team and stay hands-on with the work itself.

The Craft This Role Requires

This position draws on a specific combination of technical fluency and supervisory discipline. You need four or more years of trade experience covering HVAC, electrical, plumbing, carpentry, appliances, pool systems, and exterior structural work. EPA/CFC certification (Type I and II or Universal) is required before you start. Beyond the tools, you'll need at least one year of experience in an apartment maintenance lead, assistant supervisor, or supervisor role. Managing work orders through business software, scheduling turns, coordinating vendors, and communicating with the property management team via email are daily responsibilities, so basic computer proficiency is part of the job description.

On-call rotation is shared among team members, and a bonus is paid when you're carrying that responsibility. A valid driver's license, reliable transportation, and your own tools are all required.

What This Role Builds

Supervisors who thrive here develop sharper vendor management instincts, because you'll oversee both in-house technicians and outside contractors and learn to hold both accountable to the same quality standard. You'll also get practice using maintenance operations as a direct driver of occupancy. A well-run service team shortens turns, keeps delinquency from compounding into physical neglect, and gives leasing something real to point to during tours. Those cause-and-effect connections are the kind of knowledge that follows you through a career in property management.

Weinstein operates as an owner-manager rather than a third-party management company, which tends to mean more operational stability and a clearer internal promotion path. They state a genuine commitment to promoting from within and offer training for people who want to grow toward regional or multi-site roles.

Strong candidates will come in with a make-ready process they already own and can teach. The supervisors who separate themselves here aren't just technically capable. They run a punch list the same way every time, coach techs through unfamiliar repairs, and communicate with residents in a way that turns a service call into a retention moment.

  • 4+ years of trade experience across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and related systems
  • Minimum 1 year of apartment maintenance lead or supervisory experience
  • EPA/CFC certification, Type I and II or Universal
  • Comfort using work order and property management software
  • Valid driver's license, personal transportation, and hand tools
  • Willingness to participate in shared on-call rotation

Schedule is Monday through Friday, 8 AM to 5 PM, with on-call responsibilities shared across the team. Compensation is experience-based with quarterly and annual bonus opportunities. Benefits include health, dental, and vision insurance, a 401k with company match, PTO, paid holidays, birthday time off, an employee assistance program, and a rent discount.

job.title: Community Manager- Russellville Commons
job.description:
The leasing office closes at six, but a Community Manager's actual workday rarely does. At Russellville Commons in Portland, you might end an afternoon reviewing delinquency reports, then shift to coaching a leasing consultant through a difficult renewal conversation before the day wraps. The scope is real, and MG Properties is looking for someone who handles that scope without losing composure.

What the Role Covers

MG Properties has spent over 30 years acquiring, developing, and managing apartment communities across the Western U.S., and the Community Manager at Russellville Commons sits at the center of daily operations for the property. You'll carry full accountability for the site: building and developing your on-site team, executing the marketing strategy to drive traffic and maintain occupancy, and managing the budget with an eye toward NOI. Operational tasks span the full cycle of community management, from make-ready oversight and vendor relationships to resident satisfaction and lease administration. This is a team-leadership role as much as an operational one, and MG Properties expects its managers to actively develop the people around them, not just direct workflow.

Portland's multifamily market has softened from its pandemic-era highs, and operators here are watching concessions and MTM exposure more closely than they were two years ago. A manager who understands how to read a T-12, tighten delinquency without damaging resident relations, and adjust marketing spend in response to real traffic data will have a meaningful impact on performance at this property.

Qualifications

  • Recent, direct experience managing an apartment community (this is a firm requirement, not a preference)
  • Demonstrated supervisory experience, with the ability to hire, train, and hold a team accountable
  • Working knowledge of budgets, marketing, and sales in a residential property context
  • Yardi experience preferred
  • Valid driver's license and proof of insurance

Candidates who stand out in this type of role tend to combine financial fluency with genuine coaching instincts. Watching budget variance is one skill. Sitting down with a leasing associate after a slow week and identifying what's actually driving the gap is another. MG Properties' culture leans toward development and long-term growth, so managers who invest in their teams tend to fit well here.

Compensation includes monthly and performance-based incentive bonuses, company profit sharing, a 401(k) with employer match, and a full benefits package covering medical, dental, vision, life insurance, and flexible spending accounts. Paid time off includes 10 days of PTO, 10 paid holidays, 2 personal days, and 40 hours of paid sick time annually. Rental discounts are also available.

job.title: Customer Experience Manager
job.description:
It's move-in weekend at a 500-plus-bed student community in College Station, and the lobby is buzzing. Parents are asking questions, residents are checking in, and your team is the first impression Scion makes on every single one of them. That's the center of gravity for this role.

The Role at Lark Northgate and Z Islander

The Customer Experience Manager sits at the intersection of leasing performance, resident satisfaction, and day-to-day operations across two larger student communities in the Bryan/College Station market. This isn't a pure leasing role and it isn't purely administrative. You'll carry responsibility for driving revenue goals through customer experience initiatives while also coaching the Experience Team, keeping tabs on facilities feedback, and executing marketing strategies that generate traffic to the property.

On any given week, you might be running a market survey, pulling KPIs to spot a delinquency trend before it becomes a problem, reviewing punch list items from a unit inspection, or planning an on-campus event tied to a lease-up push. Annual turn at a student property this size is a serious undertaking, and you'll work closely with the General Manager, Assistant General Manager, and Facilities Supervisor to plan and execute it successfully. Move-in and move-out coordination are part of that cycle.

The social media piece is more than checkbox marketing. Student residents in this market are active on Instagram, TikTok, and Facebook, and you'll be expected to develop and execute strategies on those platforms that actually connect with the demographic, not just post for the sake of posting.

What Scion Is Looking For

  • A college degree preferred, with at least two years of experience in customer service, sales, or community management
  • Comfort working up to six days per week during peak periods, including turn season and move-in
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills across all levels of the organization
  • Familiarity with property management systems, with Entrata experience being a plus
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities without constant direction
  • A genuine commitment to fair housing compliance and a supportive approach to a diverse living and working environment

Student housing in the Bryan/College Station market runs on a tight annual cycle tied to Texas A&M's academic calendar. Properties here fill or struggle to fill during a compressed leasing window, and traffic patterns are highly seasonal. Candidates who understand how to build momentum early in that cycle, and sustain occupancy through renewal season, will find this role well-suited to those instincts.

The CXM role is a natural bridge toward a General Manager position for someone who builds credibility across the leasing, operations, and people management dimensions of this job. Scion operates at scale in the student living space, which means the internal career path is real if the performance is there.

job.title: Leasing Consultant (Saltwood)
job.description:
Leasing Consultant roles at apartment communities tend to look similar on paper, but the companies running them vary enormously in how much they invest in the people doing the work. At Prometheus Real Estate Group's Saltwood community in Portland, this position sits at the intersection of sales, resident relations, and property operations. That combination makes it one of the better entry points into a long-term property management career.

What the Role Actually Covers

Prometheus calls this position a Neighbor Ambassador, and the title reflects a real expectation: you're not just processing applications and handing over keys. You're guiding prospective residents through the leasing process from first inquiry to signed agreement, while also keeping current residents connected to the community in ways that make them want to stay. The customer service and sales functions aren't siloed. They run together constantly.

On the administrative side, you'll get exposure to the operational mechanics of property management. That includes preparing rental agreements, tracking and reporting on leasing activity, conducting market surveys, and managing apartment advertising. For someone newer to the industry, this breadth matters. Most leasing roles teach you traffic and tours. This one adds the back-end habits that make you a stronger candidate for an Assistant Manager role down the road.

One realistic note on scheduling: weekends are required. Portland apartment traffic peaks Saturday and Sunday, and that's when Prometheus needs its leasing team present. Your days off will fall during the week. If your life accommodates that, it's a straightforward trade. If it doesn't, it's worth considering before applying.

Who Tends to Excel Here

Prometheus explicitly recruits from outside property management, and that's not a gap-filler strategy. People coming from retail, hospitality, or service-industry backgrounds often carry strong instincts around customer experience that translate directly into leasing. What separates strong candidates isn't necessarily PM knowledge. It's follow-through on details, comfort with a sales conversation that spans multiple touchpoints, and the ability to stay organized when you're managing several prospects at different stages of the leasing cycle simultaneously.

  • Hourly rate between $21.75 and $22.50, plus a weekend shift premium
  • $200 per lease incentive and a discretionary semi-annual bonus
  • Additional bonus opportunities tied to lease-up performance, referrals, and training
  • Medical, vision, and dental covered at 100% by the company, including dependents on base plans
  • 401(k) with employer matching and tuition reimbursement
  • Tenure-based housing discounts and paid volunteer time

Where This Role Can Take You

For someone willing to learn the administrative and reporting side of the job alongside the leasing work, this position builds the foundation for an Assistant Community Manager or Leasing Manager path within a few years. You'll develop fluency in occupancy management, market positioning, and resident retention before most people in comparable roles get exposure to any of those things. Prometheus's size and portfolio also means internal mobility is a real option, not an afterthought. The skills you build here compound quickly if you treat the administrative work as seriously as the sales conversations.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
The assistant community manager role exists because running an apartment community is genuinely too much for one person. The Community Manager carries strategic accountability, but the day-to-day rhythm of resident interactions, leasing traffic, ledger accuracy, and team momentum requires a second-in-command who can own their portion of the operation rather than just assist with it. At Hawthorne Residential Partners, a Southeast-rooted multifamily company ranked among the country's 50 largest, that distinction matters. This is a real operational partnership, not a clerical support role dressed up with a nice title.

The position is based at Elevate the Crossings in Fuquay-Varina, NC, and carries a schedule that reflects how leasing offices actually work: Monday through Friday with a rotating weekday off, Saturdays from 10 to 4, and occasional evening availability for resident events.

What You're Responsible For

On the leasing side, you'll guide prospects through tours and the application process, work on renewals, and help hit occupancy goals through both new leases and resident retention. You'll also manage the community's social media presence, which at most properties has become a real driver of engagement and referral traffic.

The financial piece carries more weight here than in a pure leasing role. You'll post payments, monitor delinquency, run weekly follow-up calls on past-due accounts, review ledgers for accuracy, and coordinate eviction procedures when they're necessary. If your experience is mostly front-desk leasing, this is the area to strengthen before applying.

When the Community Manager is out, you run the office. That means keeping the team focused, decisions moving, and residents served at the same standard they'd expect any other day.

Who Fits Well Here

  • Two years of property management experience, with at least six months in an assistant manager capacity preferred
  • Comfort reading financial reports and translating them into decisions
  • A track record of de-escalating resident conflicts without letting things drag on
  • Valid driver's license; CALP designation is a plus
  • High school diploma or GED equivalent

Compensation includes hourly pay plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions, quarterly performance bonuses, and access to Hawthorne's career path program. The company has a stated track record of promoting from within, and the assistant manager seat is the most direct pipeline to a Community Manager role. If you're in this position and performing well, that next step is a realistic near-term goal rather than a distant one.

The candidate who stands out at this level typically combines financial comfort with genuine resident service instincts. Delinquency calls and difficult lease terminations are part of the job, and the people who do this work well are the ones who can be firm and fair in the same conversation without letting either quality undermine the other.

job.title: Maintenance Technician II at The Marq Highland Park Apartments
job.description:
A resident puts in a request at 7 a.m.: no hot water. By 8, you've already diagnosed the water heater, sourced the part, and updated the work order. That's the rhythm of this role.

The Work

Cottonwood Residential is hiring a Maintenance Technician II for The Marq Highland Park Apartments in Westchase, Florida. This is an intermediate-level position, which means you're expected to work independently on most repairs without needing the supervisor to walk you through it. You'll handle the full range of service requests: HVAC diagnosis and repair, plumbing, electrical fixtures, appliances, and carpentry. You'll also contribute to the make-ready process, getting vacant units turned and ready for incoming residents.

Beyond service requests, the role includes preventative maintenance on building systems, regular property walks to keep grounds and common areas in good condition, and support for pool and spa upkeep. You'll document completed work in the property management system and stay in communication with the Maintenance Supervisor on anything that needs escalation or additional resources.

On-call rotation is part of the job. After-hours emergencies happen, and you'll be expected to respond when it's your turn. The supervisor provides backup, but residents count on the team to show up.

What Qualifies You

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • 2 or more years of multifamily maintenance experience
  • EPA Type II or Universal certification (required)
  • Solid hands-on knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, electrical, appliances, and pool/spa systems
  • CPO certification (preferred)
  • Ability to lift up to 75 lbs. regularly; weights over 50 lbs. should be handled with assistance
  • Availability for evenings, weekends, and on-call shifts
  • Basic tools required; HVAC gauges required if EPA certified

The candidates who stand out here aren't necessarily the ones with the longest resume. They're the ones who can walk into an unfamiliar problem, think through it systematically, and fix it right the first time. Multifamily maintenance moves fast, and units that sit down cost money and frustrate residents. Technicians who close work orders cleanly, communicate clearly, and leave the work area better than they found it are the ones who earn trust on a team like this.

Cottonwood Residential operates a national multifamily portfolio, so there's genuine room to grow within the organization for technicians who perform well and build their skills over time.

job.title: Maintenance Technician (Nantucket Cove)
job.description:
Skills That Drive This Role

Maintenance work at a residential community draws on a wider range of skills than most people expect. On any given day at Nantucket Cove, you might be diagnosing an HVAC issue in the morning, running a plumbing repair after lunch, and closing out work orders on electrical or structural items before the end of your shift. The technical range is real. So is the need to stay organized, prioritize well, and communicate clearly with residents who are waiting on repairs that affect their daily lives.

Preventative maintenance is a significant part of the job. You'll document conditions, catch problems before they escalate, and keep the property running in a way that protects both resident satisfaction and the asset itself. That documentation habit matters more than it sounds. Technicians who stay ahead of issues keep turn costs down and reduce emergency calls, which benefits the whole team.

What You'll Bring

  • Two to three years of hands-on maintenance experience in a residential or similar setting
  • Comfort working across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and general structural repairs
  • EPA Type 2 or Universal certification (preferred, not required)
  • A valid driver's license and a high school diploma or equivalent
  • The physical stamina for a role that keeps you on your feet, climbing, lifting, and moving throughout the day
  • Clear communication with residents and teammates alike

After-hours emergency support is part of the position. That's worth naming honestly. The expectation is that residents feel taken care of when something goes wrong outside of normal hours, so the ability to respond calmly and effectively under pressure matters here.

What Makes BAM Different to Work For

BAM Companies has been operating since 2010, and their internal culture is built around what they call BAMFAM, a genuine emphasis on team cohesion and loyalty that shows up in how they staff and support their properties. For a maintenance technician, that means you're part of a team that invests in your success rather than cycling through people. The pay range for this role runs from $17 to $19 per hour depending on experience and qualifications.

The benefits package is competitive for the market. You'll get medical, dental, and vision coverage with BAM carrying a larger share of the cost, paid life insurance, and a PTO structure that starts with 14.5 paid holidays plus 88 hours of PTO after your first 90 days, growing to 120 hours after year one. There's also a rent discount available if you want to live on a BAM property, which some technicians find genuinely convenient.

One thing that separates strong candidates here from adequate ones: the ability to take ownership without being told. Nantucket Cove residents notice the difference between a technician who closes the ticket and one who genuinely solves the problem and follows up. That initiative, combined with solid technical range, is what tends to stick at a company like BAM.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Museum District, Houston, TX
job.description:
Maintenance techs at apartment communities wear a lot of hats. At Plaza Museum District, a Berkshire Residential property in Houston's Museum District, you're not just fixing things. You're the person residents see when something's wrong, which means your attitude matters as much as your tool belt.

What the Work Looks Like Day to Day

Your time splits between completing work orders, supporting make-readies, and keeping the property's physical condition where it needs to be. Curb appeal and common areas fall under your watch. You'll help manage shop inventory, equipment upkeep, and key security, which sounds routine until something's missing at the wrong moment. You'll also back up the management team on enforcing safety standards and community policies, and you'll be expected to document and communicate clearly, both in writing and in person.

The role calls for working knowledge across appliances, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, and general building systems. You don't need to be a licensed specialist in every trade, but you do need enough hands-on experience to diagnose problems quickly and know when something's beyond your scope. A minimum of one year working maintenance in a residential community is expected.

What's Honest About the Job

Maintenance work at an apartment community is physical, repetitive on some days, and genuinely unpredictable on others. Residents don't always report issues at convenient times, and the punch list before a unit turn rarely shrinks on its own. The Museum District location means you're working near a dense, active part of Houston, which brings its own pace. If you prefer a job where the problems are always straightforward and the hours are always predictable, this one will test you.

That said, this is also a role where strong techs build real credibility fast. You see the whole property. You learn what breaks, how often, and why. That operational knowledge is exactly what carries into lead tech or service manager roles over time.

What Berkshire Offers

Berkshire owns and manages its own properties rather than operating as a third-party manager, which tends to create more consistency in how decisions get made at the site level. Benefits include three weeks of vacation, personal development planning, health insurance, and a 25% rent discount for employees.

  • At least one year of residential maintenance experience
  • Hands-on knowledge of plumbing, electrical, appliances, carpentry, and general building systems
  • Proficiency in written and spoken English
  • Comfort using computers and property management-related software
  • Reliable, detail-oriented, and resident-focused approach to the work

Berkshire is an equal opportunity employer committed to fair treatment across race, color, creed, national origin, age, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, and all other protected categories.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Manager
job.description:
Fairstead runs a portfolio of more than 30,000 apartments across 28 states, and the work is genuinely affordable housing, not market-rate with a mission statement attached. They develop, build, and manage under one roof, which means the maintenance operation connects directly to long-term community preservation rather than short-term asset turnover. That context matters if you're the kind of tech who cares where their work ends up.

This posting is a pipeline role. Fairstead is building out its bench of Maintenance Managers ahead of new community launches and portfolio growth, so the location isn't fixed yet. If you apply now and clear the process, you're positioned to be considered first when a site comes online. That's either appealing or it isn't, depending on your timeline.

The Service Manager title is what Fairstead calls this position internally. The core job is what you'd expect: supervise a maintenance crew, keep mechanical systems and electrical equipment running, lead on special projects, and make sure the property stays clean and safe in line with company standards. You'll handle routine work independently and pull in support for the more complex stuff. Overtime happens, usually tied to emergencies or project deadlines, and that's worth stating plainly rather than burying.

What separates a strong candidate here from an average one is the combination of trade depth and crew management. Fairstead wants someone proficient in a specific trade who can also run a team, not a generalist who's decent at everything and exceptional at nothing. If you've spent years as a tech and recently stepped into a lead role, that trajectory fits. If you've been a solo maintenance tech on a small property, the supervision piece will be the gap to address.

Qualifications

  • At least three years of property maintenance experience
  • Proficiency in at least one skilled trade, with broader general maintenance ability
  • Solid understanding of building and mechanical trade tools, techniques, and terminology
  • Knowledge of safety standards and accident prevention practices
  • Experience supervising or leading maintenance staff
  • Ability to implement and refine maintenance policies and procedures
  • Comfortable with Microsoft Office Suite; Yardi or RealPage experience is a plus
  • Strong organizational and project management skills

Fairstead uses Yardi and RealPage across its portfolio, and comfort with work order software matters more in affordable housing than people sometimes assume. When you're managing deferred maintenance on an older asset while keeping units habitable, digital tracking of open items isn't optional.

Benefits include medical coverage through Meritain Health with a generous employer contribution, employer-paid vision and life insurance, a 401(k) with a company match (100% on the first 3%, 50% on the next 2%), 15 days of PTO, 7 sick days, 12-plus paid holidays, FSA, disability insurance, pet insurance, and employee discounts on appliances and apparel.

job.title: Community Manager (Cottonwood Creek)
job.description:
Managing a 168-unit portfolio across two sites sounds straightforward on paper. In practice, it means splitting your week between Cottonwood Creek in Littleton and Elowyn Townhomes in Denver, keeping occupancy tight, delinquency low, and two onsite teams pulling in the same direction. RedPeak has operated in Denver for 24 years, and this role sits squarely in their owner-operator model, which means decisions move faster and accountability runs deeper than at a third-party shop.

What the Role Actually Covers

Your schedule runs Monday, Wednesday, and Friday at Cottonwood Creek (8801 W Belleview Ave, Littleton) and Tuesday and Thursday at Elowyn Townhomes (4725 W Quincy Ave, Denver). Splitting your week across two assets keeps the operational rhythm interesting but demands strong systems. You'll own the financial performance at both sites: budgeting, variance reporting, NOI oversight, and keeping an eye on the T-12 so nothing creeps up on you at month-end. Delinquency management, lease renewals, and concession strategy all fall under your scope, along with coordinating make-readies and tracking maintenance through to completion.

You'll lead an onsite team, which means coaching, accountability, and setting the standard for resident experience at both properties. RedPeak's philosophy is that residents should be treated like neighbors, and that expectation flows from the Community Manager down.

  • Proven experience in market-rate residential property management
  • Financial literacy: budgeting, reporting, and NOI-focused decision making
  • Comfort with property management technology across leasing, communications, and financials
  • Strong team leadership and the ability to motivate staff across multiple locations
  • Customer service instincts that translate into measurable resident satisfaction

Compensation and Benefits

Base salary runs $60,000 to $75,000, with bonus potential on top of that. Benefits include full medical, dental, and vision, a 401(k) with company match that vests on day one, 16 PTO days, 10 paid holidays, and a 20% rent discount. RedPeak also offers a student debt repayment program, monthly maintenance bonuses, cell phone reimbursement, and up to $75 monthly toward a health club membership.

Where This Role Can Take You

Community Managers who handle multi-site portfolios build skills that translate directly into area manager and regional roles. Managing two assets simultaneously, each with its own budget, team, and resident base, gives you the reps that a single-site role doesn't. Candidates who tend to stand out in roles like this track their own numbers proactively: occupancy, traffic-to-lease conversion, renewal rates. If you're waiting for a regional to tell you your delinquency is up, that's the gap between average and strong at this level. RedPeak's Denver-focused footprint also means you're building market knowledge in a single MSA, which compounds over time in ways that jumping between markets doesn't.

job.title: Sales and Revenue Manager
job.description:
Student housing sales runs on a different clock than conventional multifamily. The leasing season compresses into months, traffic spikes are short and unforgiving, and a weak conversion rate in October can haunt your occupancy numbers all the way to August move-in. PeakMade Real Estate is hiring a Sales and Revenue Manager to own that entire performance cycle at their West Lafayette community, a market anchored by Purdue University and its consistent enrollment demand.

What This Role Actually Manages

This is the onsite sales lead. You're responsible for occupancy, renewal rates, and revenue growth, and you're expected to build the strategies that get you there, not just execute someone else's playbook. That means developing leasing strategies tied to real targets, monitoring conversion metrics at every stage of the lead lifecycle, and identifying underperformance early enough to course-correct before it damages the T-12.

Pricing and concessions decisions happen in partnership with regional and property leadership, but your read on the competitive set matters here. You'll monitor competitor pricing, track market conditions, and bring data-backed recommendations to those conversations. Knowing when to hold rate and when a targeted concession closes the gap on occupancy is a judgment call this role makes regularly.

On the lead management side, you're watching response times, tracking source performance, and working with marketing on campaigns that align with leasing objectives by season. Student housing has specific buying behavior worth noting: parents often co-sign and heavily influence decisions, urgency peaks around roommate matching and early-bird incentives, and reputation management on platforms like Google and ApartmentRatings carries real weight with incoming freshmen and transfers. Experience in that environment matters.

Team Leadership and Coaching

You'll recruit, train, and coach leasing team members, and you'll set clear expectations around outreach activity, tour conversion, application rates, and renewal closing. Regular sales coaching and performance reviews are part of the cadence. The expectation is that you can identify why a leasing consultant isn't converting and fix it, through coaching, role-playing, process adjustment, or some combination of all three.

Renewal strategy also sits in this role. That means segmenting the resident base, building targeted messaging and incentives, and coordinating with operations to address the retention risks that often live outside the leasing office entirely.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • 3 or more years in student housing, multifamily, or high-volume sales, with at least one year leading or coaching a leasing or sales team
  • Documented results: occupancy targets met, renewal rates improved, revenue goals hit
  • Fluency with CRM and property management platforms (Entrata, Yardi, RealPage, Knock, Funnel, or EliseAI are all relevant here)
  • Comfort presenting leasing reports, performance data, and action plans to ownership groups and senior leadership
  • Experience with pricing strategy or revenue management discussions at the asset level
  • Ability to work through turn season and peak leasing periods when the pace demands it

The candidates who stand out aren't just strong closers. They understand the full funnel, they can coach others to close, and they know how to create urgency in a way that protects the brand rather than undermining it. Overpromising during a lease-up is easy. Doing it without creating operational headaches or reputation damage takes real discipline.

PeakMade offers commission structures tied to monthly, quarterly, and annual performance, a housing discount, mentorship access, up to 12 weeks of paid parental leave, PTO plus two additional wellbeing days, 401(k) matching, and leadership development opportunities across their national portfolio of student, multifamily, and build-to-rent communities.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager Manufactured Housing Community
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is an operations and sales hybrid role at Richland Mobile Home Park, a 334-home manufactured housing community in Richland, Washington. Investment Property Group, headquartered in Park City, Utah, owns and operates 150 properties across 13 states, and this community sits within a portfolio that spans multifamily, manufactured home, and RV assets.

Day to day, you'll support the Community Manager across the full range of site operations. That means conducting property walks to document and address common area conditions, handling resident concerns and complaints, and keeping delinquency managed through consistent follow-up and accurate ledger maintenance. When accounts escalate, you'll coordinate eviction proceedings as needed. On the leasing and sales side, you'll run community tours, move prospective buyers through the home purchase process, and manage the application and waitlist workflow from inquiry through move-in. Occasional weekend hours support open houses and pool operations, with adjusted weekday hours to keep your week at 40 hours total.

You'll also assist with unit inspections, coordinate maintenance requests with vendors, and participate in any regulatory meetings or agency inspections that affect the property.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of experience in an assistant or support role at a manufactured housing or multifamily community of 100 or more homes
  • Hands-on experience with rent collection and delinquency management
  • Comfort with property management software, ideally Manage America, Rent Café, Blue Moon, or similar platforms
  • Strong conflict resolution skills and a customer service approach that fits a community demographic where residents are long-term, owner-occupied households
  • Sales ability to present and move available homes, not just lease vacant lots
  • Valid driver's license

Context Worth Knowing

Manufactured housing communities operate differently from conventional multifamily. Residents often own their homes and lease the land beneath them, which changes the nature of the relationship and the sales cycle. When a home comes available, you're part of a process closer to real estate sales than traditional leasing. Richland sits in the Tri-Cities area of eastern Washington, a market with steady demand from the energy and federal contracting sectors tied to the Hanford site. Occupancy in well-run manufactured housing communities in smaller regional markets like this tends to be durable, but it requires active sales effort when homes do turn.

The pay range for this role is $24.00 to $28.00 per hour depending on experience and qualifications. IPG offers medical, dental, and vision coverage, life insurance, an HSA, an employee assistance program, a 401k with company match, and four weeks of accrued PTO.

Candidates who tend to succeed in assistant manager roles at manufactured housing communities come from backgrounds where they've handled both the relational and administrative sides of property management without leaning heavily on one or the other. The combination of sales follow-through and delinquency discipline is harder to find than either skill alone.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Champion Hills at Windyke is a residential community in Memphis, and Makowsky Ringel Greenberg needs a maintenance technician who can carry real responsibility from day one. This is a full trade role, not a helper position. You'll work independently across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, appliance repair, and lock work, and you'll be expected to handle those systems with confidence rather than escalate most things to a supervisor.

What You'll Actually Do

A typical week moves between reactive repairs and scheduled work. Make-readies keep the turns moving between residents, and preventive maintenance keeps the systems from failing in the first place. You'll handle lock re-keying and installation, respond to plumbing and electrical calls, and document your work daily. Rotating weekend on-call is part of the schedule, so after-hours calls do happen. That's just honest.

The role carries a fuel allowance because you'll use your own vehicle to get to and from the property and service calls. MRG also includes a $1,000 sign-on bonus, an annual bonus structure, paid time off, holidays, and a full benefits package covering medical, dental, vision, disability, life insurance, AFLAC options, and a 401(k) with profit sharing.

What You Bring

  • HVAC certification is required. Universal certification is preferred and will matter in the hiring conversation.
  • At least two years of apartment maintenance experience, meaning you've handled the full range of residential repair work, not just one trade.
  • Solid working knowledge of common tools, appliances, and mechanical systems.
  • Familiarity with applicable building codes and OSHA safety practices. Documentation is part of the job, so you need to be comfortable with that side of it too.
  • A reliable vehicle, valid driver's license, and proof of insurance.
  • Ability to pass background, credit, and drug screenings.

Strong candidates also bring organization and time management. When you've got three open work orders, a make-ready punch list, and a resident waiting on a callback, the techs who stay steady are the ones who prioritize well and communicate clearly. Customer service matters here because residents notice how you show up in their home, not just whether the repair got done.

Context Worth Knowing

Makowsky Ringel Greenberg has been managing properties in the Memphis market for decades. Working for an established local operator tends to mean clearer processes, institutional knowledge on the maintenance side, and a management team that understands the market. For a technician who wants stability and a legitimate path toward a lead or facilities management role, that kind of operator tends to offer more runway than a smaller shop or a national REIT where the local team is thin. If you've got the HVAC cert and the hands-on background, this is a role worth taking seriously.

job.title: Maintance Supervisor
job.description:
CommonPlace puts a real emphasis on the idea that a home is more than just an apartment unit. That framing matters for this role because a Maintenance Supervisor here isn't just keeping equipment running. The condition of every hallway, every make-ready, every courtyard reflects directly on whether residents feel like they actually belong somewhere. That's the standard you're working to.

Day to day, this job is split between leading people and doing physical work yourself. You'll schedule and supervise your team, review their work, and step in alongside them when needed. Vendor oversight is part of it too. When a contractor is on site, you're the one accountable for the quality of what they deliver. You'll manage parts inventory, keep MSDS logs current, and make sure the shop stays organized enough that the next person who needs a tool can actually find it. Turns (make-readies) are a core part of the rhythm here. Units need to be genuinely move-in ready, and that punch list responsibility lands with you.

The on-call piece is worth being direct about. Emergencies don't follow business hours, and you'll be in the rotation. That's a real part of the job. The same goes for being the person who handles lock changes after evictions or responds when something breaks down on a weekend. If you've worked in property maintenance before, none of this is a surprise. But if it's new information, it should factor into your decision.

CommonPlace is also looking for someone who communicates clearly with the Property Manager, flags unusual findings early, and keeps OSHA and company safety policies in place consistently, not just during inspections. That last part separates supervisors who actually build team habits from ones who just check boxes.

What CommonPlace Is Looking For

  • 3 to 5 years of hands-on maintenance experience, ideally in residential property management
  • 1 to 3 years in a supervisory role
  • Working knowledge of plumbing, electrical, HVAC, PTAC units, appliances, and general construction
  • Comfortable with hand tools, power tools, and motorized or electrical equipment
  • Able to regularly lift, carry, or maneuver up to 50 lbs independently
  • Valid driver's license with proof of automobile liability insurance
  • Availability for on-call rotation and a flexible schedule

Pay runs $26 to $28 per hour, with medical, dental, and 401(k) benefits, plus paid vacation, sick time, and volunteer time.

One thing worth noting for candidates considering the supervisory side of this role: the strongest applicants tend to be people who've already had to hold a team accountable to a quality standard, not just complete work orders themselves. Training a newer tech to do a turn correctly takes different skills than doing the turn yourself. If that part of the job genuinely interests you, this is a role where it's a significant part of the work.

job.title: Community Relations Manager - Cortland Pembroke Pines
job.description:
Cortland sits inside the top 10 multifamily owners and operators in the country, and the Community Relations Manager role at their Pembroke Pines property puts you at the intersection of two things that drive NOI: occupancy and resident retention. If you're thinking about where a role like this leads, that answer matters as much as the day-to-day.

The position carries real operational weight. You'll support the Community Manager on daily site operations, conduct inspections across vacant units, make-ready apartments, and model homes, and keep vendor relationships calibrated so turns stay on schedule and quality holds. This isn't administrative support in a passive sense. You're the person who catches a punch list issue before a prospective resident does, or flags a curb appeal problem before it shows up in a review. That kind of attentiveness compounds over time into the habits that make a strong community manager.

On the revenue side, you're actively working a leasing pipeline. That means following up with prospects, tracking conversion metrics in the CRM, and closing leases using consultative techniques rather than high-pressure scripts. Cortland's approach is consultative by design: uncover what the prospect actually needs, then connect that need to what the community offers. Strong candidates in roles like this treat their pipeline with the same discipline a sales rep would, because that's essentially what this is. Leasing velocity and follow-up consistency are what separate people who hit their KPIs from those who explain why they didn't.

The resident experience component rounds out the role. You'll plan engagement events, manage the community's social media presence, handle objections from current and prospective residents, and generally function as the face people associate with living there. That relationship-building skill transfers directly if you move into a Community Manager seat, where retention rates and delinquency trends reflect how well the team has connected with residents over time.

Pembroke Pines sits in a competitive South Florida submarket where Class A properties compete hard on experience because the product differences across communities are often narrow. The ability to create a genuine sense of community, rather than just processing applications, matters here more than in slower markets.

What Cortland is looking for

  • At least two years of measurable sales success, ideally in multifamily, hospitality, luxury retail, or a comparable high-velocity environment
  • Proven pipeline management habits and a track record of hitting or beating leasing targets
  • Comfort with property management software, CRM systems, and social media as a marketing tool
  • Strong communication skills and the kind of professional presence that reflects a premium brand
  • Working knowledge of Fair Housing guidelines and basic operational compliance
  • High school diploma required; bachelor's degree preferred

For someone early in their property management career, this role builds the exact combination of sales discipline and operational awareness that Community Manager positions require. It's a role where the skills you develop are directly portable, and at a company with Cortland's portfolio scale, internal mobility is a real path rather than a talking point.

job.title: Onsite Project Manager
job.description:
This role lives at the intersection of construction knowledge and field coordination. The Onsite Project Manager at Asset Living's Omaha location needs to read plans, hold subcontractors accountable, and keep a renovation schedule moving, all at the same time. If those three things feel natural to you, read on.

What This Role Calls On Daily

The core skills here are schedule management, vendor coordination, and quality control. You'll interpret project plans and specifications, track construction progress against contract documents, and compile submittals for the Senior Construction Project Manager's review. You're not just walking the site, you're the person who catches deviations before they become expensive problems.

Subcontractor management takes up a meaningful chunk of your time. That means reviewing proposals, confirming contract compliance, and coordinating work sequencing so trades aren't stacking on top of each other. Strong written and verbal communication is non-negotiable since you're the daily point of contact between the field and the broader project team.

Multifamily renovation experience is a genuine advantage here. Understanding how an occupied or recently vacated unit moves through a make-ready or full rehab cycle, and what quality benchmarks matter at each stage, lets you set expectations with subs rather than just report on what they did.

Qualifications Worth Highlighting

  • High school diploma or equivalent required
  • Certified Apartment Manager (CAM) or Accredited Resident Manager (ARM) designation preferred
  • Previous multifamily renovation supervision experience strongly preferred
  • Ability to read and interpret project plans and specifications
  • Comfortable with independent judgment and real-time problem solving on-site
  • Basic computer skills and familiarity with project or property management software
  • Willingness to travel and flexibility with hours when deadlines require it
  • Ability to lift up to 25 pounds; regular standing, walking, and physical presence on the job site

Why This Role at Asset Living

Asset Living is a third-party management firm ranked in the NMHC top 50, with a portfolio spanning multifamily, build-to-rent, affordable housing, and student housing. The Onsite Project Manager reports directly to a Senior Construction Project Manager, which means you get structure and a clear escalation path, but you're expected to own the day-to-day without hand-holding.

One thing candidates often underestimate about this type of role: the documentation discipline matters as much as the field presence. Submittals, schedule updates, and quality control records are how you demonstrate that work conforms to contract. Candidates who treat paperwork as secondary to "getting things done" tend to struggle. The ones who thrive treat both as the same job.

job.title: Business Manager - 207 East
job.description:
Skills at the Center of This Role

The Business Manager position at 207 East, an Olympus Property community in Edgewood, WA, pulls from a wide stack of competencies at once. Financial analysis, team leadership, marketing execution, and physical asset oversight all run in parallel here. This isn't a role where one skill dominates. You're reading T-12 reports and then walking a punch list and then coaching a leasing agent on closing technique, sometimes within the same morning. If you've been operating as a property manager and wondering whether your skills are actually broad enough to move up, this role answers that question quickly.

The financial side carries real weight. You'll own budget forecasting, variance analysis, monthly performance reviews with regional leadership, and annual asset business plans. That means you need to understand not just what the numbers say but why they moved, and you need to articulate that clearly to a Regional Manager and Regional VP. Managers who can connect occupancy trends, concessions strategy, and NOI in a single conversation tend to stand out here. That fluency compounds over time into what owners and investors actually want in a senior operator.

What You'll Be Managing Day to Day

The property is Class A, and the expectations that come with that tier are real. Make-ready standards, amenity presentation, and resident experience all reflect on asset value directly. You'll oversee both office and maintenance staff, which means your leadership has to work across different work cultures and priorities. Training, mentoring, scheduling, and holding people accountable are constant, not periodic.

On the leasing side, you'll supervise renewal and retention programs aimed at keeping occupancy tight. You'll also take ownership of vendor relationships: bidding contracts, negotiating terms, and managing performance on both recurring service agreements and one-time capital projects. The ability to read a vendor proposal critically is a skill that carries significant value as you move into district-level or asset management roles later in your career.

  • Minimum two years of multifamily property management experience required; Class A luxury experience is preferred
  • RealPage, Knock, and Onesite software familiarity is strongly preferred
  • Full-time Monday through Friday schedule with hours varying between 8:00 AM and 6:00 PM; flexibility for after-hours resident events and emergencies

What Makes Olympus a Specific Fit Worth Considering

Olympus Property has been recognized by the National Apartment Association as a top employer three consecutive years (2023, 2024, 2025). That kind of consistency in employee recognition usually reflects actual culture investment rather than a one-time survey spike. They offer structured career pathing, leadership conferences, and budget camp, which signals that they're investing in operators who want to move into regional or executive roles, not just fill a property-level seat.

Compensation starts at $80,000 annually, with monthly commissions and quarterly and annual bonus eligibility layered on top. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, and an apartment rental allowance, among others.

For a property manager who's been executing well at the site level and wants a company that actually tracks career progression, the structure here is worth taking seriously.

job.title: Senior Leasing Consultant - Henderson/Las Vegas, NV
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role covers two properties simultaneously: Prelude at the Park in Henderson and Pearl at St. Rose in Las Vegas. That dual-site setup means your day shifts between communities, so time management and strong communication with on-site teams aren't optional. You'll be the first contact for prospective residents, qualifying applicants, preparing leases, and coordinating with maintenance to keep move-ins clean. You'll also handle the administrative side, including rental file accuracy, data entry, and the monthly paperwork that keeps a property audit-ready.

Resident relations are part of the job too. Fielding maintenance concerns, addressing complaints professionally, and staying on top of rent collection all fall within your scope. Occupancy goals are real here, and you'll be expected to use genuine sales technique to hit them, not just show apartments and hope for the best. Henderson and Las Vegas maintain a competitive multifamily market with consistent renter traffic, but concessions and lease incentives can shift quickly depending on what new supply is doing nearby. Knowing how to close in that environment matters.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of property management or leasing experience, ideally on-site at an apartment community
  • Sales ability that's genuine and consultative, not scripted
  • Comfort working across two communities and coordinating with multiple teams
  • Strong attention to detail for lease preparation and file management
  • Professional communication skills with both prospects and current residents
  • Familiarity with property management software for data entry and reporting

The Bigger Picture

MG Properties has operated across the Western U.S. for over three decades, with a portfolio that spans acquisition, development, rehab, and fee management. They're known internally for promoting from within, so a Senior Leasing Consultant role here has a real path toward Assistant Manager or beyond for someone who consistently drives occupancy and handles the administrative side with accuracy. The compensation package includes monthly bonuses, profit sharing, a 401k with employer match, full medical benefits, and a rental discount. The dual-site structure also builds a skill set that transfers well: managing relationships across multiple communities, adapting your leasing approach by asset and resident profile, and staying organized under competing priorities are all things that carry weight in mid-size and large-portfolio management roles down the road.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
Skills This Role Runs On

Student housing operates on a different clock than conventional multifamily. The entire community turns over in a compressed window once a year, delinquency pressure is constant because you're collecting from 18-to-22-year-olds with inconsistent income, and the leasing cycle runs against an academic calendar rather than market demand. The Assistant Community Manager role at Alight Laramie asks you to carry skills across three distinct areas simultaneously: financial controls, turn execution, and customer experience management. If any one of those wobbles, the whole property feels it.

On the financial side, you'll manage accounts receivable, enforce NSF and late fee policies, keep delinquency below 2% at month end, and assist with monthly close. The Entrata proficiency requirement matters here. Knowing your way around the ledger in a PMS isn't optional at this level. You're also posting damage charges from quarterly inspections and handling dispute resolution when residents push back, which they will.

The customer-facing work runs parallel. Weekly market surveys, managing concession budgets, monitoring Yelp and Google reviews, and working with the centralized sales team on occupancy goals. Laramie is a university town tied entirely to UW enrollment cycles, so traffic patterns and lease-up timelines are predictable but unforgiving if you miss the window.

The Turn Is Its Own Season

Annual turnover in student housing is a full operational sprint. This role takes an active hand in it, including physical tasks like moving furniture, assisting facilities with punch lists, and cleaning units. Scion uses Turnable to track the electronic turn board, and you'll be responsible for ensuring progress stays on pace, damage assessments are completed accurately, and final billing goes out correctly. Move-in, room assignments, transfers, and move-outs all process in a tight window. The General Manager leads this effort, and you're the second in command executing it.

It's worth noting that this role also requires you to step into the General Manager position when they're absent. That's a real expectation, not a formality buried in the job description.

What Makes This Role Work at Alight Laramie

Scion is a student housing operator with a clearly defined internal stack: Entrata, ClickUp, Lattice, Greenhouse, Qualtrics. Candidates who've worked across a purpose-built tech stack in student or conventional housing will move faster here than those learning the category from scratch. The one year of property management experience requirement is a floor, not a ceiling. Strong candidates typically bring familiarity with lease audits, resident account management, and at least one major turn season behind them.

The position includes a discretionary annual bonus, 401k matching, paid parental leave, and learning reimbursement. On-call responsibility is part of the schedule. That's standard for any community this size, but worth knowing before you apply.

  • 1+ year in property management or a residential living community
  • Proficiency in a property management system, Entrata preferred
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Comfort with accounts receivable, delinquency tracking, and resident billing
  • Ability to cover General Manager responsibilities as needed
  • Eligible to work in the United States without visa sponsorship

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
Skills at the Center of This Role

The Assistant Community Manager position at Mezza Premier Apartments draws on three skill sets almost simultaneously: leasing, financial administration, and team leadership. On any given day, you might walk a prospect through a tour in the morning, spend the afternoon reviewing ledgers for billing accuracy, and close out the day de-escalating a resident concern before the office closes. That range is real, and it's what makes this role genuinely useful for building a well-rounded property management career.

Hawthorne Residential Partners ranks among the top 50 multifamily management companies nationally and has concentrated its portfolio in the Southeast, where they've developed a recognizable operational culture called "Live It." At Mezza Premier, that translates to an expectation that the assistant manager carries that culture into every resident interaction, not just during events but in routine conversations about renewals, payment plans, and maintenance follow-up.

What You'll Be Doing, Through a Skills Lens

Your leasing skills get used consistently here. You'll conduct tours, respond to incoming leads, guide applications through to completion, and actively support renewal efforts to protect occupancy. Social media content creation for the community is also part of the leasing function, used to drive traffic and highlight resident engagement.

On the financial side, you'll need to be comfortable with rent collection workflows, including payment posting and check scanning, as well as monitoring delinquency and making follow-up calls. Ledger reviews are a regular part of the job, and you'll assist with financial reporting that goes to both the Community Manager and regional leadership. Comfort reading a basic financial report and flagging discrepancies is genuinely useful here, not optional.

Leadership skill comes into play whenever the Community Manager is out. You step into that continuity role, keep the team moving, and maintain the resident experience without a gap. That expectation is baked into the position, which is part of why prior assistant manager experience is preferred alongside at least two years in property management overall.

  • Two years of property management experience preferred
  • Six months in an assistant community manager role preferred
  • High school diploma or GED required
  • Valid driver's license required
  • CALP designation is a plus
  • Weekend availability required (Saturdays, 10 AM to 4 PM); schedule is 40 hours weekly with one weekday off

What Makes This Opportunity Specific to Hawthorne

Hawthorne's Career Path Program is a real differentiator for candidates thinking past this role. The assistant manager position is the standard entry point into the Community Manager track, and the company's Learning and Development team is structured to support that progression internally. If you've been in leasing or admin roles and want a defined path toward running your own community, that structure is already in place here.

Compensation for this role includes hourly pay plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with match, paid time off (including your birthday), paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, telehealth access, and company-paid life insurance.

Jacksonville's multifamily market has seen continued demand pressure in the north corridor, where Mezza Premier sits near the I-295 beltway. Communities in that submarket compete on amenity presentation and resident retention as much as on rent, which makes the leasing and relationship-management skills in this role particularly relevant to day-to-day performance outcomes.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Aubrey, TX
job.description:
Maintenance technician roles at vertically integrated ownership groups tend to run differently than third-party fee management shops. When the same company owns and manages the asset, there's more accountability attached to every work order, every turn, and every curb appeal walk. Berkshire Residential Investments operates that way at Park 3Eighty in Aubrey, TX, and this technician position sits in the middle of that day-to-day physical operation.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

You're covering the full range of hands-on maintenance: plumbing, electrical, appliance repair, carpentry, and general building upkeep. Beyond work orders, you'll help maintain the shop, manage inventory, and keep equipment and key security organized. Curb appeal is treated as a real priority here, not an afterthought. You'll be expected to inspect the property regularly and flag issues before residents do. Supporting the management team on safety compliance and community standards is part of the job, as is delivering consistent, professional service to both current residents and prospects walking the property.

One year of residential maintenance experience is the baseline. You need a working knowledge across the trades, not necessarily a license in every one, but you can't be starting from scratch on appliances or basic plumbing when a resident's unit is down.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

The technicians who do well in roles like this are the ones who treat a make-ready punch list the same way they treat an emergency call. Consistency matters more than occasional heroics. If you're the type who takes pride in a clean shop, tracks your parts inventory without being reminded, and communicates clearly with the office team without drama, you'll fit the culture. Berkshire puts weight on people skills alongside technical ability. Residents notice whether the tech who showed up was professional. That matters here.

The Bigger Picture

Berkshire Residential is a nationally operating ownership and management company, so technicians who grow into lead or make-ready roles have a real path toward maintenance supervisor and eventually service manager positions within the same organization. For someone early in their maintenance career, there's value in working for an owner-operator where your work has direct visibility to asset performance. Benefits include three weeks of vacation, a 25% rent discount, and personal development plans.

Aubrey sits in the north DFW growth corridor, and the submarket has seen significant new construction over the past few years. That means residents in the area generally have options, and the quality of maintenance service plays a real role in retention. It's not background noise. It shows up in renewal rates.

job.title: Apprentice Maintenance Technician - Providence Trail
job.description:
Apartment maintenance has a staffing reality that doesn't get discussed enough: the gap between a raw hire who knows one trade and a technician who can work a full punch list independently is where most operators lose time and money. The apprentice technician role exists to close that gap, deliberately, with structured support. AIR Communities is hiring for exactly that at Providence Trail in Mt. Juliet, Tennessee.

Providence Trail is a suburban garden-style community outside Nashville, and the day-to-day here reflects that profile: service requests, turns, seasonal HVAC work, appliances, and the occasional after-hours call. The compensation runs $25 to $28 per hour depending on your existing skill set, and there's a monthly customer service bonus up to $250 for techs who consistently deliver good resident experiences. The 50% rent discount at any AIR community is a real benefit worth calculating if you're in the market.

What the Work Looks Like

Your day splits between two modes. Turns involve following AIR's make-ready process to get vacated units back to move-in condition, working through the standard punch list from paint touch-ups to fixture checks. Service requests are more variable: plumbing, basic electrical, HVAC, appliances, anything that comes in through the work order queue. AIR uses technology to prioritize and route work, so you're not chasing paper or guessing what's urgent. The shop is stocked and organized, which matters more than people expect. A disorganized supply room is a quiet productivity killer.

You'll also have the option to assist with vendor oversight and move-in/move-out inspections as you develop. Responsibilities scale with your skills and community needs, which is honest language for: you'll be given more as you demonstrate you can handle it.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of maintenance experience, ideally in a facilities or residential building setting
  • Proficiency in at least two trades: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliance repair, or carpentry
  • Ability to work flexible hours including evenings, weekends, and on-call rotations (expect roughly one week per month on call)
  • Reliable transportation for after-hours emergency response
  • Physical comfort with heavy lifting and working in mechanical spaces

The technicians who advance quickly in roles like this tend to share one trait: they diagnose before they replace. Residents notice when a problem comes back, and so does your service satisfaction score. First-call resolution is the real metric here, even if nobody puts it on the job posting.

AIR's Ascend program is worth mentioning as a genuine career consideration. It's a development track designed around your specific path, and AIR has a stated preference for internal promotion. HVAC certification reimbursement and tuition assistance are included in the benefits package, which means the skills you build here can come with credentials attached. For someone at the apprentice level looking to land at lead tech or beyond, that matters.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
Bozzuto operates across development, construction, and third-party management, which means the people running their communities carry a broader operational awareness than you'd find at a purely fee-management shop. The Assistant Property Manager role in Seattle's Fremont/Wallingford corridor sits inside that environment. You're working with a recognized brand, which raises the bar on resident experience and brand consistency, and you're being positioned to grow.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Involves

This role splits its energy between two areas that don't always get equal attention in APM positions: financial accountability and people leadership. On the financial side, you're watching delinquency closely, driving rent collection, and building familiarity with P&L and budget variances. That exposure compounds fast. APMs who spend two or three years genuinely owning those numbers become very competitive candidates for Property Manager roles.

On the people side, you're coaching leasing staff, covering for the Property Manager when needed, and serving as the on-site culture carrier. Bozzuto's model emphasizes service consistency, so your ability to set a standard through your own behavior matters as much as your ability to give feedback. Weekend availability is part of this role, one to two weekends per month, with weekday days off in exchange.

The leasing component is real. You'll conduct personalized tours and contribute directly to occupancy performance. Seattle's rental market rewards consultative leasing, not scripted pitches, and Bozzuto's expectation is that you bring genuine local knowledge into those conversations.

What Bozzuto Is Looking For

  • A four-year degree or equivalent experience with at least two years in property management, hospitality, or retail
  • Hands-on exposure to budgets, P&L, and revenue tracking
  • Comfort with Yardi or comparable property management software
  • Active use of social media platforms, particularly Instagram and Facebook, for community marketing
  • Strong written and verbal communication, and the sales instincts to back it up

Where This Role Can Take You

The skills that develop in a well-run APM role transfer directly into property management and regional operations. If you're tracking delinquency and contributing to NOI conversations now, you'll be ready to own a T-12 and run a budget review inside a few years. Bozzuto offers tuition reimbursement and active career development programs, which signals they're structured to promote from within. The salary range for this position is $30 to $34 per hour, with bonus eligibility on top of that, plus full benefits including medical, dental, vision, 20 days of PTO, and 401k with company match.

If you've been in a leasing role and you're ready to take on more financial responsibility, or if you've been managing a smaller community and want the operational rigor of a larger platform, this is a natural next step.

job.title: Business Manager - Chevy Chase
job.description:
Full-site accountability in multifamily property management is one of the most complete skill sets this industry produces. A Business Manager touches every operational layer at once: financial performance, team development, resident experience, and physical asset condition. That breadth is both the challenge and the value of the role.

At Olympus Property's Chevy Chase community in Austin, TX, the Business Manager carries full operational responsibility for the property. This means owning the NOI story, not just tracking it. You'll build annual budget forecasts, analyze monthly performance against projections, and present strategies to Regional Leadership when the numbers need attention. Rents, occupancy, delinquency, expenditures, and vendor contract negotiations all fall within your scope. The financial side of this role requires someone who already reads a T-12 with confidence and understands how individual decisions ripple into asset performance over time.

What This Role Requires You to Bring

Olympus expects a minimum of two years of multifamily property management experience at the manager level. That baseline matters because this role doesn't have room for on-the-job orientation in fundamentals. You'll need to arrive knowing how to run a make-ready program, supervise maintenance staff, manage vendor bids, and keep units in market-ready condition without waiting for direction. RealPage, Knock, and Onesite experience is strongly preferred. The schedule is Monday through Friday with hours ranging between 8 AM and 6 PM, and flexibility for after-hours resident events or emergencies is part of the expectation.

  • Minimum 2 years of direct property manager experience in multifamily
  • Demonstrated ability to manage onsite teams across both office and maintenance functions
  • Experience with budget development, financial reporting, and variance analysis
  • RealPage/Onesite/Knock proficiency preferred
  • Comfort with leasing, renewals, and retention program oversight to protect occupancy
  • Vendor management experience, including bidding and contract negotiation

What This Role Builds

Strong Business Managers who spend two or three years in this seat often move into Regional Manager roles, and for good reason. Managing a full asset teaches you to think in terms of portfolio strategy, not just daily operations. You'll sharpen your ability to read the relationship between traffic, concessions, and occupancy trends, which is exactly the lens a regional needs. Olympus supports that progression directly through their Budget Camp and Leadership Conference programs, along with formal career pathing.

The candidates who perform best here tend to be the ones who treat inspection findings and punch lists with the same seriousness as a leasing call. Physical asset condition and financial performance aren't separate concerns. They compound each other, and the managers who recognize that early tend to outperform peers who treat maintenance oversight as a secondary responsibility. Compensation ranges from $75,000 to $85,000 annually, with monthly commissions and quarterly and annual bonus eligibility layered on top. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, and an apartment rental allowance.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Roofstock operates in the single-family rental space, and that context shapes this role in a meaningful way. Unlike a traditional multifamily technician who works one property with a maintenance supervisor down the hall, this position puts you across multiple homes throughout Columbia, managing your own schedule, your own truck, and your own judgment. The Columbia market has seen steady SFR (single-family rental) growth over the past several years, with a mix of older stock and newer acquisitions spread across suburban corridors. That variety means the work is rarely repetitive.

The pay range runs $25 to $30 per hour depending on experience and licensure, and HVAC Type II certification is required from day one. Universal certification is preferred and worth having if you want to handle a broader scope of refrigerant work without limitations.
