That means greeting prospects and residents, responding to inquiries across every channel with accuracy and speed, and knowing the current availability and pricing well enough to answer any question a prospective renter might ask. You'll also inspect vacant apartments and the tour path daily to confirm everything is show-ready, which requires a trained eye for what "ready" actually means: clean, functional, and presentable against a defined standard.

Beyond direct leasing activity, the role pulls in some community operations work. That includes organizing the package room, supporting community events, assisting with social media marketing, and keeping vendor and community communications on track. These aren't afterthoughts. They're part of what keeps occupancy stable and resident satisfaction consistent.

The schedule is full-time and includes evenings and weekends, which is standard for leasing-facing roles. If you've worked retail, hospitality, or any consumer-facing environment on a rotating schedule, that experience translates directly here.

Skills You Bring vs. Skills You Build

This role requires strong verbal and written communication, a genuine comfort with people, and an organized approach to daily tasks. You need to already know how to manage multiple priorities without letting the floor experience suffer. Those aren't trainable in the first 90 days.

What the role builds is different. You'll develop a practical understanding of leasing fundamentals: traffic management, pricing conversations, objection handling, and how a well-run leasing office moves prospects through to move-in. Cottonwood also positions this as an entry point into property management, so if your goal is an assistant manager or eventually a property manager track, this is a legitimate starting point rather than a ceiling.

One Thing Worth Knowing About This Operator

Cottonwood Residential was an early adopter of Self-Guided Tours, which means the leasing process here is more tech-integrated than at many conventional operators. Prospects may tour without a leasing agent present, which shifts some of the relationship-building to before and after the tour rather than during it. Strong follow-up and responsive communication become even more important in that model. If you're comfortable with digital tools and understand that the leasing conversation doesn't always happen in person, you'll fit the workflow well.

  • Full-time position with weekend and evening availability required
  • Quarterly bonus structure in addition to base pay
  • Health, vision, dental, life, and disability benefits starting within 30 days
  • 401k and HSA with company match
  • Three weeks of paid time off in the first year, plus 10.5 paid holidays
  • Defined path toward future management roles

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
The assistant community manager role exists at the intersection of operations and resident experience. You're the person who keeps things moving when the community manager is pulled elsewhere, and the one who spots financial or leasing problems before they compound. At a multifamily property in Davenport, Waypoint Management Services is filling that seat now.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

You'll work alongside the community manager on daily operations, but you'll own a real slice of the workload independently. That means tracking delinquency, supporting the eviction process when it gets there, and making sure rent collection doesn't slip. You'll monitor the make-ready schedule, keep the rent roll accurate, and flag renewal risk early enough to act on it.

On the leasing side, you'll support the leasing team's performance and training, help execute marketing strategies, and stay current on what competitors are doing with pricing and concessions. When occupancy trends shift, you're expected to bring data and a recommendation, not just a problem.

Weekend availability is required. This is a community-facing role, and the schedule reflects that.

What You'll Bring

  • At least two years in leasing, sales, or a hospitality role with transferable skills
  • Solid financial literacy: you're comfortable reading reports, tracking variances, and explaining what you see
  • Strong organizational habits and attention to detail in recordkeeping
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office; Yardi experience is a real advantage here
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills
  • Valid driver's license
  • High school diploma or equivalent

The candidates who stand out at this level already understand that leasing numbers and financial performance are connected. If you've worked renewals strategy or helped a team hit occupancy goals during a slow season, that experience carries weight in this interview.

Waypoint offers a compensation package that includes monthly leasing and renewal bonuses, an employee housing discount, medical, dental, and vision coverage starting on day one, 120 hours of PTO in year one, a 401k with company match, and commuter and referral benefits.

job.title: Business Manager - Olympus Carrington
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

The Business Manager role at Olympus Carrington in Pooler, GA puts you in the seat that most property management careers build toward. You're running the full operation: financial performance, team development, physical asset condition, and resident experience. That means owning occupancy and delinquency metrics, building and tracking budgets, and working directly with Regional Leadership on monthly performance strategy. You'll complete annual asset business plans, review T-12 financials, and translate numbers into action steps your team can execute on the ground.

On any given week, you're shifting between leasing strategy, vendor contract negotiations, make-ready oversight, and staff coaching. Keeping units in market-ready condition, running regular property inspections, and ensuring compliance aren't tasks you delegate and forget. You're the one who sets the standard and holds it. Resident events and the occasional after-hours emergency come with the territory, so schedule flexibility matters here.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of direct multifamily Property Manager experience. Luxury Class A experience is a genuine advantage for this property.
  • Comfort with financial reporting: understanding NOI, managing to a budget, and discussing variance with Regional leadership without needing the numbers explained to you.
  • Hands-on experience with RealPage, Knock, or OneSite. Olympus specifically calls these out, which signals they're woven into daily operations, not occasional tools.
  • A track record of training and developing office and maintenance staff, not just supervising them.
  • The ability to manage vendor relationships from bid through project completion.

Where This Role Fits in a Career Arc

Business Manager at a Class A community is one of the cleaner stepping stones in multifamily. The financial discipline you build here, specifically budget forecasting, variance analysis, and asset planning, transfers directly to Regional Manager roles. Olympus offers formal career pathing, Budget Camp, and leadership conferences, which aren't just perks. They reflect a structure where site-level managers are being prepared for the next level, not just retained. If you're already performing as a property manager and want a defined path toward regional leadership, the skills you compound in this seat are the right ones.

Compensation runs $80,000 to $82,000 annually, with monthly commissions and quarterly and annual bonus eligibility on top of base. The full benefits package includes medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, and an apartment rental allowance, among others.

Olympus Property has earned NAA's Top Employer designation three consecutive years (2023, 2024, 2025). For a candidate who wants to grow within a company rather than job-hop for promotions, that kind of sustained recognition is worth weighing seriously.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
Georgetown, TX has grown fast enough that lease-up and stabilized communities alike are competing hard for qualified renters. Bexley Wolf Ranch sits inside that market, and Weinstein Properties needs someone on-site who can handle both the leasing floor and the operational side of daily community management. That's the Assistant Property Manager role in a nutshell.

Weinstein is a family-owned operator with 70-plus years and more than 60 communities across the Southeast and Texas. That tenure shows up in how they run properties: hands-on, training-focused, and with real promotion paths for people who perform. A lot of operators say that. Weinstein has the internal track record to back it up.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

The role covers a wide band of on-site operations. You'll work internet leads and phone inquiries, schedule tours, process applications, and take leases from approval through signing. That's the leasing half. The other half is resident services: renewals, notices to vacate, pet addenda, transfers, account questions, and move-out processing including security deposit dispositions. You'll post rent, follow up on balances owed, and coordinate with maintenance on make-readies and work orders. Punch list walks after turns are part of the job. So is planning and hosting resident events, which occasionally means evenings or rotating Saturdays. This is an on-your-feet role. The desk is where you start and end tasks, not where you spend the day.

Starting pay is $23 per hour with increases based on experience, quarterly bonuses, a rent discount, 401k with company match, and standard health benefits. Birthday time off is a small thing, but it's the kind of detail that signals a culture paying attention.

Who Fits This Role Well

Weinstein will train someone who comes from hospitality, retail management, or sales rather than property management directly. The non-negotiables are communication skills, composure under pressure, and the ability to manage shifting priorities without losing track of the details. Delinquency follow-up, lease paperwork accuracy, and security deposit dispositions all punish people who get sloppy when things get busy.

  • Leasing, hospitality, or customer service background with some supervisory exposure
  • Comfortable having direct conversations with residents about balances, lease terms, or disputes
  • Organized enough to manage active leads, renewals, and work order follow-up simultaneously
  • Available for rotating Saturdays and occasional evenings for resident programming
  • Property management software experience is a plus, not a requirement

The career path here is worth noting. Assistant Property Manager is typically where property management careers either take hold or stall. The people who grow out of this role and into property manager or multi-site positions are the ones who treat the full job seriously, not just the leasing traffic. Renewals, delinquency, turn coordination, resident retention: those skills travel with you regardless of what platform or ownership group you end up working for later.

Weinstein Properties is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

job.title: Leasing Consultant (The Dean)
job.description:
A prospect walks in Saturday afternoon without an appointment, having toured three other communities that morning. They're tired, a little skeptical, and they want straight answers. How you handle the next twenty minutes determines whether The Dean gains a signed lease or loses traffic to a competitor down the street.

Prometheus Real Estate Group calls this role a Neighbor Ambassador, and the distinction matters operationally. At The Dean in Mountain View, you're carrying three functions simultaneously: customer experience, active sales, and leasing administration. On any given shift, you might guide a future resident through the application process, pull a market survey to benchmark rents against nearby communities, and then post updated availability before the day ends. Weekends are the high-traffic window when prospects are actively shopping, so your schedule is built around Saturday and Sunday availability, with weekday time off in return.

Day-to-Day Responsibilities

  • Guiding prospects through the full leasing process, from initial inquiry to signed rental agreement
  • Delivering a consistent, high-quality leasing experience that reflects the property's brand and drives occupancy
  • Conducting market surveys and maintaining accurate knowledge of competitive pricing and concessions in the Mountain View submarket
  • Preparing leasing documents, reports, and apartment advertising with attention to detail and accuracy
  • Supporting resident satisfaction so that current neighbors feel genuinely cared for, which directly affects renewal rates and delinquency trends
  • Problem-solving on the fly, often without a supervisor in the room

What Prometheus Is Looking For

Prometheus hires across industries, so prior property management experience isn't required. What does matter is a real comfort with sales conversations, a service orientation that reads as genuine rather than scripted, and the ability to stay organized when the leasing office is busy. Strong candidates here will close traffic efficiently without letting administrative tasks pile up behind them. The leasing-to-close ratio matters, and top performers know their numbers.

Pay runs $25.00 to $26.25 per hour, plus a $200 incentive per signed lease, a discretionary semi-annual bonus, and a weekend shift premium. Prometheus also offers company-paid medical, vision, and dental coverage including eligible dependents, a 401(k) with employer matching, tenure-based housing discounts, and tuition reimbursement. Paid volunteer time and a birthday holiday round out a benefits package that's more comprehensive than most in this wage band.

Mountain View's rental market is competitive and renter-savvy. Prospects here often arrive having already reviewed floor plans and pricing online. The consultants who perform best in this environment don't rely on a pitch. They listen, qualify quickly, and match the right unit to the right person without overselling. That skill, traffic conversion under informed, comparison-shopping conditions, transfers directly to senior leasing roles, assistant manager positions, and eventually property management if that's the direction you want to go.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
It's 9:15 on a Tuesday morning. A vendor is late for a scheduled unit inspection, two lease renewals need signatures before end of week, and a resident left a two-star review overnight. You review the delinquency report, then walk the grounds before your team huddle at 10. That's the pace of this role at Madison Woods, a Hawthorne Residential Partners community in Greensboro, NC.

What the Role Covers

As Community Manager, you own the full operation. Financially, that means managing the budget, tracking collections, overseeing deposit accounting, and keeping delinquency in check. You'll work inside Yardi and Knock daily, maintain accurate records, and report up to ownership and regional leadership. On the property side, you're conducting inspections, keeping curb appeal sharp, and coordinating with maintenance on work orders and preventative care. Vendor oversight is yours too, including quality, timing, and safety compliance.

Leasing and occupancy are central to the position. You'll support tours, guide prospects through the process, and push for strong renewal conversions. Pricing strategy and occupancy goals land on your desk, not just your leasing team's. You'll also manage the community's social media presence and keep common areas, amenities, and the leasing office presented well.

The people side is equally demanding. You hire, train, and coach both office and maintenance staff. Weekly team meetings, performance accountability, and individual development are part of your regular week. Resident escalations go through you, and so does the reputation management that follows a negative online review.

Qualifications Worth Knowing

  • At least two years of property management experience, covering both leasing and assistant manager roles
  • Six months of direct community manager experience in multifamily is strongly preferred
  • Familiarity with Yardi, Knock, and Microsoft Office is preferred
  • Valid driver's license required
  • CAM, CAPS, a real estate license, or a property management license is a plus
  • High school diploma or GED required

The office runs Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, and Saturdays from 10 AM to 4 PM. One weekday off maintains a 40-hour schedule. Some evenings and weekends may be needed for resident events or community needs.

Compensation includes a base salary plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits cover medical, dental, vision, 401k with match, paid time off including your birthday, paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, company-paid life insurance, and 24/7 telehealth access.

Candidates who stand out at this level already know how to read a financial report and act on it, not just pass it along. The ability to hold a team accountable while keeping morale intact is what separates average managers from ones who consistently hit occupancy goals and retain good staff. If your background includes managing through a lease-up or stabilizing a community with soft occupancy, that experience will translate directly here.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
Hillpointe builds and manages market-rate workforce housing across the Sun Belt, and this Community Manager role sits at the center of daily operations at one of their Phoenix properties. You're accountable for occupancy, financials, resident experience, and asset condition. All of it reports up to a Regional Manager, but the day-to-day runs through you.

What the Job Covers

You'll manage the full operational picture: budget oversight, accounts payable, vendor coordination, lease administration, and regular property walks to keep the asset in good condition. Units need to be make-ready to like-new standards before every move-in, and amenities get held to that same bar on an ongoing basis. You'll serve as the connection point between on-site needs and the facilities maintenance team, so clear communication and follow-through matter constantly.

On the revenue side, you're expected to support budgeted occupancy and rent targets, explore additional revenue opportunities as they come up, and report accurately using Entrata (preferred) and standard spreadsheet tools. Financial recordkeeping, including budget tracking and fiscal reporting, is a regular part of the role.

  • Drive and maintain budgeted occupancy in coordination with your Regional Manager
  • Oversee AP submission and vendor invoice processing
  • Conduct routine property walks and maintain curb appeal and interior standards
  • Coordinate between the facilities/maintenance team and property-level needs
  • Manage lease administration and ensure regulatory compliance
  • Build a community culture that keeps residents engaged and renewing

What You Bring

Property management experience is preferred. You need a high school diploma (or equivalent), a valid driver's license, and comfort working a flexible schedule with phone and email availability outside standard hours. The role involves routine local travel for bank deposits and training as needed, along with physical access to all parts of the property and the ability to handle up to 20 pounds independently.

Strong written and verbal communication skills are non-negotiable. You'll regularly work through legal documents, explain community features to prospective residents, and field operational questions from current ones. Proficiency with property management software, particularly Entrata, and solid math skills for financial reporting round out the core requirements.

A Note on Fit

Hillpointe controls the full development cycle in-house, from land acquisition through construction and asset management. That means the properties are relatively new and the standards for presentation reflect that. Community Managers who thrive here tend to be detail-oriented on asset condition while also being comfortable working across teams. If you've managed a lease-up or a newer community where the expectation was keeping everything looking like day one, that experience translates directly to what this role requires.

job.title: Birch Plaza Leasing Manager
job.description:
Leasing is a skill set that shows up in every corner of property management, and this role puts it front and center. At Birch Plaza, the Leasing Manager carries the occupancy numbers, owns the resident communication, and steps into community manager responsibilities when operations call for it. If you're comfortable on the phones, confident in a tour, and capable of tracking ledger balances without losing the thread, this position puts all of that to work daily.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

A typical day runs from prospect calls and scheduled tours in the morning to follow-up emails, lease paperwork, and Entrata workflow tasks in the afternoon. You'll run renewal campaigns alongside new lease efforts, which means balancing traffic from new prospects while keeping current residents happy enough to re-sign. Resident ledger accuracy is part of the job too. Catching a billing error before it becomes a collections issue is real, unglamorous work that matters.

The title says Leasing Manager, but the scope includes budget awareness, delinquency follow-up, and staff coordination. You're not just closing leases. You're helping hold the operation together.

Student and conventional housing both live under Redstone's portfolio, and Birch Plaza sits within that system. That means company-standard tools, defined processes, and SEO and social marketing expectations as part of your leasing toolkit. You'll use what's given to you, and you'll be expected to use it well.

Skills This Role Relies On

  • Oral and written communication: you'll handle calls, emails, and in-person tours in the same shift
  • Sales and follow-through: traffic means nothing if you can't convert and retain
  • Organization and time management: competing priorities are constant, not occasional
  • Computer proficiency: Microsoft Office, Outlook, SharePoint, and Entrata are daily tools
  • Composure: some days involve difficult residents, and some conversations require patience you have to choose deliberately

Who Succeeds Here

Redstone is a large third-party operator managing over 38,000 beds across 20 states, which means there's real infrastructure behind this role. Systems exist. Support exists. What the company looks for in a leasing hire is someone who can run within that structure and still show initiative, someone who hits leasing goals through consistent follow-up rather than waiting for traffic to walk in.

The strongest candidates in leasing roles like this one tend to be honest self-starters who communicate proactively with teammates rather than waiting to be asked. Renewal rates and occupancy don't improve by accident. They improve because someone keeps showing up and doing the follow-through work even when the energy is low.

This role pays $14 per hour and carries a full benefits package including health, vision, and dental coverage, a 401(k) with up to 6% matching, PTO, paid holidays, and parental leave. For someone early in their property management career, the exposure to both leasing operations and community manager responsibilities makes the position a reasonable foundation for a future move into full community management.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Maintenance technicians at affordable housing communities carry a different kind of weight than their counterparts at Class A lease-ups. Residents depend on their homes in a deeper way, and the person who shows up to fix a leaking pipe or a faulty breaker isn't just a service vendor. They're part of why the community functions. Fairstead understands that, and it shapes how they operate their portfolio of more than 30,000 apartments across 28 states.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

This is a full-scope technician role at a Fairstead property in Mobile, Alabama. Your day will move between scheduled work and the unexpected. Preventative maintenance inspections, make-ready prep on vacated units, electrical checks, safety system walkthroughs, and inventory management fill the structured parts of your week. The less predictable parts come from residents: an HVAC issue in August heat, a tripped breaker, a safety concern that can't wait. You'll be part of the on-call rotation, which means some calls come after hours. That's the honest reality of this work, and it's worth knowing upfront.

Fairstead runs an integrated platform where development, construction, and property management sit under one roof. That structure matters for technicians because decisions move faster and the maintenance team isn't an afterthought. You're working within a system that treats physical asset quality as a core part of the mission, not a cost center to minimize.

What You Bring

  • Prior experience as a maintenance or service technician in a residential or similar setting
  • Working knowledge of electrical systems, enough to diagnose problems and handle minor repairs safely
  • General mechanical skills covering plumbing, appliances, fixtures, and building systems
  • HVAC certification, CMRP, or equivalent credential (preferred but not a hard stop)
  • Ability to lift up to 70 pounds unassisted and stay on your feet for extended shifts
  • Clear communication, both with residents who may be frustrated and with a team that depends on accurate handoffs

Attention to detail separates solid technicians from great ones in affordable housing specifically. A punch list item skipped during a make-ready creates problems for a new resident on day one. A missed safety check creates liability. The candidates who do well here are methodical, not just skilled.

The Team and the Bigger Picture

Fairstead describes itself as purpose-driven, and the affordable housing space does attract people who care about more than square footage and cap rates. That doesn't mean the work is easy or the pace is slow. It means the stakes feel real. Residents in these communities aren't choosing to live elsewhere for lifestyle reasons. Keeping their homes functional and safe is straightforward mission-critical work.

Benefits include employer-contributed medical through Meritain Health, employer-paid vision and life insurance, a 401(k) with company matching (100% on the first 3%, 50% on the next 2%), 15 days of PTO, 7 sick days, and 12 or more paid holidays. There's also a flexible spending account, disability coverage, pet insurance, and employee discount programs.

For a technician who wants room to grow, Fairstead's scale means there's a real path toward senior technician, maintenance supervisor, or facilities management roles across a large multi-state portfolio. The company's tech-forward approach also means exposure to digital work order systems and data-driven operations that build skills transferable well beyond any single property.

job.title: Groundskeeper
job.description:
Groundskeeping at a luxury apartment community requires a specific combination of physical consistency and observational sharpness. You're not just picking up litter and trimming shrubs. You're the first person most residents and prospects see when they pull into the property, and the condition of the grounds communicates something immediate about how the community is managed. Griffis Residential operates a portfolio of upscale apartment homes, and this role reflects that standard.

Skills This Role Requires on Day One

Attention to detail is the primary skill this role draws on constantly. Walking a property and seeing what needs attention before a resident notices it is a trained habit, and Griffis expects that habit to be already developing when you arrive. At minimum, one year of experience in multi-family housing, hospitality, or a comparable environment gives you the foundation. Beyond the eye for detail, you'll need solid communication skills, the ability to follow standardized procedures across a range of tasks, and a genuine comfort with physical, outdoor work across all seasons. Denver winters mean snow removal and ice treatment are real parts of the job, not occasional footnotes.

The scope of daily work includes:

  • Full community inspections for cleanliness, litter, and hazards (pet waste, cigarette butts, dumpster areas)
  • Light landscaping: sprinkler adjustments, trimming trees and shrubs, sod replacement, general plant care
  • Parking lots, curbs, and walkways kept clean and clear
  • Pool and spa upkeep including chemical balancing and documentation
  • Snow and ice removal with ice melt application as conditions require
  • Identifying areas where maintenance processes could improve and communicating those observations to the team

Skills This Role Builds

Groundskeeping at a professional property management company is a real entry point into multi-family operations. The CPO (Certified Pool Operator) license is preferred at hire but required within your first six months. Griffis will expect you to obtain it, and that credential carries genuine weight if you move toward a maintenance technician or lead maintenance role later. Beyond the CPO, you'll develop a working knowledge of how a luxury community presents itself, how curb appeal connects to occupancy and resident retention, and how your daily work contributes to a property's NOI by protecting asset condition and supporting resident loyalty.

Working inside Griffis's resident loyalty programs also builds customer service habits that transfer well across the industry. Groundskeepers who understand the connection between curb appeal, first impressions, and lease renewals tend to advance more quickly than those who treat the role as purely physical work.

What Griffis Offers

The compensation range for this position runs from $20.75 to $23.00 per hour. The benefits package is genuinely broad: medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with up to 4% company match, a 50% rental discount, three weeks of PTO accruing immediately, 11 paid holidays, up to $2,000 in annual on-site bonuses tied to reputation and occupancy, tuition reimbursement up to $5,250 per year, and paid parental leave. For a grounds-level role, the total compensation picture here compares favorably to hospitality environments where similar physical demands often come with less schedule stability and fewer structured benefits.

Spanish bilingual skills are a plus given Denver's resident population, and Griffis emphasizes a commitment to inclusive team culture. If you take pride in property presentation and want to grow within a structured, professionally managed company, this role is a solid place to start building that career.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - EPA Certified
job.description:
Weinstein Properties is offering a $1,500 sign-on bonus for an EPA-certified Maintenance Technician at 3Sixty Flats in Grand Prairie, TX. The pay range runs $24 to $27 per hour, and the on-call structure is worth understanding before you apply: $150 per week guaranteed whether calls come in or not, plus an additional $150 for holiday coverage. That's real money built into the compensation model, not just a vague promise of overtime.

The schedule is Monday through Friday, 8:00am to 5:00pm, with rotating emergency on-call shared across the team. Day-to-day work covers the full range of residential maintenance: HVAC troubleshooting and repair (EPA Type II or Universal required), plumbing, electrical, appliances, carpentry, and support with turns and make-readies. You'll also help keep the community grounds, amenities, and pool areas in shape. Weinstein owns and manages its properties in-house, which matters practically. There's no third-party management layer, so decisions move faster and maintenance standards stay consistent across the portfolio.

Three years of apartment or residential maintenance experience is the baseline here. This role calls for someone who can independently diagnose a complex issue and resolve it without needing a supervisor to walk through each step. The customer service dimension is real too. Residents are in their homes, and how a technician communicates and follows through shapes renewal decisions as much as leasing does.

What the role is looking for

  • EPA Certification, Type II or Universal
  • At least 3 years of hands-on apartment or residential maintenance experience
  • Proven ability to troubleshoot and repair HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliances
  • Comfort with work order systems and mobile tools
  • Ability to lift up to 75 lbs and work outdoors year-round
  • Valid transportation and clean background check

From a career development standpoint, technicians who build this kind of multi-trade competency at a stable, owner-operated property tend to have a clear path forward. Lead Technician and Maintenance Supervisor roles at Weinstein or elsewhere become realistic targets within a few years, particularly for those who develop strong vendor coordination skills and start thinking about the cost side of maintenance decisions. Capex planning, unit turn efficiency, and reducing delinquency-driven damage claims are all things that property managers lean on their maintenance leads to help with. The skills you build in a role like this compound directly into leadership eligibility.

Benefits include rent discount, PTO, paid holidays, birthday time off, medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with company match, an employee assistance program, and a referral bonus program. Quarterly performance bonuses run up to $980 based on property and team metrics. Sign-on bonus specifics are discussed during the interview process.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor - Village at Desert Lakes
job.description:
Maintenance Supervisor roles at established Western portfolio operators tend to carry real weight. You're not just keeping lights on and fixing disposals. You're running a small department, keeping the property in condition that supports occupancy and NOI, and serving as the person residents actually call when something goes wrong at 11 PM.

What You'll Be Responsible For

At Village at Desert Lakes, you'll own the full maintenance operation: diagnosing and completing repairs across all trades, delegating work orders to your team, and making sure resident service requests move through the system efficiently. That last part matters more than people think. A slow make-ready or a stalled punch list can drag turn times, and in Las Vegas, where rental traffic is competitive, a vacant unit sitting past its ready date has a real cost. You'll also conduct regular safety meetings, keep preventive maintenance records clean, and coordinate scheduling for your crew alongside the community manager.

MG Properties has been acquiring, developing, and managing multifamily communities across the Western U.S. for more than 30 years. At this scale, they have systems in place, but they also expect their site-level supervisors to actually run the operation, not just follow a checklist.

What They're Looking For

  • At least two years of experience in a Maintenance Supervisor role
  • Hands-on background managing maintenance at a community of 150 units or more
  • Competency across all trades (HVAC, plumbing, electrical, appliance repair)
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • Strong customer service orientation and the ability to work within a team structure

All offers are contingent on a background check and drug screen. MG Properties participates in E-Verify and is an at-will employer. Audio recordings may occur during work duties as a condition of employment.

Compensation and Team Culture

The package includes monthly bonuses, company profit sharing, a 401(k) with employer match, and a standard suite of medical, dental, and vision coverage. PTO accrual, paid holidays, paid personal days, paid sick time, and a rental discount round out the benefits. For a W-2 maintenance role in multifamily, that's a solid structure.

One thing worth noting for candidates coming from independent or smaller operators: a company with 30-plus years in the business has institutionalized a lot of its processes. That can feel like more structure than you're used to, but it also means you're not building the wheel from scratch. The tools, vendor relationships, and training frameworks tend to already exist. Your job is to run the operation well within them.

job.title: Regional Property Manager
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This Regional Property Manager role sits at the intersection of student housing operations, financial oversight, and sales strategy across a portfolio of properties in the San Antonio and Austin markets. You're the connective tissue between corporate directives and on-site execution. That means regular property visits to assess curb appeal, maintenance operations, capital improvements, and brand consistency, plus the financial discipline to run monthly variance calls, review delinquency trends, and guide General Managers through budget season. When occupancy softens or closing ratios slip, you're the one building the strategy to correct it, not just flagging the problem.

The turn process in student housing is unlike anything in conventional multifamily. You're coordinating mass move-outs and move-ins within a compressed window, often measured in days rather than weeks. Strong candidates have managed this at scale before and understand what it takes to keep a team focused when the calendar is unforgiving.

On the revenue side, you'll work alongside a Regional Revenue Manager on weekly leasing strategy calls, analyzing traffic, closing ratios, and unit mix configurations to hit targeted occupancy and revenue goals for each sales year. You'll also evaluate renewal incentives, new resident concessions, and premium structures as part of the annual revenue plan. The sales component here is more analytical than most regional roles in conventional PM.

What You Bring

  • Demonstrated experience managing a portfolio of properties at the regional level, ideally in student housing or lease-up environments with compressed leasing cycles
  • Fluency in financial reporting: variance analysis, capex oversight, delinquency management, and budget development alongside General Managers
  • Experience coaching and developing on-site teams, including holding managers accountable to leasing goals and operational standards
  • Comfort working with leasing intelligence platforms and market data to shape strategy, not just review it
  • Ability to be physically present at properties in the San Antonio and Austin area on a regular basis, with availability for emergency coverage when site leadership gaps arise
  • Eligibility to work in the United States without visa sponsorship

Where This Role Leads

Regional Manager is one of the most skill-compounding roles in property management. You're developing fluency in asset-level finance, revenue management, people operations, and vendor negotiation simultaneously. Managers who perform well in this seat typically move toward Regional Vice President roles or into director-level positions overseeing larger portfolios or specific operational verticals. In student housing specifically, the analytical rigor around leasing cycles, rate setting, and revenue planning translates well to conventional multifamily, build-to-rent portfolios, and even asset management functions. The skill set you build here travels.

Scion operates as one of the larger student housing platforms in North America, which means you're working within a system that has actual infrastructure: dedicated revenue management support, training and talent development resources, and capital teams you can consult on major expenditures. For a regional manager, that kind of institutional support makes a meaningful difference in what you can actually deliver for your communities.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
Maintenance supervision at the apartment community level is where physical plant knowledge meets people management, and the gap between a strong technician and a strong supervisor is wider than most expect. This role at Hawthorne at the Hollow in Soddy-Daisy, TN asks you to bring both, and to build the people around you as deliberately as you maintain the property itself.

Hawthorne Residential Partners runs this position with a clear scope: you own the condition of the asset, the readiness of the team, and the quality of every unit turn. That's a meaningful combination of responsibilities, and the role is structured to give you real authority over each one.

What This Role Actually Requires

You'll need at least three years of apartment maintenance or skilled trade experience covering HVAC, plumbing, or electrical work. EPA certification is required; CPO certification is strongly preferred and may be mandatory depending on state regulations. A valid driver's license is expected. Prior supervisory or lead technician experience isn't a soft preference here. You'll be managing schedules, delegating work orders, tracking inventory, and overseeing the make-ready cycle from punch list to move-in inspection on day one.

The day-to-day demands include:

  • Leading and scheduling the maintenance team, with direct accountability for performance and follow-through
  • Managing the quarterly preventative maintenance program across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and building systems
  • Overseeing unit turns and personally inspecting vacants before move-in to confirm cleanliness and functionality
  • Supervising vendor partners on make-ready work and capital improvement projects, including bid management and execution oversight
  • Maintaining grounds, common areas, and amenities to support curb appeal and community presentation
  • Participating in the on-call emergency rotation and responding to after-hours service needs as scheduled
  • Keeping all work aligned with OSHA safety standards and company policy

What This Role Builds

Strong maintenance supervisors develop a specific kind of operational fluency that transfers well across property types and ownership structures. Managing a maintenance budget, tracking inventory, and overseeing capex projects gives you exposure to the financial side of asset management that pure technician roles rarely provide. If you have the technical foundation but limited supervisory experience, this role accelerates that development through daily practice rather than classroom instruction.

Vendor relationship management is another skill this position develops at scale. Coordinating timelines, holding vendors accountable to scope and quality, and keeping turns on schedule requires negotiation and communication skills that carry weight in senior maintenance and facilities management roles down the line.

The standard schedule runs Monday through Friday, 8 AM to 5 PM, with on-call rotation for emergencies. Compensation includes an hourly base plus a monthly renewal bonus, quarterly performance bonuses, and quarterly resident satisfaction bonuses. Hawthorne also offers a career path program, education reimbursement for maintenance-related training, and a full benefits package including dental, medical, vision, 401(k) match, paid parental leave, and paid time off that includes your birthday.

job.title: Affordable Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Andover Commons is a residential community managed by John M. Corcoran and Company, a New England real estate firm with roots going back to 1951. They're hiring a Maintenance Technician to join the on-site team, and this particular role sits squarely at the intersection of hands-on trade work and resident-facing service. It's a Monday through Friday schedule (8:00 am to 4:30 pm) with an on-call rotation, and the pay range runs $29 to $33 per hour depending on experience, plus a $2,500 sign-on bonus.

What You'll Actually Do

The day-to-day work covers the full range of residential building maintenance. You'll run service requests as they come in, which means anything from appliance repairs and smoke detector installations to light fixture swaps, door hardware, tile work, and handrail fixes. Make-ready work is part of the picture too, so expect painting, window replacements, and screen changes between turns. When outside contractors or suppliers are on-site, you'll coordinate with them and keep the related paperwork in order. Emergency response is part of the job as well, including flood situations and back-to-back move-ins that require quick turnaround.

The role isn't purely reactive. Keeping the property looking well-maintained is a consistent expectation, which means routine cosmetic upkeep runs alongside the urgent stuff.

What You Bring

  • At least 6 months of trade or building maintenance experience
  • Working knowledge of electrical and mechanical systems used in residential properties
  • Ability to identify safety concerns and act on them without being told twice
  • Composure under pressure, particularly during high-volume move-in periods or emergencies
  • Specialized trade experience in plumbing, electrical, HVAC, or roofing is a real advantage here

Where This Role Leads

For someone early in their maintenance career, an affordable housing property is genuinely good training ground. The resident population tends to generate consistent, varied service volume, which means you rack up repair hours faster than you might at a lower-traffic asset. Technicians who build proficiency here often move into lead or supervisor roles, and the skills you develop, including HVAC troubleshooting, contractor oversight, and paperwork discipline, translate directly to higher-responsibility positions at Class A properties or larger portfolio operations. JMC's tenure data backs this up: a meaningful number of their team members have spent years or decades with the company, which suggests internal mobility is real rather than theoretical. If you're looking to grow a trade skillset while working for an organization with actual institutional depth, this is a reasonable place to invest time.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor - Altura Apartments
job.description:
Maintenance supervision at a lease-up property demands a specific skill set: the ability to manage make-ready schedules under pressure, troubleshoot across multiple trades without calling a contractor for every problem, and build vendor relationships before you actually need them. Altura Apartments is a brand-new 201-unit luxury community in Cincinnati, and Ackermann Group is hiring the Maintenance Supervisor who will set the operational tone from day one.

What This Role Actually Requires

The technical range here is real. Ackermann wants someone who can perform specialist-level work across plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliance repair, carpentry, and painting. EPA Type I and II certification is required; CPO and CAMT are preferred. Aquatherm system experience is a plus and worth mentioning on your application if you have it. This is a hands-on supervisory role, which means you're not just delegating and reviewing punch lists. You're working alongside your team while also managing the budget, tracking parts inventory, and negotiating rates with local vendors.

Day-to-day, you'll coordinate the make-ready schedule to keep vacant units market-ready, oversee service request completion, and ensure all amenity spaces hold up to luxury-class standards. You'll also participate in capex planning and execution, coordinate preventive maintenance, and document everything in Ackermann's property management software. Admin fluency in Microsoft Office and Outlook is expected. After-hours emergency on-call rotation is part of the job. That's standard for this role at any community; plan accordingly.

Leading a Team at a New Community

Opening a new property as Maintenance Supervisor is genuinely different from stepping into an established one. There's no deferred maintenance backlog to sort through, but you're also building team habits, vendor lists, and preventive maintenance routines from scratch. The systems you put in place in the first year tend to stick. Ackermann wants someone who can participate in hiring, run productive team meetings, and hold standards without waiting to be told. Three or more years of maintenance experience with supervisory responsibility is the baseline.

Ackermann Group and This Property

Ackermann has operated in the Midwest since 1938. That kind of tenure in regional real estate usually means a stable ownership structure and an institutional memory about how properties should run. This isn't a third-party management situation where priorities shift with the client. Ackermann builds, owns, and manages its own portfolio, which tends to mean maintenance teams have more consistency in resources and decision-making support.

Compensation is hourly with quarterly bonus potential and lease renewal commission eligibility. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k with company match, PTO, and an employee rent discount at any Ackermann community.

  • EPA Type I and II Certification required
  • CPO and CAMT preferred
  • Aquatherm experience preferred
  • 3+ years maintenance experience with supervisory responsibility
  • Valid driver's license with proof of insurance
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm, with emergency on-call rotation

job.title: Assistant Property Manager at Raveneaux Apartments
job.description:
Raveneaux Apartments is a Cottonwood Residential community in Houston, and they're bringing on an Assistant Property Manager to help run the day-to-day alongside the Property Manager. It's a real operations role, not a leasing position with a fancier title.

You'll spend a meaningful part of your week on the administrative side: collecting rent, managing delinquency, keeping resident files current, and preparing legal notices when they're needed. That last piece matters. Delivering a notice correctly, on time, and with the right documentation behind it can make or break an eviction proceeding if it gets that far. Residents will also come to you with billing questions, payment disputes, and general concerns, so your ability to stay composed and clear under pressure is going to show up daily.

Vendor coordination is part of it too. You'll track work orders, follow up with contractors, and make sure things actually get done. That sounds straightforward until a vendor doesn't show, a resident is following up for the third time, and the property manager is out that day. When the PM is unavailable, this role carries the property. That's expected, not exceptional.

Cottonwood has been an early adopter of self-guided tours, so the leasing side of your work will involve some tech-forward processes. If you've only ever worked communities with traditional agent-led tours, there's a short learning curve, but it's manageable. The bigger adjustment is getting comfortable holding multiple responsibilities at once without letting the detail work slip.

Weekend availability is required. That's a real constraint for some people, and it's worth knowing upfront.

What they're looking for

  • Background in leasing, sales, or customer service
  • Solid written and verbal communication skills
  • Working knowledge of basic accounting practices
  • Familiarity with Fair Housing Laws
  • Experience with Entrata is a plus
  • Ability to juggle competing tasks without dropping the detail work

Cottonwood offers competitive base pay with a quarterly bonus, full health, vision, dental, life, and disability coverage available within your first month, a 401k and HSA with company match, three weeks of PTO in year one, and 10.5 paid holidays.

Strong candidates for this role tend to be the ones who've already handled delinquency follow-up and resident communications at the same time without needing someone to triage their day. Comfort with numbers and a working knowledge of property management software will separate you from candidates who lean entirely on the leasing side of their background.

job.title: Full-Time Concierge (Mon-Fri 4pm-12am)
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is an evening shift role, Monday through Friday, 4pm to midnight, at a Class A residential community in Rockville managed by Comstock. The hours matter: you're the face of the building during the time residents are actually home. That means handling a steady stream of arriving residents, guests, and deliveries, coordinating amenity reservations, managing the loading dock and elevator scheduling, and keeping the lobby looking the part throughout the night. You'll field phone calls, respond to resident concerns, and make judgment calls about building access every single shift.

Daily building walks are part of the rhythm. You're flagging maintenance items, straightening common areas, and doing the small things that keep a Class A property feeling like one. The work is more active than a typical front desk job, and the pace picks up around dinner hours when foot traffic peaks.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma or GED
  • At least one year in a concierge or high-end customer service role, preferably in residential property, hospitality, or a similarly guest-facing environment
  • Comfortable working with Microsoft Office, particularly Outlook, Word, and Excel
  • Ability to work holidays and pick up additional shifts when the schedule requires it
  • Strong communication skills, both written and verbal, and the instinct to handle difficult situations with composure
  • Trustworthy and accountable, two qualities that matter especially when you're working largely unsupervised on an evening shift

Context Worth Knowing

Rockville's mixed-use residential market has grown considerably with Comstock's development around the Shady Grove and Rockville Pike corridors. Residents in these communities tend to have high expectations and many options. The concierge position at this tier of property carries real weight: a confident, polished evening presence directly influences how residents feel about where they live, which connects to renewals and retention in ways that don't always show up on a punch list but absolutely show up in NOI over time.

For candidates with hospitality backgrounds looking to move into property management, this role builds the resident relations instincts that carry well into leasing or property management coordinator positions. Comstock's expanding portfolio also means internal mobility is a realistic path, not just a line in a job posting.

Compensation ranges from $18 to $21 per hour, with bonus potential and a benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, 401(k) match, housing discount, commuter benefits, free parking with EV charging, and parental leave.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role puts you at the operational center of a residential property in Waukee, Iowa. You're not just fixing things. You're building and running a maintenance operation. Day to day, that means overseeing HVAC, plumbing, and electrical systems, keeping preventative maintenance schedules on track, and making sure turns and make-readies get completed to standard. Curb appeal, common areas, and unit condition all fall under your watch. You'll also carry a budget, which means purchasing supplies thoughtfully and keeping costs aligned with what the property can sustain.

Team leadership is a real part of this job. You'll train technicians, give feedback, assign work orders, and set the standard for quality on-site. BAM Companies operates across multiple properties, so the culture and work ethic you build on your team will reflect directly on the brand.

What You Bring

  • 2 to 3 years of hands-on property maintenance experience. Prior supervisory experience is a plus but not required if you have the technical depth and leadership instincts.
  • EPA Type 2 or Universal Certification. This is a hard requirement for handling refrigerants legally and correctly.
  • Practical working knowledge of HVAC systems, plumbing, and electrical. You should be able to diagnose, not just report.
  • A valid driver's license and reliable vehicle.
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills. You'll be coordinating with residents, vendors, and property management, so communication gaps cost time and trust.

Where This Role Develops You

Maintenance Supervisors who perform well in multi-site or growing management companies tend to move toward Regional Maintenance Director roles, where they oversee technical standards and capital planning across a portfolio. The skills this role builds specifically, budget management, team development, preventative maintenance programming, and vendor coordination, are exactly what those next-level roles require. If you've been a strong technician looking to step up, this is the position where you make that transition credible.

One thing worth knowing about Waukee: it's one of the faster-growing suburbs in the Des Moines metro, which means the apartment market there sees consistent lease-up activity and steady occupancy demand. For a maintenance supervisor, that translates to a real volume of work orders and turns, which is genuinely good for skill development but does require someone who can manage a pace that doesn't always slow down.

Pay for this position runs between $27 and $32 per hour depending on experience, and BAM offers medical, dental, vision, and life insurance coverage alongside a substantial paid time off package and housing discounts at BAM properties.

job.title: Sr. Regional Real Estate Manager - Pacific Northwest Region
job.description:
Where This Role Lives in the Organization

Regional property management at this level is fundamentally a relationship-management discipline dressed in operational clothing. The financials matter, the inspections matter, the compliance matters. But what separates a strong senior regional manager from a capable one is how well they hold together a web of people: site teams spread across a market, clients with real money and real expectations, and a corporate leadership team that needs accurate information to make good decisions. CloudTen Residential is looking for someone who understands that dynamic and thrives inside it.

CloudTen manages a genuinely varied multifamily portfolio across the West, and their Portland metro group reflects that variety. Hotel-to-residential conversions, high-rise lease-ups, value-add repositioning plays. Each of those asset types carries different operational rhythms, different resident profiles, and different client expectations around performance. The person in this role needs to be comfortable context-switching between a lease-up where traffic and concessions dominate the weekly conversation and a stabilized asset where NOI discipline and delinquency management take center stage.

What the Work Actually Involves

This is a senior leadership position overseeing multiple properties and the managers who run them day-to-day. You're not the person solving a broken HVAC unit at 7am. You're the person who built the team that handles it, coached the manager who escalates it correctly, and reviews the capex line to know whether that unit should be repaired or replaced. The work is a mix of people development, financial oversight, client communication, and strategic planning, and all four have to move together.

Day-to-day, you'll be reviewing monthly financials across the portfolio, preparing and monitoring budgets, and catching variances before they become problems. You'll conduct property inspections with an eye toward operational consistency, not just curb appeal. You'll carry relationships with existing clients and help develop new ones, which means being fluent in how a T-12 tells a story and how to present a repositioning plan that earns trust.

On the people side, you'll provide direct mentorship and oversight to regional managers, assistant regional managers, district and area managers, and property administrators. That's a meaningful leadership span. Performance evaluations, sensitive personnel situations, recruitment, team culture. It all lands here.

Key qualifications CloudTen is looking for:

  • At least five years of directly relevant multifamily experience, ideally at the regional or multi-site level
  • Strong financial acumen, specifically around property financial reports, budget preparation, and income and expense analysis
  • An active real estate license (preferred)
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office, Word and Excel in particular
  • High school diploma or equivalent required; college degree or related coursework is a plus

What tends to separate strong candidates here is the combination of financial sharpness and people instincts. Plenty of regional managers can read a T-12. Fewer can walk into a site that's underperforming, figure out quickly whether the problem is operational, personnel, or market-driven, and then build a credible path forward with the site team rather than around them. That's the skill set CloudTen is hiring for.

The role carries a compensation range of $145,000 to $160,000 depending on experience, structured as a combination of base pay and expected supplemental wages. A hybrid work model is in place, alongside medical, dental, and vision benefits, FSA options, company-paid life insurance, and paid time off.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Technician - Citigate Apartment Homes
job.description:
Maintenance work in multifamily is as much about diagnostic thinking as it is about turning a wrench. At Citigate Apartment Homes in Jacksonville, the technician who thrives here carries genuine trade depth across at least two disciplines and applies it quickly, accurately, and with enough resident-facing polish that service requests close on the first visit.

The Skills This Role Puts to Work Daily

AIR Communities runs industry-leading maintenance technology at Citigate, which means work orders are prioritized and tracked in real time. That shifts the skill requirement slightly: strong technicians here combine hands-on trade ability with the organizational habits to close tickets cleanly, document accurately, and communicate status to residents without being prompted. Plumbing, electrical, appliance repair, HVAC, and carpentry are all in play. You don't need mastery in all of them, but you need genuine competence in at least two and the intellectual curiosity to keep building from there.

Make-readies are a consistent part of the workflow. Completing apartment turns on schedule, walking punch lists thoroughly, and handing over move-in-ready homes without callbacks requires the kind of systematic approach that separates good technicians from great ones. Move-in and move-out inspections round out the cycle, so you're involved in the full resident lifecycle, not just reactive repairs.

Scope and Schedule

  • Diagnose, troubleshoot, and repair plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliances, and general building systems
  • Complete apartment turns and make-ready work to support occupancy
  • Handle service requests efficiently and document them accurately using AIR's maintenance platform
  • Participate in on-call rotations (at least one week per month) and respond to after-hours emergency calls
  • Support vendor coordination and quality control efforts on-site
  • Provide trade guidance to less experienced teammates when the situation calls for it

The on-call component is real and worth understanding clearly. Emergency maintenance after hours is part of the job, and a reliable personal vehicle is required to respond. Scheduling flexibility across evenings and weekends is expected, particularly during high-traffic seasons when turn volume picks up.

Compensation, Development, and What Makes AIR Different Here

The hourly range runs $19 to $22, calibrated to your actual skill set and relevant experience. On top of base pay, a monthly customer service bonus of up to $250 rewards technicians who consistently earn positive resident feedback. That structure means your interpersonal approach directly affects your paycheck, which is an honest reflection of how central resident satisfaction is to the role.

A 50% rent discount at any AIR community is available, including the option to live on-site at Citigate itself. For someone who values eliminating commute time and wants their housing and work life aligned, that's a meaningful benefit. AIR also backs career growth with a formal development program called Ascend, built around individual career paths rather than a generic training checklist. Tuition assistance and up to 100% reimbursement for job-related certifications make it practical to pursue HVAC credentials, EPA 608, or other licenses that move your earning potential forward.

Candidates need at least two years of maintenance experience in a facilities or building environment, proficiency in two or more trades, and the physical capability to handle equipment and machinery. A pre-employment background check and four-panel drug screen (marijuana excluded) are part of the offer process.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Cortland Duluth
job.description:
Cortland operates one of the larger vertically integrated multifamily platforms in the country, which means their maintenance staff works inside a system that actually has infrastructure behind it: in-house design and construction teams, standardized processes, and a portfolio-wide approach to asset preservation. For a technician who wants more than just a work order queue, that context matters.

The Duluth property is a community-level role, but the work touches everything. On any given day you might be diagnosing an HVAC issue in one unit, responding to a plumbing call in another, checking that automatic entry doors and surveillance systems are functioning properly, and wrapping up a punch list item from a recent turn. Preventative maintenance on HVAC equipment is a real part of the job here, not an afterthought, which tends to reduce emergency call volume over time for technicians who stay on top of it. You'll also manage parts inventory and document completed work, which sounds administrative but directly supports the property's ability to close work orders fast and keep residents satisfied.

EPA certification (Type I, II, or Universal) is required before you start. Cortland is also looking for candidates with at least one to three years of hands-on experience across electrical, plumbing, HVAC, and appliance repair. On-call rotation is part of this position, so reliability during off-hours is genuinely expected, not just listed as a formality.

What strong candidates bring

  • EPA Universal certification (preferred over Type I or II alone)
  • Demonstrated HVAC diagnostic and repair skills, not just filter changes
  • Experience managing a personal work order queue across multiple unit types
  • Comfort communicating with residents directly, professionally, and with patience
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Physical readiness for ladder work, outdoor conditions, and lifting

From a career development standpoint, this kind of role inside a top-10 multifamily operator builds a foundation that transfers well. Technicians who develop strong diagnostic depth and learn to work within a standardized PM system often move into lead technician or maintenance supervisor roles within a few years. At a company of Cortland's scale, that path exists in-house. The combination of preventative maintenance discipline, resident-facing service, and asset documentation you'll build here shows up on a resume in ways that generalist handyman experience doesn't.

If you want a role where the technical work is real, the support structure is established, and the company has enough scale to offer a genuine next step, this position in Duluth is worth a close look.

job.title: Regional Manager
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is a portfolio-level operations role with Asset Living, one of the larger third-party management firms in the country. As Regional Manager based in Dallas, you'll carry full accountability for a portfolio of communities, overseeing everything from daily leasing activity and maintenance responsiveness to budget performance and personnel decisions. You're not reviewing reports from a distance. You're making calls on staffing changes, approving vendor contracts, monitoring delinquency trends, and working directly with Community Managers to keep NOI on track.

Financial oversight is a core part of the job. You'll build and defend annual operating budgets, write monthly variance narratives on income and expense lines that drift off target, and flag capex needs before they become emergencies. On the leasing side, you'll develop yearly marketing plans, assess whether on-site teams are converting traffic effectively, and step in to course-correct when occupancy or renewal performance slips. You'll also manage resident retention strategy at a portfolio level, not just site by site.

Personnel management takes up a meaningful share of the role. You'll hire, coach, and when necessary terminate Community Managers and their teams. You'll approve salary change requests, review counseling documentation, and ensure that HR processes are followed correctly across every site. Asset Living operates across multifamily, affordable housing, student housing, build-to-rent, and single-family rental, so the properties under your oversight may span more than one product type.

What You Bring

  • Demonstrated experience managing a multi-site residential portfolio, with full P&L responsibility
  • Comfort reading and explaining financial statements, T-12s, and budget-to-actual variances
  • Experience hiring and developing on-site leasing and maintenance staff
  • Working knowledge of Fair Housing regulations and the liability considerations that come with offsite leadership
  • Strong instincts around leasing strategy, including when to adjust concessions, pricing, or marketing approach based on occupancy and traffic data
  • Ability to manage multiple competing priorities across sites without losing visibility into any one property

Market and Role Context

Dallas is one of the most competitive multifamily markets in the country, and supply pressure from new Class A deliveries has kept concessions elevated across several submarkets. A Regional Manager here needs to understand how to defend occupancy and rental rates when nearby lease-ups are offering significant move-in incentives. The ability to read a T-3 and adjust strategy quickly, rather than waiting for monthly reporting cycles, separates strong candidates from average ones in this market.

Asset Living operates as a fee management firm, which means you're accountable not just to internal metrics but to ownership relationships. Accurate financial reporting, clean closeouts, and proactive communication with ownership are part of what makes a Regional Manager effective here. Candidates who come from in-house roles and haven't worked in third-party management should expect a steeper adjustment to those dual accountability demands.

job.title: Groundskeeper
job.description:
Groundskeeper work at a multifamily community is one of those roles that looks simple from the outside and reveals its real texture once you're in it. The physical demands are real: you're outdoors year-round in Texas heat and the occasional cold snap, picking up litter and pet waste daily, operating backpack blowers and power washers, moving items up to 50 pounds, and keeping up with a property's curb appeal from the moment residents and prospects first see it. That's not glamorous, but it's consequential. First impressions drive traffic, and traffic drives occupancy.

Weinstein Properties has managed apartment communities for over 70 years under continuous family ownership, which is genuinely uncommon in this industry. The company operates more than 60 communities across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia, and this particular opening is at Bexley Grapevine. The schedule is Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm, which is a real quality-of-life advantage in a field where weekend and on-call coverage is often expected. Starting pay is $16.50 per hour with quarterly bonuses and a $1,000 stay-on bonus available after 90 days in good standing.

From a career-building standpoint, this role is worth thinking about seriously if you're considering a path in property maintenance. Groundskeepers who develop a sharp eye for property conditions, build trust with their maintenance and leasing teams, and handle the physical demands consistently tend to move into make-ready and maintenance tech roles faster than people expect. The skills compound: understanding how a property looks to a prospect walking in for the first time, recognizing what needs to go on a punch list, staying organized through repetitive daily tasks without cutting corners. These are exactly the habits that maintenance supervisors look for when evaluating who's ready for more responsibility.

What Weinstein Is Looking For

  • Reliability above all. Showing up on time every day matters more in this role than almost any credential.
  • Self-direction. Much of the work happens without moment-to-moment supervision, so internal motivation counts.
  • Physical readiness to work outdoors in all weather, lift and carry heavy items repeatedly, and handle a range of equipment including golf carts and trailers.
  • Willingness to take on varied tasks, including light painting, housekeeping support, and trashing out vacant units as needed.
  • A collaborative mindset. Groundskeepers work alongside maintenance and leasing staff, and the people who do well here communicate well and help without being asked.
  • A growth orientation. The company explicitly promotes from within for candidates who demonstrate attitude and aptitude.

If you've been in labor or landscaping and are looking for a path into property management, this is a legitimate entry point with a company that has the track record to back up its growth claims. Weinstein's hands-on operational philosophy means you're more likely to be seen and developed here than at a large REIT where groundskeeping is a contractor function. That distinction matters when you're building a career.

job.title: Community Manager - Novo Apartments
job.description:
It's mid-morning and you're reviewing last night's delinquency report while a leasing consultant walks in with questions about a concession approval. Your maintenance lead texts about a make-ready that's two days behind schedule. This is the rhythm of the Community Manager role at Novo Apartments, a property where operational command and team development happen in the same breath.

What This Role Demands

MG Properties is looking for a Community Manager with recent, direct experience running an apartment community at full operational tempo. This isn't a role where supervisory responsibility is occasional. You'll own the full management cycle: building and developing your onsite team, driving leasing and marketing efforts, maintaining budget integrity, and keeping day-to-day operations running at the standard a well-positioned Mountain View property requires.

The budget component deserves specific attention. You'll be accountable for overseeing expenditures, tracking performance against targets, and making decisions that protect NOI. That means reading financials with confidence and catching variances before they compound. Yardi experience will serve you well here, as the team works within that platform for core property operations.

Mountain View sits in one of the most competitive rental submarkets in the Bay Area. Renters in this corridor have high expectations and real options, so your marketing instincts and ability to convert traffic into signed leases matter as much as your operational discipline. Concession strategy, renewal retention, and occupancy management all fall within your scope.

What You'll Build From Here

This role is a genuine leadership development opportunity, even for someone who already has years of management experience. MG Properties has operated across the Western U.S. for over three decades, and Community Managers at this level often develop toward regional oversight roles as they demonstrate sustained NOI performance and team development results. The company also offers profit sharing, which means your work has a direct line to a financial return beyond your base salary.

What separates strong candidates in this specific role is the ability to develop people while holding operational standards. Many managers can do one or the other well. Novo Apartments needs someone who can train a leasing consultant on closing technique on Monday and present a corrected budget variance to ownership on Wednesday.

Here's a summary of what the position requires and what it offers:

  • Recent supervisory experience managing a multifamily apartment community
  • Demonstrated skills across marketing, sales, and budget management
  • Yardi experience (preferred, not required)
  • Valid driver's license and proof of insurance
  • Compensation of $105,000 to $110,000 annually, depending on experience
  • Monthly and performance-based incentive bonuses, plus company profit sharing
  • 401(k) with employer match, full medical/dental/vision, and rental discounts
  • Paid time off, holidays, personal days, and paid sick time

MG Properties participates in E-Verify and conducts background checks and drug screening as part of the hiring process.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Skills at the Center of This Role

Student housing runs on relationship velocity. At 18-Seventy Nine in Huntsville, Texas, the Experience Team Member role pulls on three skill sets simultaneously: sales instincts, community marketing, and front-line operations. If you're strong in all three, this position keeps you fully engaged. If you're building toward a leasing career, it's one of the better training grounds available in the student housing sector.

Scion operates in a niche that moves faster than conventional multifamily. Lease-up timelines are compressed, Turn periods are intense, and the resident base turns over on academic calendars rather than month-to-month rhythms. That context shapes everything this role touches.

What You'll Be Doing Day to Day

Your primary function is converting prospect interest into signed leases. That means conducting tours, fielding objections, and feeding useful intelligence back to the management team about what's working and what's not in the sales process. You're not just executing a script; you're expected to identify local marketing angles and pass those recommendations up the chain.

The role also carries real administrative weight. Package management, maintenance coordination, office organization, and after-hours lockout coverage are all part of the job. In student housing, after-hours calls are a genuine part of the rotation, and Turn periods, when hundreds of residents move out and back in within days, demand a level of operational stamina that most traditional leasing roles never require.
