The pay range runs $23 to $25 per hour depending on experience and skill set. Benefits include employer-subsidized medical coverage through Meritain Health, employer-paid vision and life insurance, a 401(k) with company match (100% on the first 3%, 50% on the next 2%), 15 days of PTO, 7 sick days, and 12 or more paid holidays. There's also a flexible spending account, pet insurance, disability coverage, and employee discount programs on appliances and apparel.

Fairstead's affordable housing model puts genuine pressure on operational efficiency. NOI discipline matters, capex decisions get scrutinized, and the residents depending on these properties don't have easy alternatives if maintenance falls behind. That's not a reason to avoid the role. It's a reason to take it seriously.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - The Hixon
job.description:
Maintenance Technician roles at mid-size regional operators like CloudTen tend to be broader in scope than those at large institutional portfolios. You're not handed a narrow specialty. You handle the full range of unit and common-area work, and that variety is exactly what builds a well-rounded skill set over time.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

The Hixon is a CloudTen property in Bend, Oregon, and this role supports the day-to-day physical condition of the community. That means handling general repairs across plumbing, electrical, HVAC, carpentry, and appliances, along with keeping common areas, pools, laundry rooms, and grounds in good shape. A significant part of the rhythm here is turns: getting vacant units rent-ready within a 3-to-5-day window. That timeline requires coordination, prioritization, and the ability to move through a punch list efficiently without cutting corners on quality.

Resident service requests carry a 24-hour resolution expectation, which keeps the workload structured but fast-moving. On-call emergency coverage is part of the role, so schedule flexibility matters. The position also involves preventive maintenance work, documented inspections covering fire safety, life-safety systems, lighting, and pool equipment, and an ongoing familiarity with utility shutoffs and safety protocols across the property.

Qualifications Worth Noting

  • At least one to two years of hands-on experience across plumbing, electrical, HVAC, carpentry, and painting
  • Valid driver's license in good standing (travel between assigned properties is part of the role)
  • Comfort using a mobile device and basic computer tools for work orders and communication
  • Ability to work weekends, evenings, and holidays, including after-hours emergency response
  • Strong attention to detail and the discipline to work independently without close supervision

Where This Role Leads

Technicians who build proficiency across multiple trades and develop a track record for fast, quality turns are the ones who move into Maintenance Supervisor positions. CloudTen's portfolio spans hotel-to-residential conversions, high-rise lease-ups, and value-add repositioning projects, which means there's genuine variety in the types of properties and challenges you'd encounter over time. Exposure to that range, especially early in a maintenance career, compounds well. The diagnostic thinking you sharpen on HVAC and plumbing carries directly into more complex systems work at larger or higher-classification properties down the road.

Pay for this role runs $25.00 to $28.00 per hour depending on experience. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a flexible spending account, company-paid life insurance, and paid time off.

job.title: Part-Time Leasing Consultant
job.description:
A prospect just submitted an inquiry at 9 PM. By the time they tour Saturday morning, they've already heard from two competitors. How you handle that 18-hour window is what separates a signed lease from a lost lead.

PeakMade Real Estate is hiring a part-time Leasing Consultant at their Austin community. This is a front-line sales role, and it's structured that way intentionally. You're the first real human impression most prospects get, and the work asks you to hold that standard across every touchpoint, from the first phone call to the moment someone hands over a deposit.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Your core job is converting leads into signed leases. That means working phone, email, and in-person traffic with equal energy, running tours that actually identify what a prospect needs rather than just walking the floor plan, and following up in a way that feels personal rather than scripted. You'll track your own leads in a CRM (Yardi, Entrata, RealPage, or similar) and you're expected to keep that data clean and current. Market knowledge matters here too: pricing, availability, and what competitors are doing all factor into how you guide a prospect toward a decision.

Beyond leasing, you'll support the operational rhythm of the office. That includes collecting deposits, processing lease paperwork accurately, maintaining model readiness, and helping during turn season when move-outs and move-ins stack up quickly. It's not glamorous work, but it directly affects how prospects experience the community on tour days.

Who Fits Here

  • At least one year of sales or leasing experience with a track record of hitting conversion targets
  • Real comfort with CRM systems and consistent multi-touch follow-up habits (calls, texts, emails, not just one and done)
  • Availability to work weekends and during peak leasing hours
  • A genuine ability to read people quickly and adjust your approach by prospect

The strongest candidates in roles like this tend to be the ones who treat follow-up as a discipline rather than a chore. Conversion rates in leasing often hinge less on the tour itself and more on what happens in the 24 to 72 hours after. If you've built systems for that, even informal ones, you'll move faster here than someone who relies on natural charisma alone.

This role is commission-eligible, and PeakMade offers housing discounts, a 401(k) match, wellness programs, and development opportunities within their growing portfolio. Austin's rental market stays competitive, which means strong leasing consultants here get real reps at a high volume and tend to build a resume that translates well into full-time leasing, assistant manager, or even property manager tracks down the road.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Technician - McCullers Walk
job.description:
Maintenance techs at institutional operators like AIR Communities work differently than at your typical third-party managed community. The work order volume is real, the technology is actually used, and the expectation is that you're moving through your queue efficiently, not waiting on parts or hunting down tools. McCullers Walk in Raleigh is that kind of operation.

The Work

Day to day, you're handling the full range of residential maintenance: troubleshooting plumbing, swapping out electrical components, servicing HVAC equipment, and keeping appliances running. Turns are part of the rhythm here too. AIR runs a structured make-ready process, so when a unit comes back, you're following a defined punch list to get it move-in ready, not improvising your way through it. Some days you're completing resident service requests back to back. Others you're assisting with vendor quality checks or doing move-out inspections. The mix shifts with the season and the community's needs.

On-call rotation is real and worth knowing upfront. You'll cover at least one week per month and need reliable transportation to respond to after-hours calls. That's the nature of residential maintenance, and it's baked into the schedule expectations here.

What AIR Is Looking For

  • At least two years of maintenance experience in a facilities or building environment
  • Proficiency in at least two trades: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliance repair, or carpentry
  • Comfortable with physical demands, including moving heavy equipment
  • Flexible availability including evenings, weekends, and on-call shifts
  • Someone who fixes things correctly the first time and doesn't leave callbacks behind

Compensation and Growth

The pay range runs $20 to $22 per hour based on your actual skill set, plus a monthly customer service bonus of up to $250 for techs who consistently deliver solid resident experiences. The 50% rent discount at any AIR community is a meaningful benefit if you want to live onsite and cut your commute to zero.

AIR promotes internally whenever possible and has a formal maintenance development program called Ascend that's built around your individual path, not a generic training checklist. Techs who come in sharp at two trades and show an appetite for learning often move into lead or service manager roles within a few years. That's a reasonable trajectory at a portfolio this size.

What separates a strong candidate here from a competent one is comfort with technology-driven dispatching. AIR uses digital tools to prioritize and assign work orders, so if you're used to paper logs and verbal hand-offs, there's a learning curve. Techs who adapt quickly to that workflow tend to carry higher resident satisfaction scores, which is where that monthly bonus actually gets paid out.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Manager
job.description:
Skills That Run This Role

This position draws on a specific combination of hands-on trade knowledge and people management. You're coordinating maintenance staff, setting the tone for how work gets done, and stepping in personally when a task demands it. Organizational thinking matters here as much as technical ability. A maintenance team that's poorly scheduled or poorly supervised creates friction for residents and for the property management team above you. Strong candidates tend to be people who've worked their way up through maintenance roles and understand both sides of that equation: what it's like to be on the tools, and what it takes to manage others who are.

Safety awareness runs through everything in this job. Fairstead has specific safety policies and standards, and the expectation is that you'll model and enforce those consistently, not just reference them when something goes wrong. If you have OSHA familiarity or have managed safety compliance in a previous maintenance role, that translates well here.

What the Day-to-Day Involves

You'll oversee the repair and maintenance of residential buildings, inspect and address electrical and mechanical systems, and keep facilities clean and functional in line with company standards. That includes leading special projects and stepping into a supervisory role on any work that requires coordination across your team. For more routine tasks, you'll often work independently. For complex projects, there's support available, but the expectation is that you're managing the workflow and the people, not waiting to be directed.

  • Supervise and coordinate maintenance staff on daily tasks and special projects
  • Perform skilled maintenance and repair work across mechanical, electrical, and general building systems
  • Ensure all facilities meet Fairstead's cleanliness and safety standards
  • Apply and improve internal maintenance policies and procedures
  • Use Yardi or RealPage for work order tracking (familiarity preferred)
  • Be available occasionally for overtime tied to emergencies or project demands

Three years of property maintenance experience is the baseline. Beyond that, Fairstead is looking for someone who's proficient in at least one specific trade and can hold their own across general maintenance disciplines. Microsoft Office proficiency is expected for reporting and communication purposes.

Working Within Fairstead's Structure

Fairstead manages over 30,000 units across 28 states with an integrated platform that connects ownership, construction, and property management. That integration matters for this role because decisions don't happen in isolation. A maintenance issue that looks like a simple repair might connect to a capital improvement project already in the pipeline. Understanding how to communicate upward, flag concerns clearly, and coordinate with a broader team is part of what makes someone effective here, not just technically capable.

Affordable housing maintenance comes with its own realities. Residents often depend heavily on working systems in ways that market-rate tenants may not, and response time carries more weight. The strongest candidates for this role aren't just skilled with tools. They understand that the work connects directly to people's daily lives, and they manage their team with that in mind.

Fairstead's benefits package includes employer-contributed medical insurance, employer-paid vision and life insurance, a 401(k) with company match (100% of the first 3%, 50% of the next 2%), 15 PTO days, 7 sick days, 12 or more paid holidays, and an FSA option among others.

job.title: Leasing Specialist
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role lives at the front end of the revenue funnel. Your job is converting traffic into signed leases at Dream St. Augustine, a community in St. Augustine, FL backed by DLP Capital. Lead response time is a firm 4-hour window, which means your mornings can shift fast depending on overnight inquiries. Tours, follow-ups, CRM updates, and closing conversations fill most of the day. Lease-up experience is required here, not preferred. The expectation is that you already understand how to build occupancy from a cold start and keep it moving.

Beyond the leasing floor, you'll build genuine referral pipelines by networking with major employers, hospitals, and universities in the area. St. Augustine draws a mix of healthcare workers, hospitality industry professionals, and university staff, giving you real targets to build cross-promotion relationships with. Weekly prospecting is a formal expectation, not a nice-to-have. You'll also create and run resident programs that support retention, because keeping a current resident costs far less than filling a vacancy.

Property walks are part of the routine. You're not just selling the community on tour; you're watching it the way a prospect would see it. Punch list items that slip through affect close rates, and you'll be expected to flag them. CRM discipline matters here too. Guest cards, follow-ups, and lease paperwork need to stay current because leadership visibility into your pipeline depends on it.

What You Bring

  • Demonstrated lease-up experience (this is a hard requirement)
  • Strong customer service background with a track record of closing
  • Comfort reading income statements and basic financial documents
  • Excellent written and verbal communication across all levels, including senior leadership
  • Experience managing on-site projects and leading through change
  • Familiarity with Appfolio, G-Suite, and Microsoft Office (a plus, not required)
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation

The Role in Context

Compensation runs $18 to $23 per hour depending on experience. The position is full-time and reports into the community's management structure with direct communication lines to senior leadership at DLP Capital. The parent company has appeared on the Inc. 5000 fastest-growing private companies list for 14 consecutive years, which tells you something about the pace of growth you'd be operating inside.

Candidates who excel in roles like this tend to be the ones who treat traffic-to-lease conversion as a number they own personally, not a team metric to share credit for. If you've managed your own leasing funnel, tracked your own close rates, and built referral sources from scratch during a lease-up, this role fits the way you already think. Benefits include PTO, health, dental, vision, and life insurance, 401(k) with matching, and learning incentives.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
PeakMade Real Estate manages off-campus student housing alongside conventional multifamily and build-to-rent communities across the country. Their Springfield property is hiring a Maintenance Technician to handle the full range of day-to-day upkeep that keeps a community running and residents renewing.

What You'll Actually Do

This is a hands-on, full-cycle maintenance role. You'll work through service requests, keep the turn process moving during move-out and make-ready periods, and hold down a spot in the on-call rotation for after-hours emergencies. Preventative maintenance is a real part of the job, not an afterthought. You'll follow manufacturer schedules on equipment, keep chemical logs current for pool maintenance, and help the Maintenance Supervisor track inventory so the team isn't caught short on parts mid-repair. Curb appeal and common area cleanliness fall under your scope too, including breezeways, grounds, and exterior spaces.

On the resident-facing side, you'll be expected to communicate professionally with people who are often frustrated when something breaks. That requires patience and follow-through, not just technical skill.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of maintenance experience, ideally in the apartment industry
  • Ability to troubleshoot and repair HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliances
  • EPA Type I and II certification preferred
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Your own hand tools (required)
  • Reliable transportation and the ability to live within 30 miles of the property
  • Flexibility to work weekends, holidays, and rotating on-call shifts
  • Physical capability to lift up to 50 pounds, work at height on ladders, and operate in outdoor temperatures well above or below comfortable range

Context Worth Knowing

Springfield's rental market is heavily influenced by Missouri State University and Drury University enrollment cycles, which means a student-oriented property like this one sees predictable but intense turn seasons. If you've worked turns before, you already know what compressed make-ready timelines feel like. If you haven't, expect a steep but manageable learning curve in the late spring and summer months.

PeakMade offers a real path forward for technicians who want to grow. Their internal leadership program for facilities roles and access to HVAC and CPO certifications means this position can build credentials you carry anywhere in the industry. Technicians who develop strong preventative maintenance habits and resident communication skills tend to move into lead or supervisor roles faster than those who only focus on reactive repairs. That's the practical differentiator at this level.

Benefits include paid parental leave, PTO plus additional wellbeing days, a 401(k) match, monthly renewal bonuses, and a 10-year anniversary trip, among other recognition programs.

job.title: Maintenance Technician Apartment Community
job.description:
Apartment maintenance work is fundamentally diagnostic. Anyone can swap a part when told what's wrong. The technician who builds a real career is the one who reads a symptom, traces it to a root cause, and fixes it before a resident files a second request. That's the skill set Woodcreek Apartments in Fairview, Oregon is hiring for, and it's the skill set this role will sharpen further.

Woodcreek is a 70-unit community operated by Investment Property Group, a private firm that owns and manages roughly 150 properties across 13 states. At this scale, IPG has standardized processes for work orders, preventative maintenance schedules, and inventory control, which means you're walking into structure rather than improvising from scratch. The schedule runs Tuesday through Saturday, 8am to 5pm, with participation in an after-hours on-call rotation. Overtime pay applies to on-call hours worked. Compensation lands between $24.00 and $28.00 per hour depending on your background.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

A typical day moves between reactive and proactive tasks. You'll work through assigned work orders covering plumbing, HVAC, appliances (refrigerators, stoves, washers, dryers), and general building systems, diagnosing problems before pulling materials from inventory. You'll also walk the property and common areas to catch issues before residents do, contributing to the preventative maintenance schedule that keeps deferred costs from piling up. Communicating clearly with management about what's needed, including re-order requests and efficiency improvements, is part of the job too. This is a one-technician-style community role, meaning you have real ownership over the physical condition of the property.

What This Role Requires vs. What It Builds

Coming in, you need at least one year of multifamily maintenance experience, solid hands-on knowledge of plumbing, HVAC, and appliance repair, and your own set of hand tools. Customer service matters here as much as technical skill. Residents interact with maintenance more than almost anyone else on a property team, and how you handle those moments directly affects retention.

What this role builds is systems thinking. Working within IPG's standardized procedures across a mid-size community gives you exposure to how a regional operator tracks maintenance performance, manages costs, and connects upkeep to occupancy goals. Technicians who develop that broader operational awareness tend to move into lead or maintenance supervisor roles, because they stop seeing individual repairs and start seeing how those repairs affect NOI.

  • 1+ year of multifamily maintenance experience required
  • Working knowledge of plumbing, HVAC, and residential appliance repair
  • Personal hand tools required
  • Availability for after-hours on-call rotation
  • Strong attention to detail and resident-facing communication skills

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, life insurance, an HSA, an employee assistance program, a 401(k) with company match, and four weeks of accrued PTO. IPG also runs an employee referral program.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
Commercial property management runs on details. Lease abstracts, CAM reconciliations, vendor invoices, tenant walk-throughs, monthly reporting packages. Lincoln Property Company is hiring an Assistant Property Manager in Nashville to help keep those details in order across commercial, industrial, or retail assets.

The day-to-day here is genuinely varied. You might spend a morning reviewing vendor invoices against the management agreement's authorization limits, then shift to coordinating a tenant move-out walk-through in the afternoon, then close out the day pulling data for an operating expense reconciliation with the accounting team. Lease administration runs through this role constantly: lease setup, amendments, system updates, reporting. The Property Manager sets direction, but this role carries real execution responsibility.

Tenant communication is a significant part of the job. When a tenant reports a building issue, you're the person making sure the right people respond and that the resolution actually happens. That means working across administrative staff, building technicians, and vendors without letting things fall through the cracks. Written communication matters here because a lot of this coordination happens by email, and clear documentation protects everyone.

One honest note: commercial APM roles can carry a heavier administrative load than people expect coming in. CAM reconciliations and budget prep aren't glamorous, but they're the work. Strong candidates tend to be people who find that kind of detailed financial work satisfying rather than tedious, and who can move between a spreadsheet and a tenant conversation without losing their footing in either.

What Lincoln is Looking for

  • Bachelor's degree preferred, or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience
  • One to two years of experience in commercial property management or a related field
  • Intermediate to advanced Microsoft Office skills; experience with AP and CMMS platforms is a plus
  • Comfort with financial concepts: percentages, basic analysis, reading through lease financial terms
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Solid organizational habits and the ability to deliver on deadlines without constant reminders
  • This position is fully in-office in Nashville; remote or hybrid work is not available

Lincoln manages over 720 million square feet of commercial space across the country, which means this role connects to a large institutional platform with real training and mentorship infrastructure. For someone early in a commercial PM career, that kind of organizational depth has practical value. APMs who build strong CAM and lease administration skills here tend to move into Property Manager roles with a solid foundation that's harder to get at smaller shops.

If you know your way around a lease abstract and take vendor invoice accuracy seriously, this is a role worth taking a close look at.

job.title: Affordable Housing Compliance Specialist
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role sits inside Asset Living's affordable housing compliance operation, which means your primary function is file review. Specifically, you're pulling Affordable Housing applicant files, verifying eligibility, and confirming everything lines up with current regulatory requirements. The 24-hour turnaround expectation on file review is real, so if you work best with predictable, unhurried timelines, this one may not be the right fit.

Beyond day-to-day file work, you'll track changes in LIHTC regulations and translate those changes into actual process modifications at the property level. You'll also participate in tax credit reviews conducted by outside entities, which means you need to be comfortable with external auditors asking pointed questions about your work. Annual TDHCA training attendance is expected, and if you don't already hold the HCCP designation, you'll be required to complete that training and pass the exam within your first two years.

The travel commitment here is significant. Roughly half your work time involves travel, covering property visits, conferences, and training sessions. That's not a rounding error on the job description. Plan accordingly.

What You Bring

  • Direct experience reviewing affordable housing compliance files, particularly under the LIHTC program
  • Familiarity with RealPage OneSite Tax Credit module. This is listed as essential, not preferred
  • HCCP designation, or the willingness and eligibility to earn it within two years
  • Working knowledge of HUD programs (a plus, not a hard requirement)
  • Strong written and verbal communication. You'll be explaining compliance decisions to site staff and responding to outside reviewers
  • The kind of organizational discipline that keeps a 24-hour file review cycle from becoming a bottleneck

Context Worth Knowing

Affordable housing compliance is one of the more technically demanding specializations in third-party management. LIHTC files are not forgiving. A missed certification, an income calculation that doesn't hold up, a unit that slips out of compliance status. any of these can have real consequences for a property's tax credit allocation. Specialists who thrive in this work tend to be the ones who genuinely read the regulatory updates rather than waiting for someone to summarize them. TDHCA has made several notable adjustments to compliance monitoring in recent years, and staying current isn't optional in this role.

Asset Living operates across multifamily, student, build-to-rent, and affordable housing portfolios as a fee management firm, so the compliance team here touches a broad range of property types and structures. For someone looking to build deep expertise in affordable housing compliance, the portfolio breadth is a real advantage. The HCCP designation, once earned, also travels well if your career eventually takes you toward consulting, ownership groups, or state housing agency work.

job.title: Leasing Consultant- Andante Apartments
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

Leasing at Andante Apartments in Phoenix means you're the first face a prospect sees and the last impression that converts a tour into a signed lease. Traffic comes in, and your job is to move it through the funnel: greet, qualify, tour, close. That's the core loop. You'll work with maintenance to coordinate smooth move-ins, keep rental files current and accurate, and enter data into the property management system without letting anything slip. Delinquency conversations, maintenance complaints, lease signings , all of that lands in your lap on any given shift.

The administrative side is real. Monthly reporting tasks, organized paperwork, lease preparation , these aren't afterthoughts. A leasing consultant who can tour a prospect in the morning and reconcile files in the afternoon is the one who actually keeps occupancy healthy. MG Properties tracks performance, and bonuses (paid monthly and quarterly) reflect results.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of property management or leasing experience (preferred)
  • Proven sales ability , you know how to read a prospect and close without being pushy
  • Strong customer service instincts, especially under pressure from resident complaints or urgent move-in issues
  • Comfort with data entry and leasing software , accuracy matters when files go to compliance
  • Professional communication, written and verbal
  • A genuine preference for team environments and a company that promotes from within

Context Worth Knowing

MG Properties has operated across the Western U.S. for over 30 years, with a portfolio built through acquisition, development, and rehab. That history means internal promotion is real, not aspirational. A leasing consultant who performs here has a visible path toward assistant manager and eventually property manager. The skills you build , qualifying applicants, managing traffic-to-lease conversion, handling resident relations , transfer directly up the ladder.

Phoenix is a competitive multifamily market. Concessions come and go with supply cycles, and prospects have options. The leasing consultants who stand out aren't the ones with the slickest pitch. They're the ones who follow up consistently, know the product cold, and make the application process feel easy. That's what drives occupancy in a market like this.

MG Properties offers medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with employer match, paid time off, paid holidays, sick time, profit sharing, and rental discounts. Background check and drug screen are required prior to hire.

job.title: Porter
job.description:
The Bexley at Left Bank community in Fort Worth needs a Porter who shows up ready to work and takes real ownership of how the property looks and feels every single day. Weinstein Properties has been family-owned for over 70 years, and that history shapes how they operate: hands-on, relationship-focused, and genuinely invested in the people doing the work.

What You'll Actually Do

A typical morning starts before residents have fully left for work. You're walking the grounds, clearing litter, servicing pet waste stations, and making sure common areas are presentable before the day gets busy. From there, the work shifts depending on what the property needs: trashing out vacant units, running a backpack blower through breezeways, power washing surfaces, light painting, helping prep make-readies alongside the maintenance team, or doing general groundskeeping like weeding and planting. The schedule is Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm, which gives you consistent hours without the on-call unpredictability that comes with a maintenance technician role.

Some of the tasks repeat daily. That's not a flaw in the job description; it's just honest. Pet waste pickup and trash walks happen every day because the property has to look good every day. The people who thrive here don't resent the repetition. They find a rhythm in it and use the independence the role gives them to stay ahead of problems rather than react to them.

The physical demands are real. You'll be on your feet outdoors all day, lifting up to 50 pounds or more, operating a golf cart and trailer, and working through Texas heat, cold snaps, and humidity alike. That context matters before you apply.

What You Bring

  • Reliability and punctuality. The maintenance and leasing teams count on you to set the tone for the property each morning.
  • A self-starting approach. There's no one standing over your shoulder with a checklist. You see what needs doing and do it.
  • Physical stamina for sustained outdoor work year-round
  • Willingness to handle tasks that aren't glamorous, including pet waste, unit cleanouts, and dirty surfaces
  • A collaborative attitude. You'll work alongside maintenance techs and interact with leasing staff. How you carry yourself with residents and teammates matters.
  • Comfort operating basic equipment like blowers and power washers (or the ability to learn quickly)

Compensation and Growth

Starting pay is $16.50 per hour, with competitive hourly rates and quarterly bonuses. There's also a $1,000 stay-on bonus available after 90 days in good standing. The recruiter can walk you through the specifics.

Worth noting on the growth side: the Porter role at Weinstein Properties is a legitimate entry point into a maintenance career. Team members who bring a good attitude and a willingness to learn have moved into maintenance technician positions. If that's a direction you want to go, this company supports it. If you just want to do solid, consistent work and be fairly compensated for it, that's valued here too.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
It's a Saturday morning in August, and move-in day at The Thompson is organized chaos. You're handing out keys, tracking down packages, fielding texts from parents, and somehow still smiling. That's the job, and it matters more than the title suggests.

The Role at The Thompson

The Scion Group operates student housing communities across the country, and The Thompson in San Marcos, Texas sits in a market shaped by Texas State University. This leasing consultant position, which Scion internally calls an Experience Team Member, covers more ground than a standard leasing role. You're part of the sales team, part of the marketing effort, and part of property operations all at once.

Day to day, that means touring prospective residents, handling objections, and feeding feedback on sales barriers back to the management team. It also means helping plan and run resident engagement events, supporting social media content, and keeping the office and amenity spaces in presentable shape. Package logging and maintenance request follow-up fall to this role too. The list of responsibilities is genuinely wide.

The after-hours piece is real. You'll rotate through on-call shifts, which includes lockout calls. That's a known part of working student housing, and it's worth saying plainly before you apply.

What You'll Need

  • Strong communication skills across a diverse resident and family population
  • Comfort working in an environment where priorities shift quickly, especially around turn season and move-in
  • Availability during summers, holidays, and turn periods when traffic peaks
  • Reliability and self-discipline in a role that involves both independent tasks and team coordination
  • A customer-first approach, not just during tours but in every interaction on-site

Scion is not looking for someone who needs the work structured for them at every step. The role rewards people who can read a situation, adjust, and stay composed when the leasing office gets loud. Prior experience in student housing or property management helps, but the requirements here center more on attitude and availability than a specific resume line.

One thing worth knowing: this role is a genuine entry point into property management. Leasing consultants who learn turn operations, build a track record in sales, and get comfortable with the administrative side of a property tend to move into assistant manager positions relatively quickly in student housing. The experience translates well to conventional multifamily too, since the core skills, occupancy management, resident relations, and basic operations, carry across asset types.

This is a full-time, non-exempt position based on-site at The Thompson in San Marcos. Scion requires current U.S. work authorization and does not offer visa sponsorship.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
Skills This Role Runs On

The Community Manager position at Hawthorne Residential Partners in Kannapolis draws on three skill sets more than any others: financial literacy, team coaching, and leasing judgment. You'll read monthly reports, track delinquency, manage deposit accounting, and make budget decisions. You'll also hire, develop, and hold accountable a mixed office and maintenance team. And when occupancy softens, you'll be in the leasing process yourself, conducting tours, following up on leads, and pushing renewals alongside your team.

This is a full-scope role at Hawthorne at Concord Lake. There's no siloing between the business side and the people side. You own both.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Day to day, you're splitting time between the desk and the property. Morning might mean reviewing Yardi reports, following up on outstanding balances, or checking in with maintenance on work order status and vendor schedules. Afternoons can shift to walking the property for curb appeal, handling an escalated resident situation, or jumping on a leasing tour when traffic is high. Saturdays are part of the schedule (10 AM to 4 PM), and resident events occasionally push into evenings.

  • Budget management, rent collection, and financial reporting
  • Delinquency tracking and deposit accounting
  • Leasing, renewals, and pricing strategy to meet occupancy targets
  • Team hiring, training, and weekly performance alignment
  • Vendor oversight and maintenance coordination
  • Resident communication, conflict resolution, and online reputation management
  • Social media content tied to community events and resident engagement

Yardi and Knock are the primary platforms. Comfort with both puts you ahead on day one.

What Separates Strong Candidates

The posted requirement is two years of property management experience that includes time as both a leasing consultant and assistant community manager. Six months of direct community manager experience is strongly preferred. That path matters here because the role asks you to read a financial statement and conduct a leasing tour in the same workday, often without much transition time between them.

Candidates who do well in community manager roles tend to be comfortable with accountability on both sides: holding the team to standards while staying accessible enough that people actually bring problems to them early. The ones who struggle usually lean too far one direction. A CAM, CAPS, or real estate license strengthens your application but isn't required.

Hawthorne's internal career path program points community managers toward regional manager roles, which makes this position a reasonable next step if you're already in multifamily and looking to grow toward a portfolio-level seat. The company operates across the Southeast and ranks among the 50 largest multifamily management companies nationally, so the infrastructure for career movement is genuine.

job.title: Maintenance Service Technician
job.description:
It's 6:47 a.m. and a resident calls about a water heater that died overnight. By 8:00, you've diagnosed it, pulled the part, and the unit has hot water again before the resident leaves for work. That's the job at Lakeside Village Apartments in Clinton Township.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Paragon Properties is hiring a full-time Maintenance Service Technician for Lakeside Village. The role covers the full range of day-to-day maintenance: handling resident service requests, completing make-readies on vacant units, and keeping the property's curb appeal and physical condition where it needs to be. You'll do basic drywall patching, painting, and rough carpentry as part of unit turns, and you'll troubleshoot and repair plumbing, electrical, major appliances, pool and spa equipment, and HVAC systems.

This position includes after-hours on-call rotation, including weekends and holidays. That's the part some people underestimate when they apply. The call volume and timing are unpredictable, and the expectation is that you show up and solve the problem. Paragon does pay an on-call bonus for after-hours coverage, and there's a quarterly team bonus on top of base pay, which runs up to $26 per hour depending on experience and certifications.

HVAC certification (Type II or Universal) is strongly preferred. If you don't have it yet, the company offers a training and certification program. A valid driver's license, reliable transportation, and a high school diploma are required. Trade school or college-level technical training is a plus. Pre-employment background check, drug screening, and a physical are required before you start.

Who Fits This Role

  • At least one year of hands-on maintenance experience, whether from a technical program, vocational training, or direct on-the-job work
  • Comfortable working outdoors in all seasons, Michigan winters included
  • Solid understanding of safety procedures across trades
  • Customer-facing mindset: residents interact with you directly, and how you handle those interactions matters as much as how you handle the wrench
  • Consistent, dependable attendance. The property doesn't run itself when someone doesn't show up

The benefit package includes paid time off, nine company-paid holidays, a rent discount, 401(k) with employer contribution, and medical, dental, and vision insurance with a short enrollment waiting period. Company-paid life and disability insurance are included. You'll also receive a tool kit after completing the initial 30-day training period and a company uniform.

Strong technicians who build their HVAC knowledge and demonstrate reliability here tend to move into lead tech or maintenance supervisor roles over time. The hands-on breadth of a role like this, covering everything from appliance repair to pool equipment to electrical troubleshooting, builds a foundation that carries across any multifamily property.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Pittsboro sits in Chatham County, one of the fastest-growing corridors in the Triangle region. The residential development pressure there has been significant over the past several years, and communities like Sanctuary at Powell Place are positioned squarely in that growth wave. Keeping a property well-maintained in that environment matters more than it might in a slower market: resident expectations are high, competition from new product is real, and curb appeal directly affects occupancy and renewals.

Van Metre, a company with roots going back to 1955 and a portfolio spanning residential and commercial assets, is hiring a Maintenance Technician for this Pittsboro community. The role reports to both a Property Manager and a Service Manager, so you'll have clear direction on priorities from day to day.

What the Work Looks Like

The core of this position is hands-on property upkeep: completing resident service requests, turning vacant units, walking the grounds for curb appeal and safety issues, and supporting the Service Manager with preventative maintenance scheduling. Turns get particular attention here. A tight make-ready process on vacant units directly affects how quickly the property can lease, and someone who can move through a punch list efficiently and accurately adds real value to the team.

You'll also handle janitorial services, exterior building upkeep, inventory management for maintenance supplies, and record-keeping for completed work. After-hours emergency coverage is part of the role, and weekend availability is expected.

Qualifications

  • One to two years of hands-on maintenance experience, or documented trade training in a relevant area
  • Working knowledge of appliance, electrical, and plumbing repair
  • Basic HVAC and electrical circuitry familiarity (Universal CFC Certification preferred)
  • Current awareness of OSHA and applicable building and safety standards
  • Valid driver's license required
  • Own basic hand tools and the knowledge to use them safely

The compensation range is $23 to $25 per hour depending on experience, plus an annual bonus of up to $5,000 paid quarterly, and renewal and survey commissions. Van Metre's benefits package includes medical, dental, and vision coverage, a company-matched 401(k), generous paid time off (including holidays, sick days, personal days, and your birthday), tuition reimbursement, company-paid certifications, and an annual wellness reimbursement of up to $900.

One thing worth noting for candidates coming from larger metro markets: technicians who've worked high-volume Class A communities in Raleigh or Durham sometimes overlook suburban lease-up properties in the Chatham County area. The workload here can be just as demanding, and the experience translates well. Strong candidates will be comfortable owning their service request queue with minimal supervision and communicating proactively with management about safety and preventative maintenance needs before those issues become larger problems.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
The Role at a Glance

Maintenance Technicians at apartment communities handle a wide mix of work: service requests, make-readies, preventive maintenance, and the occasional after-hours call. At Waypoint Management Services in Palm Bay, this role sits at a high-end luxury community, so the expectation for quality and presentation is higher than at a typical garden-style complex.

What You'll Handle Day-to-Day

You're responsible for the overall upkeep of the property and its residents' day-to-day maintenance needs. That includes diagnosing and repairing plumbing issues, HVAC units, appliances, and general building systems. Preventive maintenance on HVAC and community equipment happens on a regular schedule. Priority work orders get resolved within 24 hours.

Make-ready prep is a core part of the job. You'll confirm units are rent-ready and coordinate with contractors on punch list items as needed. Beyond units, you'll maintain pool chemistry, service the trash compactor, check that gates and security equipment are functioning, and handle light grounds and carpentry work. OSHA compliance isn't optional here; you're expected to know the standards and operate within them.

On-call availability is part of the schedule. Residents at luxury properties tend to expect faster response and a higher standard of finish, so attention to detail matters more than it might elsewhere.

What Waypoint Is Looking For

  • EPA Section 608 certification, Types I and II (required)
  • CPO certification (a plus)
  • Hands-on experience with building systems, plumbing, and general repairs
  • Familiarity with service supplies, materials, and equipment
  • Working knowledge of OSHA standards
  • High school diploma or equivalent, with relevant trade experience or training
  • Strong service orientation and a professional, resident-facing attitude

Technicians who do well in luxury settings combine solid technical skills with strong communication. Residents notice when someone shows up on time, explains what they're doing, and leaves the unit clean. That combination, reliable work plus a professional presence, tends to separate strong candidates from average ones in this type of community.

Waypoint offers medical, dental, and vision coverage starting day one, 401k with matching, an onsite housing discount, and bonus opportunities. The company is in a growth phase, which typically means more communities coming online and room to move up.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
Lease-up maintenance is a different job than steady-state property maintenance, and the distinction matters. At a stabilizing property, you're managing systems that have already been tested by residents. At a brand-new community like Dream St. Augustine, you're setting the baseline. Every punch list item, every first service request, every vendor relationship gets established on your watch. That's the context for this Maintenance Supervisor role.

What the Job Actually Involves

Dream St. Augustine is a new construction community in St. Augustine, FL, and the Maintenance Supervisor hired here will build the maintenance operation from the ground up. That means establishing preventative maintenance schedules, standing up the maintenance shop, vetting vendors, and training a team before the property reaches stabilization. Day-to-day, you'll handle HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and pool systems yourself when needed, while also directing your crew on service request completion within 24-hour windows and vacancy turns on a 5-day cycle. The administrative side is real too: budget tracking, purchasing through AppFolio, security deposit dispositions, and detailed maintenance records all sit in this role.

Core responsibilities include:

  • Leading and scheduling the maintenance team, including on-call rotation
  • Performing and overseeing make-readies, targeting 5-day turns on vacant units
  • Troubleshooting and repairing HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and general building systems
  • Coordinating landscaping and vendor services, managing contracts and supply costs
  • Maintaining the OpEx maintenance budget and identifying cost-saving opportunities
  • Keeping common areas, grounds, and amenities in top condition from the initial lease-up phase forward
  • Mentoring technicians and setting service standards for the team

The schedule requires flexibility, including weekend availability and on-call rotation. You'll need a valid driver's license, a clean driving record, a reliable vehicle, your own basic tools, and the physical capacity to lift 50-plus pounds and cover multiple floors on foot throughout the day.

What Strong Candidates Bring

HVAC certification is strongly preferred, and hands-on HVAC management experience is the core technical credential this role is built around. Lease-up experience is a real differentiator here. Candidates who have opened a new property before understand the difference between a system failure at month 18 and one at month 2 of occupancy. First impressions during lease-up shape resident retention, and maintenance quality is a direct driver of both renewal rates and online reputation.

Beyond technical skill, the candidates who tend to excel in this kind of role are those who can shift between managing people and picking up tools themselves, sometimes within the same hour. If your instinct is to lead from the front rather than delegate everything downward, this structure fits that style well.

Company and Growth Context

Dream Live Prosper Communities operates as a subsidiary of DLP Capital, which has appeared on the Inc. 5000 list of fastest-growing private companies for 14 consecutive years. The company focuses on attainable housing and has stated goals around community impact at scale. For a Maintenance Supervisor, that organizational backing typically means access to systems and resources that smaller operators can't match, alongside the accountability that comes with a performance-driven culture. Monthly and quarterly bonus potential is tied to performance. This role positions well for anyone targeting a Regional Maintenance Director or Director of Facilities path as the portfolio grows.

job.title: Assistant Manager - Olympus Auburn Lakes
job.description:
Olympus Property has earned recognition as a National Apartment Association Top Employer three consecutive years, and the team at Auburn Lakes in Spring, TX reflects that. The culture here centers on genuine care rather than a polished mission statement. If you've spent time onsite at an apartment community and you understand that residents aren't just customers but neighbors, this is a place where that instinct gets put to real use.

The Assistant Manager role here is operational at its core. You're the person who keeps the money moving accurately, the files clean, and the leasing team supported. Rent collection, deposits made before bank close, final account statements after move-outs, make-ready inspections before a resident picks up keys. These aren't glamorous tasks, but they're the foundation a well-run community depends on. When the Property Manager is out, you step into that seat without missing a beat.

Residents will stop by with questions, complaints, and the occasional crisis. Your comfort with those in-person moments matters as much as your ability to manage collections and keep records. You'll also carry some leasing responsibilities when the team needs it, show apartments, and participate in retention events. Keeping an eye on what's happening in the Spring submarket, new construction, hiring trends nearby, business changes, factors that could affect occupancy, is part of how you add value beyond the front desk.

RealPage, Knock, or Onesite experience will help you get up to speed quickly. The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, with flexibility expected for resident events and for covering the first weekend of each month.

One honest note on what separates strong candidates from average ones in this role: it's the combination of financial discipline and people instincts. A lot of leasing professionals have the resident-facing warmth but struggle with the accounting rigor. A lot of administrators have the systems fluency but go stiff in a lobby conversation. The Assistant Manager position at a community like this demands both in the same person, often in the same hour.

What Olympus is looking for

  • Prior onsite experience as an Assistant Manager or a cross-trained Leasing Consultant
  • Comfort with property management software, particularly RealPage, Knock, or Onesite
  • A detail-oriented approach to financial records, rent collection, and resident file management
  • Genuine ease in direct resident conversations and the ability to handle complaints with composure
  • Availability Monday through Friday with flexibility for monthly weekend coverage and resident events

Pay starts between $22 and $23 per hour depending on experience, with monthly renewal incentives and quarterly bonuses available. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) with employer matching, educational assistance, pet insurance, an apartment rental allowance, and a sabbatical program, among others.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor- Russellville Commons
job.description:
Maintenance supervisors in multifamily carry more operational weight than the job title suggests. At a property with meaningful unit count, they're the difference between a well-run community and one that bleeds NOI through deferred repairs, slow turns, and resident frustration. MG Properties, a Western U.S. operator with three decades of acquisition, rehab, and management experience, is staffing this role at Russellville Commons in Portland.

What the Role Actually Covers

This is a full-scope maintenance leadership position. You'll diagnose and perform hands-on repairs, but the job is equally about running the team: scheduling staff, delegating work orders, inspecting completed jobs, and making sure the preventive maintenance calendar doesn't slip. Resident service requests need a system behind them, not just a person. You'll own that system. Safety meetings are a scheduled responsibility here, not an afterthought, and you'll keep accurate records on PM work and expenditures. When outside vendors or contractors come in, you coordinate that too.

Portland's housing stock trends older in many corridors, and properties like Russellville Commons can carry HVAC, plumbing, and electrical systems that require real trade fluency, not specialists for every call. MG's expectation is that you bring working knowledge across all trades. That breadth lets the property avoid unnecessary vendor costs while keeping turns and make-readies on schedule.

What MG Properties Is Looking For

  • At least 2 years in a maintenance supervisor role (preferred)
  • Direct experience at a community of 150 units or more
  • Demonstrated competency across multiple trades (electrical, plumbing, HVAC, appliances)
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • Strong customer service instincts and a collaborative approach to working with site staff and the property manager

The candidates who do well in this kind of role typically combine technical range with organizational discipline. Knowing how to fix things gets you in the door. Knowing how to prioritize a queue of 30 open work orders, keep your team accountable, and communicate clearly with residents and management is what makes you effective at scale. If your background is mostly hands-on tech work with limited team oversight, this role will ask more of you on the leadership side than you may be used to.

Compensation includes monthly bonuses, company profit sharing, and a 401(k) with employer match. MG also offers medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid holidays, sick time, and a rental discount benefit.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager (Station Center I, Station Center II)
job.description:
Affordable housing operations carry a layer of compliance complexity that most market-rate properties never encounter. At MidPen Housing's Station Center I and Station Center II in Union City, the Assistant Community Manager role exists at exactly that intersection: day-to-day property administration plus the regulatory work that keeps affordable units funded and legally occupied.

MidPen has operated in Northern California since 1970 and manages more than 142 properties across 12 counties. These aren't market-rate communities with concessions and lease-up pressure. They serve working families, seniors, and residents with special needs, and keeping those homes stable requires precision in income verification, recertification, and Tax Credit Allocation Committee (TCAC) compliance. Experience with that regulatory layer will separate strong candidates from those who need significant ramp-up time.

What This Role Covers Day to Day

The Assistant Community Manager reports to the Community Manager and carries a wide operational scope. On the leasing and compliance side, you'll schedule income verification appointments, process lease agreements, manage the waitlist, assist with recertifications, and support Management and Occupancy Review (MOR) and TCAC reviews. On the financial side, you'll assist with rent collection, security deposits, petty cash logs, and bank deposit preparation. Turns are part of the work too: you'll schedule vacancies, prepare and monitor turnover forms, and coordinate with facilities staff to keep work orders moving on a reasonable timeline.

Resident relations here go beyond the typical leasing conversation. You'll communicate emergency preparedness procedures, coordinate logistics for resident meetings, and help maintain working relationships with local law enforcement and emergency agencies. Property inspections for maintenance and security issues are also part of your regular rhythm.

  • Proficiency in MS Office; RealPage experience is a plus
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • High School diploma or GED with at least one year of residential property management, customer service, or administrative experience (or equivalent combination)
  • Organized, detail-oriented, and able to work independently with minimal supervision
  • Genuine alignment with MidPen's mission serving diverse, income-qualified residents

Context Worth Knowing

Union City sits in the eastern Alameda County corridor where affordable housing demand consistently outpaces supply. MidPen properties in this area carry waitlists that reflect that pressure, which means waitlist management and recertification accuracy aren't administrative formalities. They're how the community maintains compliance with funding sources and keeps deserving residents housed.

For candidates building a career in affordable housing property management, this role develops skills that transfer directly into Community Manager positions: LIHTC compliance knowledge, HUD review preparation, and resident services coordination. Those are qualifications that carry real weight with mission-driven housing organizations up and down the Bay Area. The pay range is $21.15 to $23.80 per hour, based on experience.

job.title: Leasing Consultant (Montrose)
job.description:
Leasing roles at apartment communities in the Bay Area carry real weight. Mountain View's rental market stays competitive year-round, and the person on the front line of touring, qualifying, and closing future residents directly affects occupancy and NOI. This is that front-line role.

What the Job Actually Involves

Prometheus calls this position a Regional Neighbor Ambassador, which reflects something real about the scope. You're not just running tours and collecting applications. On any given day you might be conducting a market survey in the morning, preparing rental agreements at midday, posting updated availability, and then pivoting back to a walk-in prospect who has questions about move-in timelines. The mix of sales, customer service, and administrative work is genuine.

Weekends are a required part of the schedule. Traffic peaks on Saturdays and Sundays, so that's when the community needs coverage. Your regular days off will fall during the week. That trade-off is worth understanding before you apply.

Pay starts at $25.00 to $26.25 per hour, with a $200 incentive per signed lease on top of base. There's also a discretionary semi-annual bonus, weekend shift premium pay, and additional bonuses tied to referrals, lease-up performance, and training. Benefits include 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and eligible dependents.

Who Fits This Role

Prometheus explicitly hires across industries. A background in retail, hospitality, or any customer-facing sales environment translates well here. Prior property management experience isn't required.

Strong candidates in leasing roles like this one tend to share a few traits worth calling out:

  • They move between tasks without losing momentum. Leasing offices don't queue work neatly.
  • They follow up. A prospect who tours on Saturday and doesn't hear back by Monday afternoon is likely already looking elsewhere.
  • They can read what a prospect actually needs and adjust their approach, rather than running the same script on everyone.
  • They handle administrative details accurately. Errors in rental agreements or lease files create downstream problems for the whole team.

This role sits at the entry point of a property management career path that can move toward assistant manager, property manager, and eventually regional or portfolio-level positions. The administrative and sales exposure you get here builds a foundation that transfers directly into those steps.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Leasing is a skills-heavy position that most people underestimate. The ones who do it well combine genuine sales instincts with something closer to hospitality, and they run that combination all day, every interaction, every tour. At Evergreen at the Bluffs in Knoxville, Hawthorne Residential Partners is hiring a Leasing Consultant to be exactly that kind of person on the front line of a community they clearly take seriously.

The Skills This Role Runs On

Traffic conversion is the core job. You're greeting prospects, conducting tours personalized to what each person actually cares about, and following up until the lease is signed. That requires reading people quickly, handling objections without getting rattled, and staying organized across phone calls, emails, and web leads simultaneously. Accuracy matters too: applications, verifications, and move-in paperwork need to be done right the first time. Errors at the front end of a tenancy tend to echo.

Resident relations is the other half. You'll coordinate and attend community events, respond to resident questions with some actual patience, and help keep common areas and the leasing office presentable. Community feel is a retention tool. Renewals don't happen in a vacuum.

Schedule and Practical Realities

The leasing office runs Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, and Saturdays from 10 AM to 4 PM. You'll get one weekday off each week to keep the schedule at 40 hours. Resident events and occasional community needs may push into evenings. That's standard for leasing roles and worth knowing upfront.

Hawthorne is a top-50 multifamily operator with deep Southeast roots. They run a formal Career Path Program with in-house learning and development, which matters if you're thinking about the next step. The leasing-to-assistant-manager pipeline is one of the most natural progressions in our industry, and companies that actually invest in it make a real difference in how fast that move happens.

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

Hawthorne lists the traits they're looking for, and the honest translation is this: the candidates who thrive in leasing roles aren't necessarily the ones with the most apartment experience. One year of customer service or sales is preferred but not required. What actually separates good leasing consultants from average ones is coachability and consistency. Showing up with the same energy on a slow Tuesday as a busy Saturday. Following up when it's inconvenient. Learning the local comp set well enough to speak to it intelligently on a tour.

  • High school diploma or GED required
  • One year of customer service, sales, or leasing experience preferred (not required)
  • Valid driver's license required
  • CALP certification is a plus

Commission eligibility on leasing and renewals is part of the compensation structure, alongside an hourly base rate. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, 401k match, paid time off, pet insurance, and paid parental leave options.

job.title: Service Manager
job.description:
It's 7 a.m. on a Monday and you've got two service requests from the weekend sitting in the queue, a unit turning this week, and a contractor showing up at nine to work on building exteriors. That's a normal morning at West Pointe Apartments, and this role is built for someone who can triage all of it without losing composure.

The Work

West Pointe is a 100-unit residential community in Burlington, NC, currently being built out under Van Metre's portfolio. As Service Manager, you'll oversee one Maintenance Technician and report to both the Property Manager and the Director of Facilities. The scope is hands-on and operational. You're managing daily service requests, coordinating the make-ready process for vacant units, scheduling vendors, meeting with contractors, and keeping the preventative maintenance program on track. HVAC maintenance, repair, and replacement fall squarely in your lap, as does carrying the 24-hour emergency maintenance schedule. That last part is real: after-hours calls happen, and this position requires someone who's comfortable with that reality.

Beyond the day-to-day, you'll manage the facility side of the budget, submit weekly reports to the corporate office, and stay current on OSHA standards and any state or federal compliance programs the property is subject to. Work also includes hands-on repairs across electrical, plumbing, carpentry, appliance repair, and painting, so this is a working supervisor role, not a desk job with a title.

What You Bring

  • At least 3 years of maintenance experience, or equivalent formal training
  • EPA Certification (required)
  • CPO Certification (required)
  • Prior supervisory experience (preferred)
  • Working knowledge of HVAC systems and electrical circuitry
  • Solid skills in appliance, electrical, and plumbing repair
  • Current knowledge of OSHA, building codes, and safety standards
  • Your own basic tools and the ability to use them safely
  • Valid driver's license

The interpersonal side of this job matters too. You'll interact with residents, visitors, and contractors regularly, and how you handle a frustrated resident waiting on a repair reflects directly on the property. Professionalism under pressure is part of the job description, not just a line in the posting.

Candidates who tend to do well in roles like this are the ones who take the make-ready process seriously. At a 100-unit property, a slow turn costs money and occupancy. If you've owned that process before, including managing the punch list, coordinating vendors, and keeping the timeline tight, that experience will matter more than anything else you bring to the interview.

Van Metre offers a base salary between $58,240 and $62,400 annually, with up to $5,000 in annual bonus potential paid quarterly. Benefits include 11 paid holidays, vacation, sick leave, personal days, a birthday day off, parental leave, company-matched 401(k), up to $900 in annual wellness reimbursement, and professional development support including tuition reimbursement and company-paid certifications.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is the top site-level role at a Winooski, Vermont property operated by Redstone Residential, a third-party management company running over 38,000 beds across 20 states. Redstone built its name in student housing and has been expanding its conventional multifamily portfolio, so depending on the property, you may be dealing with a resident profile that straddles both worlds. Either way, the Community Manager owns everything: budget, occupancy, delinquency, leasing strategy, renewals, staff performance, and reporting up to the Regional Manager.

Day to day, that means watching KPIs closely, staying ahead of delinquency before it compounds, and making sure your leasing team is executing on traffic conversion rather than just logging showings. You'll manage to an approved operating budget with real P&L ownership. Marketing initiatives, construction coordination, and client-facing reporting are all part of the job. Redstone uses Entrata, so comfort with property management software matters, though they'll work with candidates who are quick to learn.

Vermont's rental market is relatively tight, and Winooski in particular sits adjacent to Burlington and the University of Vermont, which means your resident base likely includes a mix of students, young professionals, and long-term renters. Understanding how to position the property in that market, and how to retain residents who have genuine options, requires more than posting specials and hoping for the best.

What You Bring

  • At least 3 years in student housing or conventional multifamily, with 2 or more years specifically in a property manager seat
  • Demonstrated budget management and P&L ownership, not just familiarity with financials but accountability for them
  • Experience interfacing with clients or ownership groups directly. Redstone is a third-party operator, so client-readiness isn't a soft skill here, it's a job requirement
  • The ability to manage multiple workstreams at once without losing the details
  • Comfort with Google Workspace, Microsoft Office, and property management software (Entrata experience is a plus)
  • Genuine ability to coach and develop on-site staff, not just assign tasks

A Few Things Worth Knowing

Third-party management sharpens certain skills quickly. You're accountable to both ownership and a regional structure, which means your reporting has to be clean and your explanations have to be backed by data. Community Managers who grow in this environment tend to move into Regional Manager roles faster than peers who come from fee-light or in-house-only backgrounds, because third-party work forces you to communicate performance clearly and defend your decisions. The $70,000 base comes with a performance bonus opportunity of up to 20% of salary, which in this industry is a reasonable structure if the property is set up to hit its targets.

This is a full-time, exempt role with health, vision, and dental coverage, 15 days PTO, 10 paid holidays, paid parental leave, and a 401(k) with up to 6% matching. Redstone also offers a continued education program and professional development support, which is worth noting for someone who wants room to grow beyond the site level.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor - Roving - Pine Vista, Vogue Manor, Castilian and Las Palmas
job.description:
Roving maintenance roles exist because multi-family portfolios rarely distribute deferred work, turnover volume, or staffing gaps evenly across sites. Sunrise Management's solution is a Maintenance Supervisor who moves across four San Diego communities , Pine Vista, Vogue Manor, Castilian, and Las Palmas , plugging in where the need is highest on any given week. The role pays $29 to $31 per hour depending on experience.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

The core accountability is keeping four communities physically healthy and market-ready at the same time. Turns are a significant part of that. Sunrise expects make-ready apartments to be painted, cleaned, and punched out within three to five days of vacancy. At multiple sites simultaneously, hitting that window consistently requires real scheduling discipline and the ability to direct a crew without micromanaging every task.

Beyond turns, the day-to-day spans a wide range of trades: HVAC, plumbing, appliance repair, electrical, pool and spa maintenance, carpentry, and custodial work. Preventive maintenance runs on a monthly directive cycle covering lighting, fire safety, life and safety hazards, pool systems, and signage. You'll maintain the logs, track inventory across sites, and flag any capital-level repairs or deferred maintenance to the property manager. Emergency on-call service is part of the job. Service requests carry a 24-hour completion target, and when parts delay a repair, the expectation is proactive communication to both management and the resident , not silence.

Because this is a supervisory position, you'll also coordinate with site management teams on scheduling, assist with hiring and performance reviews for maintenance staff, and run monthly safety meetings. MSDS recordkeeping, PPE compliance, and adherence to Sunrise's hazard materials policies are non-negotiable. Fair Housing awareness applies to maintenance staff just as it does to leasing , you're expected to understand why that matters operationally.

What Separates Strong Candidates

The multi-site structure is where this role gets interesting and where underprepared candidates struggle. You won't have the luxury of owning one property's rhythm and settling in. Priorities shift depending on which site has the highest vacancy, the most urgent work orders, or the thinnest staffing. The strongest candidates here are the ones who can triage quickly, communicate clearly across multiple managers, and maintain consistent standards at each stop.

  • 2 or more years of hands-on property maintenance experience, required
  • Prior supervisory experience, required
  • Valid driver's license, required (travel between sites is a core function)
  • Familiarity with Entrata or AppFolio, preferred
  • Broad trades competency across plumbing, HVAC, electrical, pool systems, and carpentry
  • Comfort working within preventive maintenance programs, PPE requirements, and safety compliance frameworks

Experience with portfolio-wide or roving maintenance work is a genuine differentiator here. Someone who has only ever managed one property's physical plant will find the context-switching demanding at first. Someone who's done it before will recognize the pattern and adapt quickly. Entrata experience in particular helps, since work order tracking and communication across sites runs through the platform.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
It's 10 a.m. on a Saturday and three walk-ins just showed up at the same time. You greet all three, pull up available floor plans, and start working the room. By noon, two of them have submitted applications. That's the job.

The Role

Karya Property Management is hiring a Leasing Consultant for their Dallas portfolio. This is a front-line sales and hospitality position where your output shows up directly in the occupancy number. You'll carry the property's traffic from first contact to signed lease, which means greeting walk-ins, working internet leads, conducting tours, processing applications, and staying on top of follow-up until a lead converts or goes cold. The closing ratio and the vacancy report are your scorecards.

Day-to-day, you'll match prospects to floor plans, process income and credit screenings, prepare lease documents and addenda, and keep guest cards and traffic logs current in the property management system. Before any showing, you'll confirm units are market-ready. You'll walk the property regularly and flag curb appeal or maintenance issues as you go. Move-in orientations, renewal outreach, and lease-expiration follow-up are all part of the cycle.

Beyond direct leasing, the role includes competitor market surveys (pricing, specials, concessions), contributing content for social media and listing sites, supporting outreach to local employers and referral partners, and helping staff resident events. Fair Housing compliance and general office coverage round out the responsibilities.

What Karya Needs From You

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • At least one year in a customer-facing role: leasing, sales, hospitality, retail, or similar
  • Comfortable asking for the sale and following up persistently without crossing into pushy
  • Strong phone, email, and in-person communication
  • Basic computer proficiency; Microsoft Office or Google Workspace
  • Weekend availability and flexibility for evening hours during peak leasing season
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation

Prior multifamily experience, working knowledge of Yardi, Entrata, RealPage, or a comparable platform, and bilingual ability in English and Spanish are all preferred but not required to apply.

The candidates who stand out aren't necessarily the ones with the most leasing experience. They're the ones with tight follow-up habits, a genuine ability to read what a prospect actually needs in a home, and the discipline to treat every guest card as an open task until it's resolved one way or another. Leasing coordinators who come from restaurant or retail backgrounds often bring exactly that instinct, and it translates quickly in this environment.

job.title: Assistant Manager Manufactured Housing Communities
job.description:
Investment Property Group operates 150 properties across 13 states, with a portfolio spanning multifamily, manufactured home communities, and RV parks. This role puts you on the ground at two of their Auburn, Washington communities: Skylark Village Estates 1, a 141-home senior community, and Skylark Village Estates 2, a 116-home all-ages community. Combined, that's 257 homes worth of resident relations, rent collection, delinquency management, and daily ops sitting in your queue.
