  • Strong communicators who can shift tone depending on whether they're texting a prospect, posting on Instagram, or explaining a lease policy to a concerned parent
  • People who stay organized under variable workloads, because quiet weeks and chaotic weeks can follow each other quickly
  • Candidates available for weekend hours and key seasonal periods including turn

Growth and Team Fit

Experience Team Members who develop a feel for both the sales and operational sides of this role often move into assistant manager or leasing manager positions as they build tenure. Student housing is a distinct specialty, and people who understand the academic-calendar-driven leasing cycle carry that knowledge into any future multifamily role. Scion offers learning reimbursement, which signals that internal development is something the company actually invests in rather than just lists on a job posting. This position is full-time, non-exempt, and based on-site at Copper Beech Harrisonburg.

job.title: Leasing Consultant - Lake View
job.description:
A prospect walks into the leasing office at Lake View on a Tuesday afternoon, having already toured two other buildings that morning. What you say, how you show the space, and how quickly you follow up afterward will determine whether Reside Living gets that lease or not. That's the core of this role.

The Work Itself

Reside Living manages roughly 3,000 apartments across Chicago, with this position focused on properties in East Lake View and Gold Coast. Both are high-demand neighborhoods where occupancy expectations are real and traffic needs to convert. You'll handle the full leasing cycle: responding to inquiries by phone, text, and email; scheduling and conducting tours; recording every touchpoint in the CRM; and closing applications in compliance with fair housing law, the Fair Credit Reporting Act, and all applicable state and federal regulations.

Beyond the direct leasing work, you'll physically inspect vacant units and common areas, flag anything that needs attention from maintenance, and help coordinate resident events. You'll also run monthly audits of the property's online presence, looking for gaps in how the building shows up in search, on ILS platforms, and in reviews. Findings go directly to the Property Manager, and Reside Living expects consultants to bring ideas, not just observations.

Daily and weekly reporting is part of the job. You'll track your own numbers closely, because the path to earning commission and quarterly bonuses runs through your ability to hit and hold occupancy targets.

What This Role Requires vs. What It Builds

You need to bring at least one year of leasing or sales experience, strong written and verbal communication, and a working knowledge of Microsoft Office and a property management platform like Yardi. Attention to detail and follow-through aren't optional here: a missed callback or a sloppy CRM entry can cost a lease.

What the role builds is more interesting. Leasing consultants at Reside Living have a stated path into property management and leadership. You'll start developing the NOI awareness and occupancy management instincts that property managers use every day. Strong performers here learn to read their own traffic trends, adjust marketing strategy in real time, and build the kind of resident relationships that reduce turnover. Those skills transfer directly upward.

Candidates who stand out tend to already understand that leasing is a sales role with a service component baked in permanently. The follow-up after the tour matters as much as the tour itself. The best consultants treat every prospect touchpoint as part of a longer conversion process, not a one-time pitch.

  • High school diploma or GED required
  • Minimum one year of leasing or sales experience
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite
  • Experience with Yardi or comparable CRM platform preferred
  • Personal smartphone required (iPhone or Android); $50/month stipend provided

Compensation includes a base salary plus commission and quarterly bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and life insurance, paid time off, 401(k) matching, a commuter benefit, a 25% monthly apartment discount, and $100 per month in student loan assistance.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor at Antero Apartments
job.description:
A Maintenance Supervisor role at a residential apartment community carries real weight. You're responsible for the physical condition of the asset, the experience of every resident who submits a work order, and the development of the technicians who work alongside you. At Antero Apartments in Colorado Springs, Cottonwood Residential is looking for someone who can hold all three of those responsibilities at once without letting any of them slip.

The Work Itself

The technical foundation here is non-negotiable. You'll troubleshoot and resolve HVAC, electrical, plumbing, and appliance issues, and you'll need EPA Type II or Universal certification coming in. CPO certification is a plus. A valid driver's license is required. What you'll build on top of that foundation is systems thinking: managing the make-ready and turn process so units move through the punch list quickly, keeping occupancy gaps tight and new residents moving in on schedule. You'll also oversee grounds maintenance, general upkeep, and ensure the property stays compliant with applicable building and safety codes. Emergency coverage doesn't stop at 5pm, and you'll be the one setting the staffing schedule that ensures 24/7 response capacity.

On the people side, you'll hire, train, and develop your maintenance techs and community care associates. That means formal classroom instruction and hands-on coaching, not just assigning work orders and walking away. The standard you set for response time, attention to detail, and resident communication becomes the team's standard.

What You Bring vs. What You'll Build

The skills this role requires on day one include:

  • Considerable HVAC troubleshooting experience
  • EPA Type II or Universal certification
  • Working knowledge of electrical, plumbing, and appliance systems
  • Experience managing a make-ready or turn process
  • Ability to lead a team and hold performance standards

What the role develops is harder to list but worth naming. Running a team that handles emergency calls, coordinates turns, and keeps a community clean and code-compliant sharpens your operational judgment in ways that transfer directly to multi-site maintenance roles or regional facilities management. Supervisors who demonstrate strong unit economics in their turn cycle, specifically low vacancy days and controlled make-ready costs, tend to move into those broader roles faster than those who stay purely technical.

The Company Context

Cottonwood Residential positions itself around the resident experience, and that shows up in how they approach maintenance. Timely service ticket follow-up and genuine care for how residents feel about their home are treated as part of the job, not extras. They've also invested in technology like Self-Guided Tours, which signals an organization open to operational change. Compensation includes competitive pay, a bonus structure, full health benefits available within the first 30 days, 401k and HSA company match, three weeks of PTO in the first year, and 10.5 paid holidays.

If you take pride in the physical quality of a community and know how to build that pride in the people who work with you, this role has real room to grow.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
What This Role Actually Demands

This position runs on two core skill sets: trade expertise and operational discipline. You need real plumbing knowledge, the kind that keeps repair calls from turning into vendor invoices. And you need to manage work orders, budgets, schedules, and people with the same attention you'd bring to a tough repair. Birgo operates a paperless maintenance operation across nine multifamily properties in the Buffalo area, so comfort with mobile apps and digital workflows isn't optional. AppFolio is the platform. You'll live in it daily.

The territory covers Tonawanda, Buffalo, and Hamburg. That means you're moving between sites, not anchored to one building. Multi-site experience matters here because the coordination load is real: turns across multiple properties, vendor scheduling, contractor oversight, and an on-call rotation all happen simultaneously. The schedule is Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM, with on-call coverage shared across the team.

Day-to-Day Responsibilities

  • Lead apartment turnovers and make-readies across all nine properties, including punch list completion and quality checks
  • Complete high-skilled trade work, particularly plumbing, but also electrical, HVAC, drywall, and general repairs, to reduce outside vendor costs
  • Manage and develop a two-person maintenance tech team: hiring, training, performance, conflict resolution
  • Process work orders and maintain records through AppFolio on a mobile device
  • Track expenses, control costs, and report against budget
  • Source and coordinate vendors and contractors when outside help is required
  • Support preventative maintenance programs and capital improvement projects as needed
  • Set and enforce safety standards for the team
  • Serve as the operational link between property management and the maintenance crew

What Separates Strong Candidates Here

Five or more years in multifamily maintenance and three or more years supervising are the baselines. What pushes a candidate from qualified to exceptional in this role is the combination of hands-on trade skill and administrative follow-through. A lot of experienced technicians don't want to manage paperwork. A lot of supervisors have drifted away from the tools. Birgo needs both in one person, and they're paying $32 to $34 per hour to find it.

The technology fluency piece is worth taking seriously. Birgo runs a fully paperless operation, which keeps the team efficient but requires genuine buy-in. If you've spent years resisting software and prefer paper work orders, this environment will be a grind. If you've already worked in a digital-first maintenance operation, you'll get up to speed quickly and spend more time on the work that actually matters.

Birgo offers a profit-sharing program, mileage and boots reimbursement, professional development support, and a full benefits package including medical, dental, vision, and a 401(k) with employer match. The company manages its own properties rather than operating as a third-party firm, which tends to mean more operational consistency and clearer accountability at the site level.

job.title: FT Exterior Porter (Mon-Fri, 3PM-10PM)
job.description:
Exterior porter work at a mixed-use property like Comstock's Reston portfolio is a skilled trade in its own right. This full-time position with ParkX runs Monday through Friday, 3PM to 10PM, which means you're covering the busiest part of the day for foot traffic, tenant movement, and common area wear. The hours demand someone who can assess what needs attention quickly and prioritize without being told twice.

Skills This Role Uses Every Day

The core of this position is sensory and physical: you read a space and know when it falls short of standard before anyone else notices. Pressure washing, window cleaning, trash removal, and routine janitorial tasks are the daily foundation. You'll also support event setup and breakdown when the schedule calls for it, which requires flexibility and an ability to shift from a steady cleaning rhythm to short-burst, deadline-driven work.

Chemical handling, equipment maintenance, and supply inventory management are real responsibilities here. Knowing how to use cleaning agents safely, keep a janitorial closet orderly, and flag equipment issues before they become failures is part of the craft. End-of-shift documentation and handoff procedures mean your work doesn't disappear when you clock out; it gets recorded and transferred properly.

Customer interaction matters more in this role than people expect. You're visible to tenants, guests, and property staff throughout your shift. A professional demeanor, a courteous acknowledgment of the people around you, and the ability to respond to cleanliness concerns without being prompted are all things the team will notice and rely on.

Skills This Role Builds

Porters who pay attention here develop a strong operational eye. You'll start to recognize patterns: which areas generate the most foot traffic, which surfaces need more frequent attention, and how event activity changes the maintenance load. That kind of pattern recognition is directly transferable to facilities coordination, operations support, and maintenance roles within property management.

Working within a structured reporting chain, communicating hazards to management, and following standardized checklists are habits that translate well into any service-side property role. If your goal is to grow into a lead porter, facilities coordinator, or operations manager position, the documentation and communication habits you form here are the foundation.

What Comstock Offers and What They Expect

Comstock brings a portfolio scope that gives this role real variety. The ParkX operation covers multiple sites in the Reston area, so familiarity with different property types and common area configurations is part of what you'll gain. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, 401(k) match, life insurance, free parking with EV charging, and an annual professional development fund. The company invests in advancement from within, which matters for anyone treating this as a career entry point rather than a placeholder.

The role requires a valid driver's license, a high school diploma or equivalent, and the physical capacity to lift up to 50 pounds and work in variable outdoor conditions. Availability for occasional weekend and after-hours event coverage is part of the position. The posted compensation is $17.80 per hour.

The candidates who stand out in this kind of role are the ones who don't need a supervisor to identify a problem. They see a sidewalk that needs attention at 4PM and handle it before the complaint comes in. That self-direction, paired with consistent reliability, is what separates a good porter from one who gets promoted.

job.title: Property Manager
job.description:
Onsite property manager roles in Southern California often spread candidates thin across a single large community. This one works differently: you'll oversee three separate properties totaling 87 units in Pasadena, which means daily variety and a real ownership mentality over a small portfolio rather than one building.

What the Day-to-Day Looks Like

Property Management Associates needs someone who can run the full cycle. That means morning walk-throughs across the properties, tracking preventative maintenance items, coordinating with your maintenance staff and outside vendors, and handling unit and property inspections. You'll also carry the leasing side: showing units, running competitive rent analyses, and keeping occupancy where it needs to be. Delinquency follow-up, notices, and the operational paperwork that keeps everything moving are all part of the job.

You'll live on-site in a provided one-bedroom apartment. One weekend day per week is required, and on-call availability comes with the territory. A valid driver's license and auto insurance are required. PMA provides a $300 monthly auto allowance to cover the multi-site driving.

What You Need

  • At least three years of conventional multifamily property management experience
  • Working knowledge of Yardi for property accounting
  • Ability to supervise maintenance staff and schedule vendors
  • Demonstrated leasing skills, including market analysis
  • Strong written and verbal communication; solid command of Microsoft Office
  • Valid driver's license and current auto insurance

Background check, DMV check, and pre-employment physical are required before hire.

Compensation and Benefits

Pay runs $23 to $25 per hour, plus the on-site apartment and auto allowance. Full-time employees receive medical, dental, vision, and life insurance with an employer contribution, a 401(k) with discretionary company match after one year, short- and long-term disability, supplemental plans, and a generous PTO package covering vacation, holidays, and sick time.

One thing worth noting for candidates considering this role: managing three separate addresses rather than one sharpens your operational instincts fast. You'll build skills in portfolio-level thinking, multi-site vendor coordination, and independent decision-making that translate well into regional or area manager positions down the line. PMA has been in business over 30 years and promotes from within, so the growth path is real for someone who performs.

job.title: Regional Manager
job.description:
You're on a call at 8 a.m. reviewing last month's T-12 for a property that missed NOI targets, and by noon you're walking a site with a community manager who needs coaching on leasing follow-up. That's a Regional Manager's day at Asset Living. The role covers the full range, and it moves fast.

What This Role Covers

Asset Living is a third-party management firm, and this Regional Manager position oversees a portfolio of multifamily communities in the Atlanta market. You're the offsite leader accountable for operations, personnel, financial performance, leasing strategy, and compliance across every property in your book.

On the personnel side, you screen, hire, coach, and develop on-site staff. You handle counseling documentation, performance management, and terminations when necessary. You approve timesheets and salary requests, and you work directly with HR and senior leadership when situations escalate.

Financially, you build and own the yearly operating budgets. You track income and expense variances monthly, write evaluations when line items drift off-budget, and flag capex needs before they become emergencies. You also oversee vendor contracts, invoice coding, and deposit reconciliation to keep each property's financials clean at closeout.

Leasing strategy falls to you as well. You develop annual marketing plans, sharpen site-level leasing techniques, and monitor conversion and follow-up across your portfolio. Resident retention programs, including events and outreach, are part of the mix. So is handling escalated resident complaints when on-site staff can't resolve them.

On the administrative and maintenance side, you conduct regular property inspections, monitor service request turnaround, and make sure punch list items get closed. You coordinate emergency response procedures and ensure your teams follow company guidelines when something goes wrong on-site.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • Demonstrated experience managing a multifamily portfolio as a regional or multi-site leader
  • Comfort reading and presenting financial statements, including budget-to-actual variance analysis
  • Experience developing site-level staff, including performance documentation and HR coordination
  • Solid working knowledge of fair housing regulations and risk management practices
  • Ability to manage multiple community managers and keep each site accountable without micromanaging

Because Asset Living operates as a third-party management company, regional managers here often oversee properties with different ownership groups, asset classes, and reporting expectations simultaneously. Candidates who have worked in fee management environments adapt faster than those who've only managed in-house portfolios. That context matters when you're presenting ownership reports and fielding client calls alongside your day-to-day operations work.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Student housing operates on a rhythm that most multifamily professionals never experience. The lease-up timeline compresses into a single academic calendar, traffic spikes in waves tied to housing fairs and move-in weekends, and the resident population turns over almost entirely once a year. If you want to understand leasing fundamentals under real pressure, this is a strong place to start.

What You'll Actually Do

Scion's Experience Team Member role at Redpoint Tuscaloosa sits at the intersection of leasing, marketing, and customer service. Day to day, you're giving property tours, fielding prospect questions, and handling the back-and-forth communication that moves someone from curious to signed. You'll also support social media content, help plan and run resident engagement events, and flag what's working (and what isn't) in terms of sales conversations and objections. On the administrative side, expect package management, office upkeep, maintenance request coordination, and rotating after-hours on-call coverage including lockouts. Turn periods at student properties are dense, fast, and require everyone on the team to show up ready to execute.

What You Bring

  • A genuine comfort with talking to people from different backgrounds, in person and online
  • Reliability and self-discipline, especially during high-volume periods like summer and Turn
  • Flexibility to work evenings, holidays, and rotating on-call shifts as the schedule demands
  • Strong organizational habits that hold up when the office gets busy
  • Eligibility to work in the United States (visa sponsorship is not available)

Where This Role Takes You

The skills you build here transfer directly into roles like leasing manager, assistant community manager, or marketing coordinator at conventional multifamily properties. Student housing teaches you to close under urgency, communicate across a wide demographic, and manage operations during one of the most logistically demanding events in property management: a full community turn. Operators in Class A garden-style and mid-rise communities actively recruit people with student housing backgrounds because of that experience. The ETM position at Scion is a legitimate entry point into a career track, not just a leasing job. Candidates who advance quickly tend to be the ones who treat every resident interaction as a data point, actively report what's slowing down conversions, and take the on-call rotation seriously rather than treating it as an inconvenience.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Hillpointe builds and manages market-rate workforce housing across the Sun Belt, and they do it with an unusually tight vertical structure: land acquisition, construction, procurement, and asset management all run in-house. That means a maintenance technician at one of their communities isn't working for a third-party manager with a slim ops budget. They're working inside an owner-operator that controls its own capital and cares about long-term asset performance.

What the Work Looks Like Day to Day

This role covers the full range of residential maintenance at a garden-style community in Cartersville, GA. You'll run work orders for resident repair requests, perform preventive maintenance on building systems, and turn vacant units through the make-ready process so they're move-in ready on schedule. Grounds upkeep, common area inspections, and supply inventory management round out the routine. Documentation matters here: tracking materials used, logging work orders accurately, and keeping records clean are part of how the property stays operationally sound.

You'll also participate in a rotating on-call schedule, which means evening, weekend, and morning availability come with the position. That's standard at most residential communities, and worth knowing before you apply.

What Hillpointe Is Looking For

  • Hands-on mechanical troubleshooting ability across building systems and common areas
  • Comfort with pre-move-out inspections and punch list work during unit turns
  • EPA Type I and II or Universal certification for refrigerant handling, or willingness to obtain it
  • Experience coordinating with vendors and contractors, including scheduling and materials tracking
  • Valid driver's license for on-site equipment operation
  • High school diploma or GED, plus relevant hands-on experience
  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs regularly, work at heights, and handle tools in varying outdoor conditions
  • Familiarity with OSHA standards and willingness to follow safety protocols consistently

Where This Role Can Go

Technicians who build strong diagnostic skills and learn to manage turns efficiently tend to advance into lead tech or maintenance supervisor roles as their portfolio of properties grows. At a company developing multiple communities across the Sun Belt at once, internal mobility is a realistic path, especially for someone who takes ownership of their unit and communicates well with the property management team. The combination of preventive maintenance discipline and solid vendor coordination is what separates candidates who grow quickly from those who plateau at the technician level.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor at Cottonwood Clermont
job.description:
Maintenance Supervisor roles at apartment communities demand a specific kind of person: someone who can swap a motor, coach a junior tech through their first HVAC call, and still make time to follow up with the resident in 4B who's been waiting on a work order. At Cottonwood Clermont, that full picture is exactly what this position covers.

What the Day Actually Looks Like

Your mornings will likely start with a review of open service tickets and a check-in with your team before the day gets going. From there, the work is genuinely varied. You'll troubleshoot HVAC, electrical, plumbing, and appliance issues yourself when needed, but a big part of your value here is knowing when to step in and when to let a tech work through a problem on their own. The make-ready process will take real attention: units need to be turned on time so leasing can keep pace, and that punch list mentality matters. Grounds, common areas, pool compliance (CPO certification is a plus here), and building systems all fall under your watch too.

You'll own the on-call schedule, making sure 24/7 emergency coverage is covered without burning out your team. Scheduling is one of those quiet leadership tasks that either builds trust or erodes it fast. Getting it right matters.

Who You're Working With

You'll interact daily with residents who just want things fixed promptly and communicated clearly. That follow-through on service tickets isn't just a performance metric. It's a real piece of how residents decide whether they want to renew. You'll also coordinate with vendors, work alongside the property management team, and take the lead on developing your technicians through both hands-on training and any available classroom education opportunities. Cottonwood supports that development, which means you're expected to take it seriously.

The people dynamics here are real. Not every tech will come in at the same skill level. Some days, you're a plumber; some days, you're a coach; some days, you're the person who has to have a hard conversation about standards. All of that is part of the job.

What the Role Requires

  • EPA Type II or Universal certification (required)
  • Substantial hands-on HVAC troubleshooting experience
  • Valid Driver's License
  • CPO certification (preferred)
  • Experience leading or mentoring a maintenance team
  • Comfort working within building, county, and safety codes

Candidates who tend to stand out in roles like this aren't just technically sharp. They document well, communicate with residents in a way that feels human rather than transactional, and bring a consistency to how they run the team that doesn't depend on who's watching. If you've supervised a maintenance team at a garden-style or mid-rise community before, that experience translates directly here.

Cottonwood Residential has positioned itself as an operator that invests in both tech and people, including early adoption of self-guided tour tools that put more of the leasing process in the resident's hands. That broader mindset tends to carry into how they support maintenance operations too. For a supervisor who wants room to develop a team and build real systems around preventive maintenance and turn efficiency, that context is worth noting.

job.title: Paint & resurface tech
job.description:
The make-ready cycle is where resident impressions get set, and a sloppy paint job or a bubbling countertop resurface will undermine everything else the team did right on that turn. Karya Property Management is building out the maintenance side of their residential portfolio in Phoenix and adding a dedicated Paint and Resurface Technician to keep that work consistent and in-house.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Most of your time will split between unit turns and ongoing property upkeep. On a turn, you're prepping surfaces, patching holes and cracks, sanding, priming, and laying down finish coats on interior walls and trim. You'll also handle countertop and cabinet resurfacing, which is the kind of work that significantly changes how a unit photographs and how it feels to a prospective resident walking in. Exterior surfaces come into the rotation too, so you're not confined to unit interiors.

Beyond the turn work, you'll coordinate with the broader maintenance and property management teams to schedule jobs and move efficiently across properties. That scheduling piece matters more than it sounds. A tech who can sequence prep, cure times, and resurfacing work without holding up a unit goes-live date is genuinely valuable. Phoenix heat affects dry times and material behavior, so knowing how to adjust application technique in high temperatures is a real skill here.

What Karya Is Looking For

  • Prior experience in painting and surface resurfacing, residential preferred
  • Familiarity with different finishes, application techniques, and appropriate materials for various surfaces
  • Detail orientation and consistent workmanship quality
  • Ability to manage your own schedule and work independently across sites
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • Clear communication with maintenance coordinators and property teams

Karya offers health and wellness benefits, PTO, and maternity and paternity leave. The role includes the standard safety protocol expectations that come with any maintenance position.

One honest note: techs who do this work well tend to become indispensable on any maintenance team, because consistent, quality paint and resurface output is hard to find and easy to notice when it's missing. It's a role with a clear path toward senior maintenance or facilities coordination for someone who wants to grow.

job.title: Front Door Waste Technician-Cortland Lake Ridge Ridge
job.description:
It's 6:30 p.m. on a Tuesday. Residents are getting home from work, dogs need walking, and the valet trash window is open. Your route needs to run clean and on time, because in multifamily, the details residents notice most are the ones that happen right outside their front door.

What the Role Actually Involves

Cortland is hiring a Front Door Waste Technician at their Lake Ridge community in Hilliard, OH. This is a valet trash position, which means you're running a nightly collection route through the property, picking up resident waste bags set outside unit doors, loading them into leak-proof carts, and transporting everything to the onsite compactors or waste containers. You'll also clear trash from dog waste stations, pool areas, mail kiosks, parking lots, and common areas throughout the property.

The job has a real physical component. You're climbing stairs, covering ground on foot, and lifting up to 50 pounds through the full shift. Outdoor work in all weather is part of it, and so is the occasional strong odor. That's just the reality of the role. If you've worked in waste services or a service-focused job before, you already know what you're signing up for.

Cortland tracks route completion through a mobile app. You'll log start and end times, document your work with photos, and flag any improper or prohibited waste you encounter. Staying visible on property and communicating clearly with residents and staff is a daily expectation, not an afterthought. This is a resident-facing position, and how you carry yourself matters.

What Cortland Is Looking For

  • High school diploma or equivalent, preferred
  • At least one year of experience in waste services or a customer-facing role
  • Working knowledge of EPA and OSHA regulations for waste handling
  • Strong communication skills; bilingual ability is a plus
  • Ability to operate basic equipment, including compactors
  • Valid driver's license for local driving as needed
  • Personal smartphone (Android 2.2+ or iPhone iOS 4.3+) with an active data plan for app-based reporting
  • Physical ability to climb stairs, walk long distances, and lift up to 50 lbs throughout a shift

What separates the candidates who stick around in this role from those who don't is consistency. Routes run five or more nights a week. Residents notice immediately when service slips, and property managers notice too. Reliability, a professional attitude with residents, and attention to site cleanliness are the things that actually matter here day to day.

Cortland is a large, vertically integrated multifamily operator, founded in 2005 and ranked among the top ten multifamily owners in the country. They run their own design, construction, and operations, which means their properties tend to be actively managed with clear standards. For the right person, this kind of environment offers stability and a defined set of expectations, which can be easier to succeed in than a loosely run smaller operation.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
Weinstein Properties has been family-owned and operated for over 70 years, with more than 60 apartment communities across Virginia, North Carolina, Texas, Tennessee, and Georgia. That kind of longevity doesn't happen by accident. It reflects a consistent commitment to how people are treated, both residents and employees. This Assistant Property Manager role in Henrico's West End sits at the center of that philosophy.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Looks Like

This role touches nearly every part of community life. In the morning, you might be responding to internet leads and scheduling tours. By midday, you're walking a make-ready unit with maintenance to confirm it's truly move-in ready. The afternoon could bring a lease renewal conversation, a security deposit disposition, or helping a resident work through an account question. No two days stack up the same way.

Specific responsibilities include:

  • Working with prospective residents from first contact through lease signing, including phone and internet inquiries, tours, applications, and paperwork
  • Providing ongoing resident support: renewals, notices to vacate, transfers, pet addendums, work order follow-ups, and general account questions
  • Posting rent, tracking balances, and following up on amounts owed
  • Coordinating with maintenance on unit readiness and property upkeep
  • Processing move-outs and handling security deposit dispositions
  • Planning and hosting resident events
  • Supporting the Property Manager and helping train and lead the on-site team

Saturday hours are part of the schedule, worked on a rotating basis with the team. Occasionally, resident events or weather situations will ask something extra of you. That's the nature of on-site property management, and Weinstein is straightforward about it.

Who Tends to Succeed Here

Prior property management experience is a plus, but Weinstein genuinely recruits from hospitality, sales, and customer service backgrounds. If you've managed people or handled difficult customer situations with composure, the leasing and operations knowledge can be taught. What's harder to teach is the ability to hold a conversation with a frustrated resident, de-escalate without getting defensive, and then pivot to showing a prospective resident the community with genuine warmth. That's the real skill set this role demands.

Strong candidates tend to be organized without being rigid. They keep the punch list moving on a make-ready while also catching an incoming call and not making either person feel like they're second priority. Attention to detail matters here because mistakes on lease paperwork or security deposit dispositions create real problems downstream. Leadership experience is required because this role carries real responsibility for team outcomes, not just individual tasks.

Growth and Company Culture

Weinstein has a track record of promoting from within. Many of their current leaders started in leasing or assistant roles. The training program here is structured and intentional, so if you're newer to property management, you won't be left to figure things out on your own. The company wants this to be a career you grow into over time, which shows up in how they invest in coaching and professional development at the site level.

Compensation starts at $21 per hour, increases with experience, and includes quarterly bonuses. Benefits include health, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k with company match, paid holidays, birthday time off, an employee assistance program, and a rent discount.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

At Redpoint College Station, the Experience Team Member role sits at the intersection of sales, marketing, and daily operations. On a given day, you might tour a prospective resident through the community, field a maintenance request from a current tenant, pull a package from the receiving area, log the follow-up, and then pivot to helping promote an upcoming resident event on social media. The throughline is customer interaction, and there's a lot of it.

You'll conduct community and amenity tours, execute leasing and engagement initiatives set by the management team, and assist with local marketing efforts including social platforms and community programming. Administrative tasks are part of the mix too: keeping the office and common areas organized, scheduling maintenance follow-ups, and covering after-hours lockout calls on a rotating basis. Turn periods at a student property move fast, and availability during those windows is a genuine requirement of the role.

What You Bring

  • A customer-first orientation and the communication skills to back it up across a wide range of personalities
  • Flexibility to shift between sales conversations, administrative tasks, and physical property duties within a single shift
  • Reliability during high-demand periods: summers, holidays, and Turn
  • Self-discipline to manage responsibilities without constant supervision
  • Comfort with social media as a marketing and community engagement tool

What This Role Builds

Student housing operates on a tighter leasing calendar than conventional multifamily, and that compression teaches you to work quickly and precisely. You'll develop a practical understanding of how leasing traffic converts, what objections stall a lease signing, and how resident engagement affects retention. These are skills that transfer directly into leasing roles at Class A conventional properties or into assistant manager positions as you grow. The experience of managing customer relationships inside a collegiate community, where expectations are high and patience runs short, prepares you well for resident-facing leadership down the road.

Scion works specifically in the student housing sector, so the environment reflects that focus. This position is based on-site at Redpoint College Station, with daytime business hours as the baseline and an after-hours on-call rotation included. Work authorization in the United States is required; visa sponsorship is not available.

job.title: Leasing Consultant (Part-Time)
job.description:
A prospective resident walks in on a Saturday afternoon, having toured three other communities that week. They're tired, they're skeptical, and they haven't signed anywhere. What happens in the next thirty minutes depends entirely on you.

That's the central skill this part-time leasing consultant role at Berkshire Residential Investments builds, day after day: reading people quickly, earning trust, and converting genuine interest into a signed lease. Berkshire owns and manages its own properties, which means the team you join has real stake in outcomes. This isn't third-party management where directives come from a distant asset manager. The people above you in the org chart care about occupancy and resident satisfaction for the same reasons you will.

What the Work Actually Involves

Your primary job is guiding prospective residents from curiosity to commitment. Berkshire holds consultants to a closing ratio of at least 20%, which is a real benchmark that keeps you honest about your sales technique. Beyond the close, you'll maintain tour routes and model units so they consistently make the right first impression, track local market conditions so your pitches stay grounded in reality, and handle resident communications with enough professionalism that people feel heard rather than processed. Administrative accuracy matters here, because leasing paperwork done sloppily creates downstream problems for the whole team.

You'll also contribute ideas on marketing and resident satisfaction to the property manager. That collaboration matters more than it sounds. Consultants who pay attention to what objections come up repeatedly, or which concessions actually move traffic, bring real operational value beyond their closing numbers.

What You're Building Toward

Part-time leasing roles are often where strong property management careers start, and for good reason. The skills compound fast. You develop fluency in lease terms and fair housing compliance, you learn how occupancy decisions ripple into NOI, and you build the resident relationship skills that become essential if you move toward assistant manager or leasing director roles. Consultants who take the market-awareness piece seriously, not just memorizing comps but understanding why rents move, tend to make the jump to management-track positions more quickly.

Berkshire looks for at least two years of transferable customer service experience, comfort with technology, and strong written and verbal communication skills. Prior leasing experience isn't listed as a requirement, which means this can be a genuine entry point into residential property management for someone coming from retail, hospitality, or another client-facing field.

  • Minimum 20% closing ratio expectation
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • At least two years of customer service or related experience
  • Comfort adapting to leasing software and emerging technology
  • Attention to detail in administrative tasks

Anticipated base salary ranges from $21,750 to $25,000 annually, with placement determined by experience and qualifications. The position is part-time and based at Ellington Metro West.

job.title: Leasing Manager
job.description:
Affordable housing leasing in New York City operates under a distinct set of pressures. HUD regulations, NYC Rent Stabilization rules, waiting list management, and income eligibility requirements stack on top of one another in ways that have little parallel in conventional market-rate leasing. Fairstead, which owns and manages more than 30,000 units across 28 states, is hiring a Leasing Manager to oversee leasing operations at its New York properties and lead a team of leasing specialists through exactly that complexity.

What the Role Actually Covers

This is a supervisory leasing position with hands-on responsibility for occupancy performance. You'll manage the full leasing cycle: qualifying prospective residents against program eligibility criteria, showing units, processing applications, preparing leases and addendums, and reviewing move-in files for completeness and accuracy. Beyond your own activity, you're accountable for the accuracy of data entered by your leasing team in Yardi, and you'll monitor weekly occupancy and traffic reports to spot gaps before they become problems.

Waiting list management is a meaningful part of the job at affordable properties. Keeping those records current, processing applicants in compliance with HUD and agency guidelines, and ensuring all correspondence reflects program requirements takes consistent attention. NYC Rent Regulation laws add another layer, so familiarity with Rent Stabilization procedures matters here in a practical, day-to-day sense.

You'll also stay involved after move-in. Resident retention support, ongoing customer service, and work order coordination are part of the scope, which reflects Fairstead's integrated owner-operator model where leasing and operations stay connected rather than siloed.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • Three or more years of on-site leasing or sales experience, ideally with exposure to affordable or subsidized housing programs
  • Working knowledge of HUD regulations and NYC Rent Stabilization requirements
  • Proficiency in Yardi and Blue Moon, both of which are used actively in this role
  • Experience supervising or coaching leasing staff, with a track record of improving team performance
  • Comfort managing applicant eligibility reviews under specific program guidelines, not just standard credit and income screening
  • Bachelor's degree
  • Fair housing knowledge and strict adherence to compliance standards

The candidates who stand out in affordable leasing management typically combine genuine compliance fluency with the ability to coach their team through nuanced eligibility conversations. Getting an application wrong at an affordable property isn't just a leasing miss; it can trigger regulatory exposure. The managers who do this well understand that distinction and build habits in their teams accordingly.

Compensation for this role ranges from $90,000 to $100,000 annually, with a benefits package that includes employer-contributed medical coverage, employer-paid vision and life insurance, a 401(k) with company match, and 15 days of PTO plus 7 sick days and 12 or more paid holidays.

job.title: Regional Manager
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is a portfolio-level operations role with Asset Living, one of the largest third-party management firms in the country. You'll oversee a group of communities in the Salt Lake City market, working offsite but staying close enough to each property that nothing slips through. Your week will pull you between financial reviews, site visits, staffing conversations, and ownership reporting. The leasing environment in the Wasatch Front has been active, and occupancy pressures shift quickly as new supply continues to come online along the I-15 corridor. Knowing how to read that kind of market and translate it into a sharp marketing plan matters here.

On the financial side, you'll own NOI performance across your portfolio. That means developing annual operating budgets, reviewing monthly variance reports on income and expense line items, and flagging capex needs before they become emergencies. You'll monitor rent collections, reconcile deposits, approve vendor invoices, and make sure ownership financial reports close accurately and on time. When a property's T-12 starts showing a pattern, you're expected to catch it and recommend an adjustment, not wait for someone upstream to notice.

Personnel management takes up a significant share of your attention. You'll screen and hire community managers, coach them consistently, and hold them accountable using documented processes. Salary recommendations, timesheets, performance counseling, and terminations all run through you. Asset Living operates across multifamily, build-to-rent, affordable housing, and student housing segments, so your portfolio may not be uniform. The ability to lead site teams through different compliance environments and operational rhythms is genuinely useful here.

You'll also be responsible for leasing strategy at each property. That includes developing yearly marketing plans, evaluating staff leasing techniques, and building resident retention programs that keep renewals strong. When traffic slows or concessions creep up, you'll be expected to diagnose why and respond with a real plan.

What You Bring

  • Demonstrated experience managing a portfolio of multifamily communities as a regional or district manager
  • Solid grasp of property financials: budgeting, NOI analysis, variance reporting, and capex planning
  • Hands-on experience hiring, training, and managing on-site property management teams
  • Working knowledge of fair housing regulations and safety compliance requirements
  • Familiarity with leasing performance metrics and marketing strategy for multifamily assets
  • Strong communication skills with ownership groups and internal leadership
  • Experience with property management software and reporting systems

Context Worth Knowing

Asset Living operates as a fee management company, which means your communities have owners who expect accurate reporting and responsive communication. Regional managers in third-party management carry a different kind of accountability than those at owner-operators. You're representing the firm's reputation on every property, every quarter. Candidates who do well in this kind of role tend to be disciplined about documentation, comfortable having direct conversations with both site staff and ownership, and consistent in how they apply company standards across a mixed portfolio. The Salt Lake City market rewards managers who stay ahead of the leasing calendar rather than reacting to vacancy after it appears.

job.title: Lead Maintenance Technician - Olympus Latitude
job.description:
Olympus Property has earned the National Apartment Association's Top Employer designation three years running (2023, 2024, 2025), which tells you something about how the company treats the people doing the actual work. The Lead Maintenance Technician role at Olympus Latitude in Albuquerque sits at the center of that operation. This is a maintenance supervisor position in all but title, and the scope reflects that.

Day to day, you're running the service operation for the community. That means scheduling your team's daily, weekly, and monthly workloads, coordinating turns so vacant units are make-ready on time, and managing both in-house technicians and outside contractors. You'll handle preventative maintenance, oversee grounds and irrigation, coordinate repairs across structural, mechanical, electrical, and HVAC systems, and keep the shop organized and properly stocked. Monthly, quarterly, and yearly property inspections fall to you as well. You'll work closely with the on-site office team and the Business Manager to keep show units and upcoming move-ins clean and ready.

EPA/HVAC certification is required, along with at least three years of residential or apartment maintenance experience in a technician or supervisor capacity. The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 5 PM, with weekend availability and on-call rotation built in.

What This Role Builds

Lead tech roles are often where strong maintenance careers take a meaningful turn. You stop being purely reactive and start developing skills that compound: team development, vendor management, budget awareness through inventory control, and the kind of cross-functional communication that property managers rely on when things go sideways. People who do this role well often move into Regional Maintenance Supervisor positions or transition into property operations roles where that technical fluency becomes a real asset. The software systems Olympus uses to track service requests and inventory are the same types of platforms you'd encounter across any institutional owner's portfolio, so what you learn here travels.

What separates strong candidates from average ones at this level isn't just technical range. It's the ability to prioritize competing demands without losing track of unit turns, keep a team motivated through busy seasons, and build contractor relationships that actually hold up when you need someone on-site fast. Albuquerque's climate puts real demands on HVAC systems and irrigation, so comfort with both is genuinely useful here.

  • Minimum 3 years residential or apartment maintenance experience
  • EPA/HVAC certification required
  • Full-time availability, Monday through Friday, with weekend and on-call coverage
  • Experience managing or coordinating a maintenance team preferred

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, pet insurance, short and long-term disability, life and AD&D insurance, paid time off, an apartment rental allowance, and a sabbatical program. Monthly and quarterly bonuses are part of the compensation structure for eligible team members.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
West End Station is a property that calls for a community manager who can run a full operation, not just put out fires. Hawthorne Residential Partners, one of the larger Southeast-based multifamily operators in the country, is hiring for this Winston-Salem location and looking for someone who's ready to own the outcome.

What This Role Actually Covers

This is the full seat. You're accountable for financial performance, occupancy, team development, resident satisfaction, and the physical condition of the asset. On any given week, that means reviewing delinquency reports and following up on collections, walking the property for curb appeal and punch list items, coordinating with maintenance on work order backlog, and making sure your leasing team is converting traffic. It also means sitting in on a tough conversation with a resident and then turning around to coach a new leasing consultant on objection handling. The scope is real.

On the leasing side, you'll set pricing strategy and renewal targets alongside whatever guidance comes from regional. You'll support your team on tours when volume demands it, and you'll monitor occupancy closely enough to adjust concessions or marketing spend before a problem becomes a headline. Yardi and Knock are the core platforms here, so comfort with both matters from day one.

Vendor management, compliance, deposit accounting, move-out processing, online reputation, social media, resident events. It's all on your plate. That's the job.

Who Fits This Role

  • At least two years in multifamily, including time as a leasing consultant and assistant manager
  • Six months of direct community manager experience, strongly preferred
  • Working knowledge of Yardi, Knock, and Microsoft Office
  • High school diploma or GED; CAM, CAPS, or a real estate license is a plus
  • Valid driver's license

The candidates who tend to succeed here aren't necessarily the ones with the flashiest resumes. They're the ones who understand how financial performance and team morale connect. A manager who can read a T-12, spot where NOI is leaking, and then walk back to the leasing office and genuinely motivate their team is a different skill set than most people think. If you've only ever done one or the other, this role will stretch you.

Growth and Compensation

Hawthorne structures a career path from community manager to regional manager and backs it with a formal learning and development program. That's worth taking seriously if you're looking at your next two to three years in multifamily. The compensation package includes a base salary plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid time off (including your birthday, which is a small thing that's actually a nice touch), pet insurance, paid parental and adoption leave, and company-paid life insurance.

The leasing office runs Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, with Saturday hours from 10 to 4. One weekday off per week keeps it at a 40-hour schedule, though resident events and community needs can pull you outside those hours on occasion. That's property management.

job.title: Multifamily maintenance tech
job.description:
Maintenance tech roles at multifamily properties are pretty straightforward on paper. In practice, your day shifts between planned preventive work and whatever residents decided needed attention overnight. At Karya Property Management in Phoenix, this position covers the full range of day-to-day upkeep across residential apartment communities.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

You'll handle repairs across the standard trades: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, carpentry, and painting. Some days that means working through a ticket queue of resident requests. Other days it means responding to something urgent before the morning's half over. You'll also carry a share of the turn and make-ready workload, which in Phoenix's market means moving efficiently through punch lists during peak leasing periods without cutting corners on quality. Preventive maintenance rounds, tool upkeep, and inventory management round out the routine.

The role requires flexibility on hours, including evenings, weekends, and on-call availability. That's not a buried footnote. It's a real part of the job and something worth factoring in before you apply.

What Karya Is Looking For

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • One to three years of hands-on multifamily maintenance experience, or comparable work in a related field
  • Working knowledge of HVAC systems, plumbing, electrical, and general carpentry
  • Ability to troubleshoot and complete repairs independently without waiting for someone to walk you through it
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • Solid communication skills and enough organizational sense to manage your own ticket flow

HVAC knowledge carries real weight in Phoenix. The Valley runs air conditioning hard for a long stretch of the year, and a tech who can diagnose and address HVAC issues without escalating every call keeps residents satisfied and keeps the maintenance team running smoothly. If that's a strength you've built, lead with it.

Where This Role Can Take You

Technician roles at well-run multifamily companies are a legitimate path into lead maintenance and eventually maintenance supervisor positions. The techs who move up tend to be the ones who treat preventive maintenance as seriously as emergency response, who communicate clearly with the office team, and who bring a consistent standard to make-readies regardless of how tight the turn schedule gets. Karya offers health and wellness benefits, strong PTO, and parental leave, which signals a company that's thinking about retention rather than just filling a seat.

job.title: Customer Experience Specialist at Antero Apartments
job.description:
A prospective resident walks in on a Saturday afternoon, slightly frazzled after touring three other communities that morning. Within five minutes, you know their move-in timeline, their must-haves, and which available floor plan fits both. That's the core of what this role asks of you every day at Antero Apartments in Colorado Springs.

What the Role Actually Covers

Cottonwood Residential is hiring a full-time Customer Experience Specialist at Antero Apartments. The schedule includes evenings and weekends, which is standard for leasing-side work at any occupied community with consistent traffic. You'll greet prospects, residents, and vendors in person, respond to inquiries across phone, email, and text, and keep detailed records of every interaction. Knowing current availability, pricing, and unit details cold is a baseline expectation, not a stretch goal.

Beyond the leasing desk, the position has a real operational component. You'll walk the tour path, vacant homes, amenities, and common areas regularly to confirm everything meets Cottonwood's presentation standards. Make-ready readiness before a prospect tour or a resident move-in falls partly on you. You'll also organize the package room daily, support community event planning, assist with social media content, and help maintain vendor communication. It's a broad scope for an entry-level role, and that's intentional: Cottonwood structures this position as a genuine on-ramp toward property management.

Cottonwood was an early adopter of Self-Guided Tours, so you'll be working within a leasing model that expects technology comfort alongside interpersonal skill. Prospects who come in after a self-guided tour often arrive more informed and with sharper questions. Being able to meet them at that level matters.

What Cottonwood Is Looking For

  • Strong verbal and written communication across in-person, phone, and digital channels
  • A track record of staying organized under competing priorities
  • Comfort with a rotating schedule that includes weekend availability
  • A genuinely warm, professional presence when greeting anyone who walks through the door
  • Curiosity and a willingness to learn systems, pricing tools, and community-specific details quickly

Colorado Springs has seen meaningful apartment supply growth over the past several years, with several lease-up communities competing for the same renter pool. At a property like Antero, the leasing experience itself becomes part of the competitive advantage. Prospects have options, and the quality of that first interaction often determines whether they come back or sign elsewhere. Strong candidates in this role tend to understand that instinctively, without needing it explained.

Compensation includes a competitive base pay plus a quarterly bonus structure. Benefits, including full health, vision, dental, life, and disability coverage, become available within the first 30 days. The company also offers a 401k with match, HSA match, three weeks of paid time off in the first year, and 10.5 paid holidays.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Dallas, TX
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is a hands-on maintenance technician role at Berkshire's Medical District property in Dallas. Day to day, you're handling service requests across the full range: appliances, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, and general building upkeep. You're also keeping an eye on curb appeal, managing inventory in the shop, tracking keys, and making sure safety standards stay where they should be. Make-readies and punch list work are part of the rhythm here, not the exception.

Berkshire owns and manages its own portfolio, which means you're working for the owner, not a third-party fee manager. That tends to translate into more consistent capital support and less of the "we have to get approval from ownership" runaround when something genuinely needs fixing.

The Medical District location puts you in a dense, high-traffic Dallas submarket. Expect a mix of healthcare professionals and young renters who keep odd hours and have real expectations for service turnaround. Quick, clean response times matter here.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of residential maintenance experience in a multifamily or similar setting
  • Working knowledge of plumbing, electrical, appliances, and carpentry
  • Comfort with computers and related maintenance or work order applications
  • Strong written and verbal communication in English
  • Genuine attention to curb appeal and property presentation

A Few Honest Notes

Maintenance tech roles at multifamily properties involve after-hours on-call rotations. The posting doesn't detail the schedule, but plan for it. The candidates who thrive in this kind of role aren't just technically capable. They communicate well with residents, close out work orders cleanly, and don't leave management guessing about what got done and what didn't. That last part matters more than most postings let on.

Berkshire offers three weeks of vacation, a 25% rent discount, and personal development plans, which is a reasonable package for this level. For a tech looking to grow, time with a vertically integrated owner like Berkshire can build toward a lead tech or maintenance supervisor path, since you're seeing the full operational picture rather than a narrow slice of it.

job.title: Floating Maintenance Technician
job.description:
The Role at a Glance

Floating maintenance positions cover multiple properties instead of one fixed site. That means more variety day to day, but also more coordination. You need to read a new property quickly, assess what's behind, and get to work. CommonPlace by Collective Residential operates garden-style communities in the Raleigh-Durham area and is hiring a Floating Maintenance Supervisor to keep those properties safe, clean, and ready for residents.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

A good portion of your time goes toward unit turns. You'll complete make-readies, run punch lists, and confirm units are genuinely move-in ready before keys hand over. You'll also schedule and perform preventive maintenance, handle service requests per company guidelines, and oversee vendor work on-site to make sure quality and compliance standards are met.

On the supervisory side, you're responsible for training the maintenance team, managing schedules, and holding work to CommonPlace's standards. You'll track inventory, submit supply orders, maintain MSDS sheets and replacement logs, and keep tools and equipment organized. Lock changes after evictions, snow removal, and on-call emergency response are also part of the job.

You'll report unusual conditions directly to the Property Manager. Staying ahead of problems before they become resident complaints is a core part of performing well in this role.

Key qualifications CommonPlace is looking for:

  • 3 to 5 years of hands-on maintenance experience in property management
  • 1 to 3 years of supervisory experience
  • Solid working knowledge of plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliances, and general construction
  • Comfortable with hand tools, power tools, and motorized equipment
  • Ability to lift and carry up to 50 lbs independently
  • Valid driver's license and personal auto liability insurance (required for traveling between properties)
  • Availability for an on-call rotation

What Sets Strong Candidates Apart

The floating nature of this role is the real differentiator. Technicians who do well in fixed-site roles sometimes struggle when the property, the team, and the punch list change week to week. The candidates who stand out here are the ones who can walk a property they've never seen, identify what needs attention without being told, and get a team moving quickly. HVAC competency in particular goes a long way in Raleigh's climate, where summer calls spike and residents feel every delay. If you've worked lease-up or heavy turn seasons before, that experience translates directly.

Pay runs $31.00 to $34.00 per hour. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, and a 401k with employer match, plus paid vacation, sick time, and volunteer time.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
Apartment maintenance is unglamorous work much of the time. You're unclogging drains, patching drywall, replacing appliances in vacant units, and picking up trash before residents notice it piled up. Then your phone rings at 11 p.m. because a water heater went out. That's the job, and FLATS LLC in Las Vegas wants someone who already knows this and shows up anyway.

FLATS LLC, part of the ProperXPM family, is hiring a Maintenance Supervisor for one of their Las Vegas residential communities. The scope covers what you'd expect from a full-service maintenance role: completing work orders, handling turns on vacant units, keeping common areas clean and functional, and running preventive maintenance on building systems. Pool maintenance and seasonal amenity upkeep are part of the rotation too. Minor plumbing, electrical, drywall, painting, light carpentry , you need to be competent across all of it, because this isn't a role where you wait on a specialized sub for every small fix.

After-hours on-call is on a rotating schedule, so it won't be every night, but it will come around. That's worth knowing before you apply.

What you bring

  • Proven apartment or building maintenance experience, or a strong background in a related trade
  • Working knowledge of electrical, plumbing, HVAC, and appliance repair
  • Comfortable with hand and power tools, physical tasks, and lifting up to 50 lbs
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • High school diploma or equivalent preferred

The candidates who do well in roles like this tend to be self-directing. A property manager can't follow you from unit to unit. You'll get a list of work orders, a punch list of make-ready tasks, and the expectation that you'll work through them without constant check-ins. If you need a lot of hand-holding to prioritize your day, this will be frustrating for everyone. If you're the type who finishes a turn and immediately checks what's next, you'll fit the rhythm of this operation.

Las Vegas heat puts real stress on HVAC systems and pool equipment, which means preventive maintenance here isn't just a checkbox. Catching a failing condenser before peak summer is the difference between a manageable repair and a building full of unhappy residents. Technicians with experience in desert climates know this already.

Benefits include health, dental, and vision insurance, a 401(k), paid time off, and a referral program. This is a full-time, on-site position.

job.title: Leasing Consultant (Hearth)
job.description:
A prospective resident walks in on a Saturday afternoon, unsure whether a studio or one-bedroom fits their budget. By the time they leave, they've toured the apartment, asked every question they had, and feel genuinely good about the decision in front of them. That moment is the center of this role.

What This Role Actually Covers

Prometheus Real Estate Group calls this position a Neighbor Ambassador rather than a Leasing Consultant, and that distinction reflects how the job is structured. You're responsible for the full leasing cycle: responding to inquiries, guiding prospects through tours, preparing rental agreements, and following up to convert interest into signed leases. At the same time, you're a day-to-day point of contact for current residents, which means customer service runs alongside sales rather than separate from it.

The administrative layer is real and worth understanding before you apply. You'll conduct market surveys, generate neighborhood reports, and post apartment listings. These tasks build operational fluency that most entry-level leasing roles don't offer as deliberately. If you've worked in retail, hospitality, or any customer-facing sales environment, the interpersonal skills transfer directly. The property management side is what you'll build here.

Weekend availability is a firm requirement. Leasing traffic peaks on Saturdays and Sundays, so your regular days off will fall during the week. This schedule suits some people well and frustrates others. Know which category you fall into before you apply.

Qualifications and Compensation

Prometheus hires across industries and doesn't require prior property management experience. What they're looking for is genuine customer orientation, comfort in a sales environment, and the kind of self-direction that makes someone effective without constant supervision. Strong written communication matters too, since much of the administrative work involves drafting-facing content and reports.

Compensation for this role includes:

  • Hourly pay range of $25.00 to $26.25, plus a weekend shift premium
  • $200 per lease incentive
  • Discretionary semi-annual bonus
  • Additional bonuses tied to referrals, training, renovation projects, and lease-up assignments
  • 100% company-paid medical, vision, and dental coverage including eligible dependents
  • 401(k) with employer matching
  • Tenure-based housing discounts
  • Educational assistance and tuition reimbursement
  • Paid volunteer time and 12 paid holidays, including your birthday

One thing worth noting for career-minded candidates: leasing consultant roles at well-structured companies like this one tend to feed directly into assistant manager and property manager tracks. The combination of sales performance, resident relations, and administrative exposure you get here covers the core competencies that most promotion decisions in property management are based on. If you treat this as a training ground rather than just a job, the path forward is clear.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role splits your week between leasing and ledgers, and you need to be comfortable with both. Some days you're walking prospects through available homes at Enclave at Deep River, building rapport, and closing leases. Other days you're deep in accounts receivable: posting payments, reviewing ledgers for billing errors, making delinquency follow-up calls, and coordinating with the Community Manager when an eviction procedure needs to move forward. Neither side of the job is optional.

You'll also step in as the acting lead when the Community Manager is out. That means keeping the team on task, fielding resident concerns, and making judgment calls without someone to escalate to. It's a real test of whether you can hold the operation together under pressure, and Hawthorne's structure treats it as preparation for the next step, not just gap coverage.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, and Saturdays 10 to 4, with one weekday off each week to hit 40 hours. Resident events or community-specific needs can pull you into evenings occasionally. That's the honest reality of the schedule.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of property management experience, with preference for candidates who've already held an assistant community manager title
  • Comfort reading a rent roll, catching ledger discrepancies, and having direct conversations with delinquent residents
  • Leasing instincts: identifying what a prospect actually needs, matching them to the right home, and moving the paperwork through cleanly
  • High School diploma or GED required; a CALP credential is a plus
  • Valid driver's license
  • Ability to de-escalate resident conflicts without losing your composure or your paper trail

Context Worth Knowing

Hawthorne Residential Partners manages communities across the Southeast and ranks among the 50 largest multifamily operators in the country. For candidates thinking about career trajectory, this role is a direct pipeline to Community Manager. Hawthorne runs a formal Career Path Program with internal learning and development support, so the path isn't just implied, it's structured.

What separates a strong candidate here from an average one is financial fluency. Plenty of people can run a tour. Fewer can catch a misapplied payment, hold a firm but fair delinquency conversation, and still retain the resident at renewal. If you've done both sides of the job consistently, this role fits your experience well.

Compensation includes hourly pay plus monthly leasing and renewal commissions and quarterly performance bonuses. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, paid time off (including your birthday), paid parental and adoption leave, pet insurance, company-paid life insurance, and 24/7 telehealth access.

job.title: Floating Maintenance Technician (Fayetteville)
job.description:
Fayetteville's rental market carries a particular rhythm shaped by Fort Liberty. High resident turnover, frequent PCS moves, and a consistent demand cycle mean properties here stay busy year-round. Van Metre operates four communities across the city, and this floating technician role sits at the center of keeping all of them running.

The position covers The Villagio, Hunter's Ridge, Stone Gate, and Village on the Lake. Rather than being anchored to a single property, you'll move between sites based on need, which means your day can shift from completing turns at one community to knocking out service requests at another. Occasional travel to Van Metre properties in Greensboro and Burlington is possible, though Fayetteville is the primary focus. The role reports to the Director of Facilities and works closely with Service Managers on the ground at each site.

The core work covers the full range of a technician's responsibilities: service requests, make-ready turns, preventative maintenance, exterior and grounds upkeep, and daily property walks for curb appeal and safety. You'll also carry on-call responsibility as part of the team's 24/7 coverage rotation, so after-hours calls are part of the job and worth factoring in before you apply.

Candidates need to come in ready to work. This means holding an EPA 608 certification, CFC credentials, and a current CPO. Solid working knowledge of appliance repair, plumbing, electrical, and basic HVAC is expected. You'll also need to supply your own basic tools and hold a valid driver's license for travel between sites.

Qualifications

  • 1 to 2 years of hands-on maintenance experience, or equivalent formal training
  • EPA 608 and CFC certifications (required, not preferred)
  • CPO certification current and active
  • Working knowledge of appliance, electrical, and plumbing repair
  • Basic understanding of HVAC systems and electrical circuitry
  • Familiarity with OSHA and current building safety standards
  • Own basic tools and ability to use them safely
  • Valid driver's license
  • Availability for weekend work and after-hours emergency calls

Pay runs from $23 to $26 per hour depending on experience and credentials, with an annual bonus of up to $5,000 paid quarterly. Van Metre's benefits package includes a strong PTO structure, company-matched 401(k), tuition reimbursement, company-paid certifications, and a wellness reimbursement of up to $900 per year. Employees also receive rental discounts across Van Metre communities.

One thing worth noting for technicians considering the floating structure: the variety accelerates your familiarity with different property layouts and maintenance histories faster than a single-site role typically does. If you're aiming toward a Service Manager position down the road, cross-site exposure gives you a broader operational picture and makes that transition easier to argue for.

job.title: $1,500 Sign-On Bonus - Multisite Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
A resident puts in a work order at 7 a.m. By 8, you've already triaged it, assigned it to the right tech, and moved on to a scheduled HVAC inspection at the second property across town. That's the rhythm of this role.

BAM Companies, a Indianapolis-based property management firm founded in 2010, is hiring a Multisite Maintenance Supervisor to lead maintenance operations across multiple residential properties. The pay range runs $25 to $30 per hour, and the position comes with a $1,500 sign-on bonus plus a housing discount at a BAM property.

What the Job Covers

You'll oversee a team of maintenance technicians and take direct responsibility for keeping mechanical systems, common areas, and grounds in good working order across properties. Day-to-day, that means scheduling and tracking preventative maintenance, managing supply purchasing, and making sure work orders get completed to standard.
