You'll also carry a training and coaching function: this is a supervisory role, so developing your team is part of the job, not a side task.

  • Lead and train maintenance staff across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and general upkeep
  • Build and manage a preventative maintenance calendar to catch problems before they become costly
  • Hold the team to consistent property standards across all sites
  • Manage supply budgets and keep operations cost-efficient
  • Maintain curb appeal and common areas alongside mechanical systems

What BAM Needs from You

Two to three years of hands-on property maintenance experience is the baseline. Supervisory experience is a plus, but BAM is open to candidates who have the technical depth and are ready to step into a leadership role. You'll need an EPA Type 2 or Universal certification, a valid driver's license, and a reliable vehicle since you're moving between sites regularly.

Strong written and verbal communication matters here. You're coordinating between residents, your team, and property management, so the ability to communicate clearly across all three keeps things from falling through the cracks.

Benefits include medical, dental, vision, and life insurance, plus 14.5 paid holidays and PTO that kicks in after 90 days.

One thing worth knowing about multisite maintenance roles: the split-focus nature of the job means you need strong organizational habits. Techs at one property may need direction while you're physically at another. Supervisors who succeed in this setup tend to build reliable checklists and communication routines early so the team can operate with some autonomy between your visits. If you've worked a single-site role and want more scope, this is a natural next step.

job.title: Apartment Accounts Receivable Assistant
job.description:
Skills This Role Puts to Work Every Day

Delinquency management sits at the intersection of financial operations and resident relations, and the skills it demands are specific. You'll need steady communication instincts, the ability to hold a firm position without escalating tension, and enough organizational discipline to track dozens of accounts simultaneously across different stages of the collections cycle. This role at AIR Communities draws on all of that, daily.

AIR is one of the largest apartment owners in the country, operating high-quality properties across major U.S. markets. Their Shared Services Center in the Denver Tech Center handles centralized collections across that portfolio, which means the volume and variety of accounts you'll work is meaningful from day one. This is a five-day-in-office position at their corporate headquarters, which spans the top two floors of a DTC tower.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

The core of this job is outbound contact with delinquent residents: phone calls, written notices, and follow-up on payment arrangements. You'll process late notices, handle legal filings, review warrants of restitution, and coordinate evictions when accounts reach that point. Setting up alternative payment plans is part of the toolkit, as is documenting every interaction and activity accurately for audit and legal purposes. You may also recommend charge-offs on accounts that have exhausted recovery options.

The negotiation piece is real. Conversations with residents who owe back rent are rarely easy, and maintaining professionalism under that kind of pressure is a skill this role will test and develop. Composure matters as much as process knowledge here.

On the technical side, you'll work across multiple systems and office tools. AIR uses software common in large-scale multifamily operations, and comfort picking up new platforms quickly is expected.

What Separates Strong Candidates

The candidates who perform best in centralized collections roles like this one tend to combine two things that don't always travel together: genuine patience in difficult conversations and a consistent follow-through habit on documentation. Missing either one creates problems. If you've worked in collections, property management, or any high-volume customer-facing role where you had to hold people accountable to financial commitments, that experience transfers directly.

The commission structure tied to collections performance also means your earning potential has a real ceiling determined by how effective you are, not just by the base pay range of $21 to $23 per hour.

  • Strong verbal and written communication across a range of resident situations
  • Negotiation skills with the ability to reach workable resolutions
  • Ability to manage stress and stay composed during difficult account conversations
  • Computer literacy and comfort learning new property management or collections software
  • Attention to detail in documenting collection activity accurately

AIR's benefits package includes medical, dental, vision, and life insurance, HSA and FSA options, short and long-term disability covered by the company, a 401(k) with up to 6% employer match, paid parental leave up to 16 weeks, tuition assistance, and a 25% rent discount at any AIR community. For someone building a career in multifamily finance or operations, the exposure this role provides to large-scale delinquency workflows across a national portfolio is genuinely useful experience.

job.title: Portfolio Performance Specialist
job.description:
Third-party management firms like Asset Living operate across dozens of properties simultaneously, which means performance gaps at the site level can compound fast. The Portfolio Performance Specialist exists to close those gaps: stepping in when sites are understaffed, diagnosing underperforming properties, and embedding better operational habits before problems escalate.

What This Role Actually Covers

This is a field-facing, problem-solving position. You'll split your time between covering staffing vacancies at sites across the portfolio and working alongside the Executive Vice President on special projects tied to operational improvement. Some weeks that means running leasing operations at a property mid-transition. Other weeks it means auditing resident files, reviewing move-in and move-out procedures, or identifying where a site's processes have drifted from standard.

You'll gather performance data, evaluate what's working on the ground, and communicate findings back to the corporate operations team. When a property is struggling, you help build the path forward, whether that's identifying skill gaps on the onsite team, flagging process breakdowns, or supporting training initiatives that get operations back on track.

The resident-facing side of the role is real. You'll handle resident account issues, support renewal processes, and assist with marketing events including grand openings and resident appreciation programming. You'll also pull market surveys and competitive set data for new acquisitions, which means you need to understand how a property positions itself relative to its submarket.

Qualifications

  • Prior experience as an Assistant Community Director or Community Director is required
  • Solid working knowledge of Fair Housing, ADA, and Landlord/Tenant law fundamentals
  • Comfortable in Yardi and the standard MS Office suite
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, since much of this role involves translating field observations into actionable feedback for regional and corporate teams
  • High school diploma required; additional education preferred

Candidates who do well in this type of role tend to have one specific skill that separates them from solid site-level operators: they can read a struggling property quickly. They walk in, assess the team, review the numbers, and know within a short window where the real problems are. That diagnostic instinct, combined with the patience to coach rather than just correct, is what makes this position effective. If your background is mostly execution without exposure to cross-property operations or training, expect a steeper learning curve.

Asset Living manages multifamily, student housing, affordable, build-to-rent, and single-family rental communities across the country, so the portfolio variety is broad. You should expect to work across asset types and markets, which adds complexity but also gives you exposure that most single-site or single-region roles simply don't.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
The Scion Group operates student housing at scale, and 44 North in Minneapolis reflects that model: a community where occupancy pressure, lease-up timing, and resident satisfaction all hit at once, usually during the same week. The Assistant Community Manager title here carries real operational weight. Scion calls the role Resident Services Manager internally, and the scope matches: this person owns the resident experience from move-in to move-out while keeping leasing workflows, delinquency follow-up, and compliance processes moving in parallel.

Day to day, you're watching the Entrata dashboard the way a revenue manager watches a hotel's booking curve. Delinquency notices go out on schedule. Lease documents get generated, reviewed, and countersigned under the General Manager's direction. Move-in inspections get coordinated. When a resident dispute escalates, you're the one mediating it before it becomes a negative review or a legal matter. Reputation management across review platforms is an explicit part of the job, which means your resident interactions have a measurable downstream effect on traffic and lease conversion.

The leasing support component is real. You're not running the leasing team, but you provide backup on lead follow-up, sales calls, and lease execution when volume demands it. During peak move-in periods, which in student housing often means a compressed August window where hundreds of residents arrive in days, evening and weekend availability is expected. The role also calls for occasional support at other properties in the Scion portfolio, so comfort operating outside your home community matters.

Student housing creates a specific operational challenge worth naming: residents are often first-time renters, which means the volume of service requests, questions, and complaints runs higher than at a conventional multifamily property. Strong candidates come in with conflict resolution instincts already developed, not just customer service polish. The ability to handle a crisis call, a delinquency escalation, and a resident event all in the same day without losing composure is the real differentiator here.

What Scion is looking for

  • 2 or more years in property management, leasing, or resident services
  • Hands-on experience with Entrata or a comparable property management platform
  • Demonstrated conflict resolution and de-escalation skills
  • Comfort managing social media and local marketing initiatives
  • Organized enough to track renewals, notices, insurance compliance, and leasing metrics concurrently
  • Flexibility for evening and weekend coverage during move-in, peak leasing, and emergency situations
  • Eligible to work in the United States without visa sponsorship

The Minnesota base salary range runs $50,000 to $55,000, with a discretionary annual bonus on top. Benefits include health, dental, and vision coverage, 401k matching, paid parental leave, and learning reimbursement. This is an exempt, full-time, on-site position at 44 North in Minneapolis.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor at Raveneaux Apartments
job.description:
Raveneaux Apartments is a multifamily community in Houston managed by Cottonwood Residential, a fully integrated real estate company with a national portfolio. The Maintenance Supervisor role here carries real weight. You're the person residents think of when something goes wrong, the person your techs look to when priorities shift mid-morning, and the person ownership counts on to keep costs in line without letting the property slip. That's a lot of relationships to manage well, and it's worth being honest about that from the start.

Day to day, you're running maintenance operations end to end. That means owning the make-ready process, keeping the preventative maintenance schedule from becoming a wishlist, and making sure work orders don't age out in the system. You'll also be hands-on when the situation calls for it, working across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and general repairs alongside your team rather than just delegating from a distance. Vendor coordination is a meaningful part of this job too. Scheduling, supervising scope, holding people accountable to timelines. Houston's vendor market is active and competitive, so knowing how to build productive working relationships with reliable contractors matters more than it might in smaller markets.

The leadership piece is where this role gets nuanced. You'll hire, onboard, train, and coach your service team, which means you're responsible for both their output and their development. That's not always easy. Techs come in with different skill levels, different work styles, and sometimes different ideas about urgency. The supervisors who do well in this kind of role tend to be direct communicators who set clear expectations without micromanaging, and who understand that retention on the maintenance side often comes down to whether people feel respected and supported on the job.

Cottonwood also expects you to stay close to the numbers. You'll manage maintenance-related expenses against the property budget, support purchase order processes, and keep documentation accurate, including SDS logs and vendor records. Resident communication runs through this role as well. When a service request sits too long or something gets missed, it's usually the maintenance supervisor who fields the follow-up, whether that's from the resident directly or from the leasing office.

What You'll Need

  • High school diploma or GED
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • At least 2 years of multifamily maintenance experience
  • At least 2 years supervising or leading a maintenance team
  • EPA Type II or Universal certification (required)
  • CPO certification (preferred)
  • CAMT certification (preferred)
  • Solid working knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, and electrical systems
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office; experience with Entrata is a plus
  • Availability for evenings, weekends, and on-call rotation
  • Ability to lift up to 75 lbs. regularly, with assistance for heavier loads

Candidates who stand out tend to have a track record of low delinquency on their work order queues and can speak specifically to how they've developed junior techs. If you've overseen a lease-up or brought a neglected property back to standard, that experience translates directly here. Cottonwood is growing nationally, and supervisors who demonstrate operational discipline and people leadership tend to find real advancement opportunities within the portfolio.

job.title: Leasing Consultant (Floating)
job.description:
Berkshire Residential Investments is looking for a Floating Leasing Consultant to cover communities across New Jersey as staffing needs shift. The base salary runs $43,500 to $50,000, depending on experience.

This is a travel-heavy role. You won't be anchored to one property. Berkshire will move you between communities based on where the leasing team needs coverage, so adaptability isn't optional. You need to walk into an unfamiliar office, get oriented quickly, and start contributing the same day.

The core of the job is leasing. You're working leads, conducting tours, following up, and closing. Berkshire sets a minimum 20% closing ratio as a baseline expectation, so this isn't a role where showing people around counts as success. You're converting traffic into signed leases. Beyond that, you're keeping the leasing office and tour routes in good shape, staying current on local market conditions, and communicating professionally with both prospects and current residents.

The administrative side matters here too. Floating consultants often step into communities mid-process, which means picking up where someone else left off. Clean notes, accurate records, and attention to detail keep things from falling apart during transitions.

What separates a strong floating consultant from an average one is the ability to read a community fast. Every property has its own rhythm: different resident demographics, different competitive pressures, different objections in the leasing office. The consultants who do well in this structure don't need weeks to get comfortable. They ask the right questions on day one and adjust.

What you'll bring

  • At least two years of customer service experience, ideally in leasing or a sales environment
  • Comfort with technology and the ability to pick up new platforms quickly
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Reliable transportation and willingness to travel across New Jersey communities

Berkshire owns and manages its own portfolio, so you're working within a single organization rather than a third-party management structure. That tends to mean more consistency in systems and standards across properties, which helps when you're moving between sites regularly.

job.title: Senior Community Manager - Affordable Housing
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role sits at the intersection of compliance, operations, and resident services on an affordable housing property in Saint Paul. The day-to-day is dense. You're tracking delinquency, managing recertifications, coordinating with the compliance department on regulatory responses, and keeping your maintenance program tight enough to pass a REAC inspection without scrambling. When a Management and Occupancy Review lands on the calendar, you're the one who owns the preparation.

Compliance is a core function here, not a side task. HUD 4350.3 is your operating manual. You'll handle annual and interim recertifications, monitor EIV activity, and stay current on LIHTC requirements through TCS. When residents fall out of compliance with lease or program requirements, you're coordinating intervention strategies with your Regional Manager rather than waiting for a problem to escalate into litigation.

On the financial side, you're attending monthly budget meetings, watching bad-debt write-offs, and pursuing delinquencies through legal channels when necessary. You're also the point person for vendor coordination, unit inspections, and bi-annual walk-throughs with the Building Superintendent. Construction updates, violation avoidance, and resident access during renovation cycles all run through you.

What You Bring

  • At least three years of management experience that includes direct team supervision (property management experience in affordable housing is the target profile)
  • COS or CPO certification, active and current
  • TCS certification for tax credit compliance
  • Hands-on EIV experience and comfort in Yardi
  • Working knowledge of HUD regulations, Fair Housing, ADA, and FCRA
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and the ability to manage multiple compliance deadlines simultaneously
  • Bachelor's degree preferred but not required

The Operational Reality

Affordable housing management at this level requires a specific kind of attention. Recertification errors, missed MOR prep, or delinquency that goes unmanaged long enough to hit bad-debt don't just affect NOI, they affect residents and regulatory standing. The candidates who perform well in roles like this tend to be comfortable owning compliance outcomes end-to-end, not just flagging issues upward. If you've managed a HUD or LIHTC property through a REAC cycle or an MOR and came out clean, that experience translates directly here.

Fairstead operates as an integrated platform across development, construction, and property management, which means a Senior Community Manager here has more visibility into capital projects and construction coordination than you'd typically find in a third-party management environment. The salary range for this position is $68,000 to $70,000, with a benefits package that includes employer-contributed medical and dental through United Healthcare, a company-matched 401(k), and 15 days of PTO plus 12 paid holidays.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
Skills This Role Runs On

This Community Manager position at Griffis Residential in West Palm Beach centers on three core skill sets: financial oversight, team development, and operational execution. You'll read budgets, track delinquency, manage capex projects, and keep occupancy where it needs to be. At the same time, you're coaching leasing staff, running inspections, and staying current on the local competitive market. The role requires someone who can shift between a budget spreadsheet and a resident conversation without losing a beat.

Strong lease comprehension matters here. You'll handle collections, interpret legal documents, and make calls on rent-related situations that have real financial consequences. Griffis uses iPad-based leasing and marketing tools, so comfort with technology is part of the daily workflow, not an occasional task.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

Day-to-day, you're running the property. That means leading and delegating to your team, reviewing community conditions through regular inspections, responding to resident service needs, and keeping vendors accountable to scope and budget. You'll oversee capital improvement projects from progress monitoring through payment approval.

On the leasing side, you're coaching associates on conversion and customer service standards, not just watching the numbers come in. Griffis has defined leasing and marketing expectations, and part of your job is making sure your team meets them consistently.

You'll also track market conditions and competitors, which feeds your recommendations on concessions, pricing, and strategy. This isn't a passive reporting function. Griffis expects Community Managers to bring informed opinions to the table.

  • Three or more years in multi-family or hospitality management
  • Solid grasp of community financials, collections, and lease documentation
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Outlook, Excel, Word)
  • High school diploma required; bachelor's degree or CAM/ARM certification preferred
  • Demonstrated ability to build and coach a team

What Makes This Role Worth a Closer Look

The compensation range sits between $87,000 and $100,000, plus a $2,500 sign-on bonus. The bonus structure is layered: a quarterly bonus of up to 25% of annual salary, a retention bonus, and an occupancy bonus starting at $175 per lease. That's meaningful upside if you perform.

The benefits package is substantial. Griffis offers a 50% rental discount, 401(k) with up to 4% company match, 11 paid holidays, a minimum of three weeks PTO accruing from day one, paid parental leave, and tuition reimbursement up to $5,250 annually. The PTO exchange for student loan repayment is a less common perk worth noting if that's relevant to you.

One thing that separates strong candidates in this role: the ability to hold a team accountable while still developing them. Managers who focus only on results without investing in their staff tend to see turnover that hurts occupancy and morale. Griffis has built out coaching and cross-training expectations into the role itself, which signals they take team development seriously at the operational level.

job.title: Regional Manager, Affordable Housing
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role puts you over a portfolio of affordable housing communities across the Colorado Springs and Denver markets, reporting up through Asset Living's third-party management structure. The compliance side of affordable housing is front and center here. You'll monitor LIHTC application and annual recertification processes, conduct file reviews, run semi-annual physical inspections, and stay current with regulatory agencies. If you've managed affordable portfolios before, you already know that a single file error can create audit exposure that ripples back to ownership. That's the standard you're held to.

Beyond compliance, this is a full regional management role. You'll build and manage operating budgets, review monthly variances against budget, and push toward the highest achievable NOI through cost control and occupancy strategy. You'll also handle capex planning, oversee vendor contracts and work in progress at your sites, and ensure property closeout and ownership reporting land on time. On the personnel side, you'll hire, train, coach, and when necessary counsel or terminate site staff, with proper documentation and coordination with HR. Approving timesheets, signing off on salary requests for Community Managers, and keeping your teams running at a consistent standard all fall to you.

Leasing and marketing aren't an afterthought. You'll develop yearly marketing plans, evaluate leasing technique effectiveness at the site level, and implement resident retention programs. Affordable communities carry their own leasing dynamics, and you'll need to understand how income restrictions, waitlists, and recertification timelines affect occupancy strategy differently than a conventional portfolio.

What You Bring

  • Hands-on experience managing LIHTC and/or Section 8 communities, including file reviews and regulatory reporting
  • Demonstrated ability to oversee multiple sites simultaneously as an off-site regional leader
  • Experience building and managing operating budgets with monthly variance analysis
  • A track record of developing on-site staff through coaching, documentation, and consistent performance management
  • Working knowledge of Fair Housing and EHO/Affirmative Fair Housing requirements
  • Comfort with the administrative side: reporting accuracy, invoice coding, deposit reconciliation, and closeout processes

Context Worth Knowing

Asset Living is a large third-party management firm with an NMHC top-50 ranking and an AMO designation through IREM. Their affordable housing division sits alongside conventional multifamily, student, build-to-rent, and single-family rental operations, which matters for how this role connects to the broader organization. You're not operating in isolation. Decisions on staffing, capex, and budgets run through a Regional and Senior VP layer, and you'll coordinate regularly with HR and ownership reporting teams.

The Colorado Springs and Denver markets have seen significant affordable housing pressure in recent years, with tax credit developments becoming a more prominent part of the housing stock as rents have climbed across both metros. Strong regional managers in affordable housing tend to have an edge when they treat the compliance infrastructure with the same rigor they give to financial performance. The candidates who stand out at this level know how to read a T-12 and a regulatory agreement in the same sitting.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
A resident submits a work order at 7 a.m. for a broken A/C. By 8, you've already pulled the service history, diagnosed the issue, and ordered the part. That's the pace at Ion at the Ballpark, a student housing community in Birmingham operated by The Scion Group.

What the Job Covers

This is a full-scope maintenance role. You'll handle service requests, run preventive maintenance on major building systems, and prep units for turn. Life safety systems are part of your regular responsibility: fire pumps, sprinkler systems, smoke and CO2 detectors, emergency lighting, backflow preventers, and alarm panels all fall under your watch. When vendors come on site, you coordinate their schedules and escort them as needed. You'll also help develop emergency preparedness plans and maintain key management protocols.

Student housing turns are compressed and unforgiving. The gap between a resident moving out and the next one moving in is tight, and the punch list has to be done right the first time. This role requires someone who tracks their own assignments, follows through without being reminded, and communicates clearly with the facilities manager and the broader team.

What You'll Need

  • High school diploma, GED, or trade school credential plus 3 to 5 years of full-time general maintenance experience
  • EPA 608 certification (Core, Type I, II, and III)
  • Certified Pool Operator (CPO) license, or willingness to obtain one within six months of hire
  • Valid driver's license
  • Comfort working in property management software and building automation systems (Entrata and CMMS experience is useful)
  • Physical ability to stand for extended shifts and lift up to 100 lbs.
  • Availability for on-call coverage, including after-hours and weekend emergencies

Strong candidates in this role tend to have HVAC and plumbing depth, not just surface-level familiarity. Diagnosing a building automation issue or running a fire system test requires real technical confidence. If your background is mostly light repairs and cosmetic work, this position will be a stretch.

The Scion Group offers health, dental, and vision insurance, 401k matching, paid parental leave, paid time off with floating holidays, a discretionary annual bonus, and learning reimbursement. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Full-Time
job.description:
Redstone Residential manages more than 38,000 beds across 20 states, making it one of the largest third-party student housing operators in the country. The Station at Millrace in Provo is part of that portfolio, and this full-time Maintenance Technician role sits at the center of how the property performs day to day.

The work itself covers the full range of ground-level maintenance: completing make-readies before new residents move in, keeping common areas clean and presentable, handling basic repairs, managing landscaping upkeep, and responding to emergencies according to established procedures. Pool service and maintenance is part of the regular rotation, so working knowledge there is a genuine requirement. You'll coordinate directly with the Maintenance Supervisor or Property Manager when issues exceed routine scope, which means clear communication is a practical skill you'll use constantly, not just a soft-skill checkbox.

What this role demands from day one is attention to detail during turns, basic mechanical competence, customer service instincts, and the physical stamina for 8 to 10 hour shifts on your feet with lifts up to 75 lbs. What it builds over time is a sharper eye for preventive maintenance, a stronger sense of how curb appeal and unit condition directly affect occupancy and resident retention, and familiarity with the systems and standards a large third-party operator runs at scale. Technicians who develop those instincts often move into lead maintenance roles or Maintenance Supervisor positions as portfolios grow.

One honest note about the work: student and conventional multi-family properties tend to generate concentrated maintenance demand around turn season. At a community this size, a well-executed punch list and tight make-ready process matter more than most residents ever realize. Technicians who take pride in a unit being genuinely move-in ready, not just visually acceptable, are the ones who stand out here.

Qualifications

  • At least one year of relevant maintenance experience; property management background is a plus
  • Working knowledge of pool service and maintenance
  • Strong customer service skills and attention to detail
  • Ability to lift 75 lbs. and sustain 8 to 10 hour standing shifts

Compensation is $23.00 per hour. Benefits include health, vision, and dental insurance, 15 days of PTO, 10 paid holidays, paid parental leave, a 401(k) with up to 6% company match, short-term disability coverage, and continued education and professional development programs.

job.title: Business Manager (Property Manager) - Phoenix, AZ
job.description:
Most multifamily operators separate the financial stewardship of an asset from the day-to-day people management. The reality is those two things are inseparable, and the Business Manager role at Olympus Property is built around that truth. You're running the full operation: NOI, occupancy, team performance, and resident experience all sit on the same desk.

What the Role Actually Covers

Olympus uses the title "Business Manager" deliberately. This is a conventional Property Manager position in scope, but the framing reflects what they expect: someone who reads a T-12 with the same fluency they use to walk a punch list. You'll own the annual budget, monthly variance reporting, and business plan forecasts while keeping the Regional Manager and Regional VP informed on performance trends and strategy. On any given week, that might mean reviewing delinquency with your leasing team in the morning and negotiating a vendor contract in the afternoon.

The day-to-day also includes supervising both office and maintenance staff, which means you're accountable for the full cycle of the resident experience from traffic through renewal. Olympus places real emphasis on retention programs and renewal strategy, so if your instinct is to chase new leases rather than protect existing ones, that's worth reflecting on before applying. Market-ready unit condition and regular property inspections are part of the cadence here, not occasional checkboxes.

Luxury Class A experience is preferred, which signals the expectation around service standards, finish quality, and the kind of resident who has options and knows it.

What Olympus Brings to the Table

Olympus has earned recognition as a top employer through the National Apartment Association three consecutive years, which in our industry means their internal culture metrics hold up to outside scrutiny. They offer a compensation structure that includes base pay, monthly commissions, and quarterly and annual bonuses. The base range for this Phoenix role sits at $75,000 to $80,000, with the variable comp giving strong operators real upside.

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer matching, an apartment rental allowance, and tuition reimbursement. They also offer a sabbatical program and structured career pathing, including Budget Camp and leadership conferences, which is worth noting if you're a PM who wants to move toward a Regional role. That's typically where this position leads for high performers, and Olympus appears to build that ladder intentionally.

Who Fits This Role

  • Minimum two years of experience as a Property Manager in multifamily
  • Comfort with RealPage, Knock, or Onesite is strongly preferred
  • Available Monday through Friday with flexibility for resident events and emergencies outside standard hours
  • Able to lead a mixed team of leasing and maintenance staff without leaning too hard on either side

The candidates who tend to thrive in roles like this are the ones who don't need to be reminded that financial performance and resident satisfaction aren't competing priorities. They move between a budget spreadsheet and a community tour without losing a step. If you've managed a Class A asset and have the financial reporting experience to back it up, Phoenix is a market where Olympus has real presence and this role has real teeth.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Snoqualmie, WA
job.description:
It's 7 AM and a resident just flagged a leaking water heater before heading to work. By 8, you've assessed it, ordered the part, and updated the work order. That's the rhythm here.

The Work

Echo Ridge is a Berkshire-owned and managed community in Snoqualmie, WA, which means you're working for the owner, not a third-party fee manager. That distinction matters: decisions move faster, standards are consistent, and the property you maintain today is the same one the company plans to hold long-term.

As a Maintenance Technician, you carry a broad scope. Curb appeal, unit turns, make-ready punch lists, work orders across plumbing, electrical, appliances, and carpentry. You'll also help manage shop inventory, equipment upkeep, and key security. Safety compliance isn't a checkbox here; you're expected to actively enforce it. The role supports management directly, which means you'll occasionally be the first person a resident talks to when something goes wrong, and how you handle that interaction matters as much as the repair itself.

Berkshire uses the phrase "jack of all trades," and they mean it. A technician who gets tripped up by a tricky appliance diagnosis or a minor carpentry fix is going to struggle with the pace. The candidates who do well here have a working knowledge across all the core trades and enough confidence to triage a problem before escalating it.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of hands-on maintenance experience in a residential community setting
  • Practical knowledge of appliances, plumbing, electrical systems, carpentry, and general building maintenance
  • Comfort with computers and property management software for work order tracking
  • Strong written and verbal communication in English
  • A resident-first mindset, because this role is customer-facing whether you're fixing a garbage disposal or walking the grounds

One honest note about this market: Snoqualmie sits in the foothills east of Seattle, and Pacific Northwest winters are real. Exterior maintenance, drainage issues, and weather-related work orders pick up seasonally. If you've worked in wet climates before, that experience translates directly here.

Berkshire offers three weeks of vacation, a 25% rent discount, personal development plans, and solid insurance coverage. They're a nationally recognized residential investment firm with a track record of promoting from within. A strong technician who builds diagnostic depth and some supervisory presence often moves toward a Lead Tech or Maintenance Supervisor role over time.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Student housing runs on a different rhythm than conventional multifamily. Leases align with academic calendars, traffic spikes arrive in waves tied to housing fairs and move-in weekends, and the resident base turns over almost entirely each year. If you want to build leasing skills in that environment, this role at Redpoint West Lafayette gives you a concentrated education in all of it.

Skills This Role Requires From Day One

The Experience Team Member position draws heavily on interpersonal communication and adaptability. You'll conduct community and amenity tours, field objections from prospective residents (and their parents), and represent the property in conversations that happen both inside the office and around campus. That takes genuine customer-service instincts, not just a script. You'll also need to be organized enough to manage package logging, maintenance request follow-ups, and office operations without letting any of it slip. Scion calls this role a combination of marketing, relationship building, administration, and customer service, and that description is accurate. The workload shifts depending on the week, and availability during Turn periods and summer is a real requirement, not a footnote.

Skills This Role Builds Over Time

What you'll develop here goes beyond leasing basics. Working in student housing teaches you how to read traffic patterns against a leasing calendar, how to adjust messaging when occupancy targets aren't being met, and how to contribute to social media and local marketing in ways that actually connect with a collegiate audience. You'll learn to give useful feedback on sales barriers to your management team, which is a habit that sharpens your own understanding of why prospects don't convert. The after-hours on-call rotation, including lockout assistance, builds the kind of composure that carries into every future property management role you'll hold.

Student housing leasing also trains you to work through an annual lease-up cycle with a defined end date. That pressure is real, and learning to perform inside it makes conventional multifamily leasing feel more manageable by comparison.

What Makes This Specific Opportunity Worth Considering

Scion manages student communities across the country and has built operational systems around the particular demands of the collegiate market. Working at Redpoint West Lafayette means you're operating near a large Big Ten university with consistent demand, competitive traffic, and a resident base that expects amenities and experience to match their expectations. The role sits at the property full-time, so you'll develop real fluency with the community rather than splitting attention across a portfolio.

  • Strong candidates bring genuine curiosity about what drives leasing decisions, not just enthusiasm for talking to people
  • Reliability during high-demand periods (Turn, move-in, peak leasing season) is where this role is actually won or lost
  • Comfort with social media as a leasing tool is increasingly useful in this market segment

Applicants must be eligible to work in the United States. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Manager
job.description:
Maintenance management at an affordable housing portfolio demands a different skill set than luxury or market-rate work. The residents depend on fast, reliable service, and the operator depends on you to keep aging or mixed-vintage systems running efficiently without the budget latitude that Class A properties sometimes enjoy. At Fairstead, that challenge is real and so is the scale: over 30,000 apartments across 28 states, managed under a single integrated platform that combines development, construction, and property operations.

What This Role Actually Covers

The Service Manager position in Jacksonville puts you at the center of day-to-day building operations. You'll supervise a maintenance team, which means your organizational skills and ability to set priorities matter as much as your hands-on trade knowledge. You'll handle inspection and repair of electrical equipment and mechanical systems, lead special projects, and hold the line on safety compliance and sanitation standards across the property. Routine work you'll carry independently. More complex projects come with support.

Overtime is part of the picture when emergencies arise or special projects demand it. That's honest. Maintenance leadership at the property level means being reachable when systems fail outside business hours.

Skills You Bring vs. Skills You'll Sharpen

Fairstead requires at least three years of property maintenance experience and genuine proficiency in a specific trade, whether that's HVAC, electrical, plumbing, or another mechanical discipline. You also need working knowledge of building systems terminology, a real understanding of safety protocols, and comfort with Microsoft Office. Yardi and RealPage experience is a plus, not a requirement.

What this role builds is supervisory depth. Leading a team through a demanding make-ready cycle, managing a punch list across multiple units while keeping occupied buildings clean and safe, and implementing or improving maintenance procedures all develop the kind of operational judgment that carries well into regional maintenance director or facilities management positions over time.

  • Three or more years of hands-on property maintenance experience
  • Proficiency in at least one skilled trade with broad general maintenance ability
  • Strong safety knowledge and adherence to precautionary standards
  • Organizational and project management skills sufficient to lead a team
  • Ability to evaluate and improve existing maintenance policies and procedures
  • Microsoft Office proficiency; Yardi or RealPage familiarity is a bonus

The Broader Context

Fairstead positions itself as a tech-forward affordable housing operator, which matters for maintenance managers more than it used to. The company's emphasis on data-driven decision-making and digital tools means you'll likely encounter work order systems and reporting structures that go beyond a clipboard. Candidates who already think in terms of documentation, system performance trends, and process improvement tend to fit this environment better than those who rely purely on reactive repair habits.

The benefits package is substantive: employer-contributed medical coverage through Meritain Health, employer-paid vision and life insurance, a 401(k) with a 100% match on the first 3% and 50% on the next 2%, 15 PTO days, 7 sick days, and 12 or more paid holidays, along with a flexible spending account, disability coverage, and employee discount programs.

job.title: Housekeeper
job.description:
Housekeeping at a luxury apartment community covers more ground than most people expect. You're not just cleaning units. You're maintaining the standard that residents paid a premium to live within, and your work directly shapes how the property presents to prospects walking through on a tour.

What the Work Actually Involves

At Griffis Residential's Seattle community, the housekeeper role spans both common areas and apartment interiors. Common areas include the clubhouse, fitness center, business center, and leasing office. These spaces get daily attention, and the standard you hold them to reflects the property's overall brand. On the apartment side, you'll follow make-ready cleaning procedures using provided checklists to get units ready for incoming residents. If a ready unit has been sitting for more than a week, you'll return to refresh it so it stays move-in ready. You'll also communicate any maintenance issues you notice to the Service Manager, which makes you an extra set of eyes for the broader facilities team.

Daily tasks come from the Community and Service Managers, so you'll need to work comfortably within a structured schedule while also responding to what you find as you move through the property. Following product safety labels and cleaning protocols correctly matters here, both for resident safety and for protecting surfaces in a higher-finish environment.

Skills This Role Requires and Skills It Builds

You need to bring attention to detail, physical stamina, and at least a year of cleaning experience in multifamily housing, hospitality, or a comparable setting. Strong communication skills matter too, since you'll be interacting with residents and associates regularly. Bilingual ability in Spanish is a plus given Seattle's diverse resident base.

What this role builds is a working knowledge of the make-ready process and how turns function within a multifamily operation. That's a transferable skill. Housekeepers who understand make-ready standards, punch list thinking, and unit condition expectations are much better positioned to move into maintenance coordinator or make-ready technician roles over time. You're learning how a luxury property operates from the inside out.

Compensation and Benefits

The hourly range is $23 to $24.50. Full-time associates receive a 50% rental discount, a quarterly bonus program tied to occupancy and online reputation, 401(k) with up to 4% company match, medical, dental, and vision coverage, at least three weeks of PTO accruing from day one, 11 paid holidays, and tuition reimbursement up to $5,250 annually. The benefit package is notably more comprehensive than what most hospitality or hotel housekeeping roles offer at comparable pay.

  • High school diploma or equivalent required
  • One year of experience in multifamily, hospitality, or similar preferred
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to follow cleaning checklists and safety protocols
  • Clear communication skills; bilingual in Spanish is a plus
  • Ability to work within a team structure directed by Community and Service Managers

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
Maintenance Supervisor roles at student housing and multifamily companies tend to blend trade work with crew oversight more than most candidates expect. At PeakMade, the split is explicit: roughly 60 to 70 percent of your time is hands-on repairs, and the rest goes toward directing your team, managing vendors, and keeping the operation running on budget.

What the Job Actually Looks Like

This is a working supervisor position at an apartment community in Los Angeles. You're not managing from an office. You're on the property daily, inspecting grounds, completing or assigning service requests, and making sure vacant units are turned and ready for marketing. You'll run the turn process end to end: scheduling workers, supervising contractors, and pushing units through make-ready within budget. You'll also maintain the preventative maintenance program, manage supply inventory, and keep the maintenance shop organized and OSHA-compliant. When capital improvements come up, you'll work directly with the National Facilities Director to gather bids.

Resident interaction is part of the role. Move-ins, move-outs, unresolved concerns. You're expected to handle those professionally and without delay.

What PeakMade Needs From You

  • At least 2 years of maintenance supervisory experience, preferably in multifamily
  • EPA Type II certification required; CPO preferred
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Valid driver's license, current auto insurance, and a reliable personal vehicle
  • Must live within 30 miles of the property
  • Basic hand tools (your own)
  • Ability to diagnose and repair: HVAC, intermediate plumbing, intermediate electrical, major appliances, sheetrock, general carpentry, pool systems, roofing, painting, irrigation, and landscaping
  • Physical ability to lift up to 50 pounds, work at height on ladders, and perform tasks in extreme temperatures

Additional licenses or certifications may be required depending on local and state code. The posting notes other certifications as applicable by law, so candidates should be prepared for that review.

Compensation and Growth

The pay range is $80,000 to $90,000 annually, with final offers based on experience and internal equity. PeakMade includes monthly renewal bonuses, a 401(k) match, paid parental leave, 15 days PTO plus two wellbeing days, and access to a facilities leadership program with technical certifications available in HVAC and CPO.

That leadership program matters. Strong maintenance supervisors at companies like PeakMade often move into regional facilities roles or facilities director positions as they build out their portfolio experience and vendor management track record. The exposure to capex bidding here gives you a skill set that carries real weight at that next level.

PeakMade specializes in off-campus student housing, multifamily, and build-to-rent communities. The Los Angeles market means a dense regulatory environment, so comfort with local permitting, pool regulations, and sign ordinances is genuinely useful from day one.

job.title: Assistant Manager - Gainesville, GA
job.description:
The Skills This Role Puts to Work Every Day

An Assistant Manager role at a well-run apartment community is one of the best skill-building positions in residential property management. You're doing financial reconciliation, delinquency tracking, rent collection, and deposit accounting on one side of the desk. On the other, you're handling resident relations, inspecting make-ready units before move-in, and stepping into leasing when traffic demands it. That combination is exactly what trains people to run a property independently.

At Olympus Property's Gainesville community, the role asks for both precision and flexibility in the same week. You'll safeguard and accurately post incoming rent receipts, manage move-out account statements, and keep resident files airtight. You'll also monitor local submarket conditions, track nearby construction, and flag anything that could affect occupancy or income. That's a skill set that compounds: operators who understand both ledger accuracy and market positioning tend to move into Property Manager roles faster than those who specialize in only one.

What the Day-to-Day Actually Looks Like

Most of your core hours run Monday through Friday, 9 to 6, with some flexibility expected for the first weekend of each month and occasional resident events after hours. Practically speaking, mornings often involve posting deposits and clearing the prior day's transactions before the bank close deadline. Mid-day shifts toward resident touchpoints, whether that's addressing a complaint, walking a make-ready unit with a punch list in hand, or covering the leasing floor when a consultant is tied up. Late afternoon can pull you back to the books or into a conversation with the Property Manager about delinquency trends.

When the Property Manager is out, you run the operation. That exposure to full-site accountability, even temporarily, is something you can't replicate in a pure leasing role.

What Olympus Brings to This Position

Olympus Property has earned recognition as a top employer through the National Apartment Association three consecutive years running (2023, 2024, 2025). That's not accidental in a sector where turnover is notoriously high. The benefits package here is substantive, including medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer matching, tuition reimbursement, and an apartment rental allowance. There's also a formal career pathing program, which matters if your goal is to move from Assistant Manager to Property Manager and eventually into a regional or portfolio role.

Candidates who tend to succeed here bring onsite experience, either as an Assistant Manager or as a cross-trained leasing consultant, and familiarity with RealPage, Knock, or Onesite. Comfort with both detail-level financial work and face-to-face resident interaction is the combination Olympus looks for. If you've been strong on leasing but want to build the operational and financial side of your resume, this is a natural next step. If you're already handling books but want a company with defined growth tracks, Olympus is worth a close look.

job.title: Community Manager
job.description:
Hillpointe builds and manages workforce housing across the Sun Belt, and this Community Manager role sits at the center of that operation in Savannah. You'd be running a market-rate property from the ground up on the operational side: occupancy, financials, resident experience, and the daily coordination between maintenance and management. Because Hillpointe handles development, construction, and asset management in-house, community managers here tend to work closely with the broader organization rather than operating in isolation from ownership.

What the Day-to-Day Looks Like

A significant part of this role is keeping the asset performing the way ownership expects. That means regular property walks to catch issues before they become deferred maintenance problems, making sure units are genuinely make-ready standard before a new resident takes possession, and ensuring amenities stay in condition that reflects the property's positioning. You'll also manage accounts payable, submit invoices correctly, and support your Regional Manager in hitting and holding budgeted occupancy and rent levels.

On the leasing and revenue side, you're expected to stay active, not reactive. Identifying additional revenue opportunities, keeping concessions in check, and maintaining traffic conversion are all part of the job. Entrata experience is a real plus here since that's the platform Hillpointe works with, and comfort with spreadsheets and financial reporting is genuinely necessary rather than optional.

  • Oversee daily property operations and financial performance against budget
  • Coordinate with the Facilities Maintenance Group to address property-level needs
  • Manage vendor relationships and ensure proper invoice processing
  • Administer leases and maintain compliance with applicable regulations
  • Drive occupancy through leasing support, marketing strategy, and resident retention
  • Conduct routine property inspections and maintain asset standards

Who Fits This Role Well

Savannah's rental market has grown meaningfully over the past several years, with workforce housing demand driven by a mix of logistics, healthcare, and hospitality employment. Residents at properties like this often have specific expectations around value and responsiveness, and the managers who do well here are the ones who take both seriously. Strong candidates communicate clearly with residents and vendors alike, stay organized across multiple operational tracks at once, and bring genuine comfort with property management software and financial reporting. Prior community management experience gives you a real edge, but the combination of financial literacy, people skills, and operational follow-through matters more than any single credential.

Flexibility and Availability

This role requires a flexible schedule and consistent availability by phone and email outside of approved time off. Some local travel is expected for bank deposits, training, and business needs. Physical access to all areas of the community, including exterior spaces in varying weather, is part of the job. A valid driver's license is required.

For someone who wants to grow in multifamily operations, a vertically integrated developer like Hillpointe offers real exposure to how properties perform from the ownership side, which tends to accelerate the learning curve for managers who pay attention.

job.title: Centralized Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Centralized leasing roles differ from on-site positions in one key way: you're handling traffic and applications across multiple properties at once, not just one community. At Ackermann Group, a Midwest developer and manager with roots going back to 1938, this position sits at corporate headquarters in Cincinnati and covers leasing activity across their residential portfolio.

What the Work Looks Like

Your day runs from first contact to lease signed. Prospects reach you by phone or through digital channels, and your job is to convert those inquiries into tours and move-ins. You'll manage guest cards, prepare leases, track follow-ups, and document interactions in Yardi Voyager and Rent Cafe. The CRM is your paper trail, and keeping it accurate matters as much as your sales close rate.

Because you're covering multiple properties, product knowledge is a real requirement. You need to know unit counts, building specs, utility setups, and local market conditions well enough to speak to each community confidently and adjust your pitch accordingly. Fair housing compliance runs through every part of this job, from how you answer inquiries to how you document decisions.

You'll also field basic resident service needs, route work order requests, and support renewal conversations. It's a full-cycle leasing role with administrative depth. Occasional light physical tasks come with the territory.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of leasing experience with measurable results
  • Comfort working across Yardi Voyager, Rent Cafe, and CRM platforms
  • Strong written and verbal communication, with the ability to build rapport quickly
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Must live in the Greater Cincinnati area
  • Availability Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm, plus Saturdays as needed

The Bigger Picture

Centralized leasing is increasingly common as operators look to reduce per-property overhead while keeping leasing velocity up. The skill set you build here, managing volume across a portfolio, tracking leads in a CRM, and staying current on multiple micro-markets, transfers well to leasing manager and portfolio management roles. Ackermann offers commission on new leases and renewals, a quarterly bonus structure, health benefits, 401k with company match, and an employee rent discount at any community in their portfolio.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Enclave on Golden Triangle in Fort Worth needs a maintenance technician, and Cottonwood Residential is open to someone still building their skill set. This is a genuine entry point into apartment maintenance, which means you won't be expected to walk in knowing everything. You will be expected to show up, work hard, and learn fast.

The day-to-day work covers the full range of what keeps a residential community running: plumbing repairs, basic electrical, carpentry, and grounds upkeep. Turns and make-readies are part of the rhythm. You'll move through units on punch lists, respond to resident work orders, and handle the kind of repairs that pile up on a busy property. Some of it is satisfying problem-solving. Some of it is crawling into tight spaces or hauling materials in Texas summer heat. Both are real.

On-call is part of this role. After-hours emergencies happen, and you'll rotate into that coverage with support from the Service Manager. That support matters, especially early on, but you should go in knowing that the phone can ring at inconvenient times. That's the nature of residential maintenance, and it's worth being honest with yourself about before you apply.

Physically, the job asks a lot. You'll be on your feet most of the day, climbing ladders, stooping, kneeling, and lifting items up to 50 pounds. A valid driver's license is required. If you hold EPA Type II or Universal certification, or have HVAC troubleshooting experience, that carries real weight here. CPO certification is a plus as well, though none of these are hard requirements for an entry-level candidate.

What Cottonwood is looking for

  • Ability to communicate clearly in English, written and spoken, for work orders and safety procedures
  • Comfort working evenings, weekends, and on-call rotations
  • Physical ability to handle the demands described above
  • Valid driver's license
  • EPA Type II or Universal, HVAC experience, or CPO certification (preferred, not required)

Benefits kick in quickly, within the first month, and include full medical, vision, dental, life, and disability coverage. The 401k and HSA both come with company matching. In your first year you'd be eligible for three weeks of paid time off plus 10.5 paid holidays, which is a solid package for a technician role at this level.

For someone early in their maintenance career, this kind of role builds a foundation that transfers anywhere in the industry. Technicians who develop strong HVAC and plumbing skills at a community like this often move into lead tech or Service Manager roles within a few years. The learning curve is real, but so is the ceiling.

job.title: Temporary Maintenance Technicians Needed (Pittsburgh or Greensburg)
job.description:
Birgo manages residential properties across the Pittsburgh area, and right now they need a few extra sets of skilled hands to keep things running. These are temporary maintenance technician roles covering Greensburg, North Versailles, and the South Hills, with a realistic duration of one to three months. If things go well, there's room for the work to extend or convert to a full-time position.

The day-to-day work spans the full range of residential maintenance: make-readies, grounds upkeep, common area care, and general repairs covering drywall, painting, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, and HVAC. You'll also contribute to preventative maintenance routines. The schedule runs Monday through Friday, with shifts either 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. or 9:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., plus participation in an on-call rotation. Pay runs $19 to $24 per hour, paid weekly, and the role is overtime eligible. Mileage reimbursement, paid time off, and PPE are included.

Because you'll be moving between properties, a valid driver's license and your own reliable transportation are required. You'll also need to comfortably lift and carry 50 pounds, work in confined spaces, and handle ladders and staircases safely.

Temp roles like this one reward technicians who come in ready to contribute without a long ramp-up period. The people who tend to stand out are the ones who carry a genuinely broad skill set, communicate clearly when something unexpected comes up on a unit, and treat residents with the same care they'd give a full-time property. Birgo's culture puts a lot of weight on how people show up with each other and with residents, so attitude matters as much as technical range here.

What they're looking for

  • Authorization to work in the United States
  • Valid driver's license and personal, reliable transportation
  • Ability to lift 50 pounds unassisted and work safely with power tools
  • Comfort in confined spaces and on ladders
  • Well-rounded building maintenance skills across trades
  • Strong communication and resident-facing professionalism

If you've done residential maintenance work before and you're between positions or looking to pick up temporary work while you weigh your next move, this is a practical opportunity to stay active, earn competitive hourly pay, and get a real look at how Birgo operates before deciding if a longer-term fit makes sense.

job.title: Experienced Field Maintenance Technician- West Valley (3+ Years Required)
job.description:
Third-party property services at scale creates a different kind of maintenance career than traditional on-site work. Instead of owning one building, you own a portfolio of work orders across multiple properties, which means your diagnostic speed, organizational habits, and trade depth get tested daily in ways a single-site role rarely demands.

Lessen operates a tech-enabled platform that processes millions of work orders each year across residential and commercial real estate. Their field technicians in the West Valley are the ground-level execution layer for that model, and they're looking for someone in the Glendale area with at least three years of verifiable, hands-on maintenance experience who can carry that weight independently.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

This role puts you in a company fleet vehicle with a fuel card, moving through a defined territory and closing out work orders with an emphasis on quality over volume. You'll manage budgets tied to individual jobs, coordinate comprehensive maintenance across a portfolio of properties, and be expected to arrive on site already knowing your trade. Lessen provides OSHA training and a monthly tool and equipment allowance, but the expectation is that you bring the experience and problem-solving instincts. The schedule is weekday-only with no on-call rotation, which is a real structural difference from most maintenance positions in property management.

On the compensation side, the base rate starts between $24 and $27 per hour depending on your qualifications and skill depth. There's a $1,500 sign-on bonus, a quarterly discretionary bonus of up to 5% of quarterly earnings, plus the vehicle, fuel card, and monthly allowances for tools and a cell phone.

Where This Role Can Take You

The career path here is clearly defined: strong technicians move into Lead Technician roles, and from there into Field Maintenance Manager positions as Lessen expands nationally. That trajectory matters because the skills you build in a multi-property, work-order-driven environment translate well across the broader industry. Managing your own schedule, triaging jobs by priority, tracking spend against a budget, and maintaining documentation through a technology platform are exactly the competencies that separate senior technicians from those who plateau. Companies running scattered-site portfolios, single-family rental operators, and third-party managers all prize technicians who've worked in this model because the self-direction required is harder to teach than any specific trade skill.

  • Minimum 3 years of hands-on maintenance or related trade experience (verifiable)
  • Ability to manage work orders independently across multiple properties
  • Solution-oriented approach to scope and budget decisions in the field
  • Comfortable working within a tech platform for job tracking and communication
  • Based in or able to cover the West Valley / Glendale, AZ area

If you've spent years on a single property and want to see how your skills hold up across a real portfolio, this is the kind of role that answers that question fast.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Cielo
job.description:
A resident submits a work order at 8 AM: no hot water. By 9, you've diagnosed a faulty heating element, swapped it out, and updated the ticket in the system before the office team even opens their email. That rhythm, moving from diagnosis to resolution without a lot of hand-holding, is what this role runs on.

The Work at Cielo

Cielo is an Olympus Property community in Charlotte, and this full-time Maintenance Technician position runs Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 6 PM, with emergency availability when needed. You'll work alongside the Lead Maintenance Technician and the broader service team, handling the full scope of day-to-day repairs: HVAC maintenance and filter changes, plumbing repairs and fixture replacements, appliance work across refrigerators, washers, dryers, ovens, and stoves, electrical switches and fixtures, and lock changes or door repairs. Preventative maintenance on HVAC units, including coil cleaning, is a regular part of the calendar. You'll also help maintain grounds, common areas, and pool areas, and keep the maintenance shop organized and properly stocked. Work orders get tracked through property management software, so staying current on documentation matters as much as the wrench work.

The pay range starts at $24 to $25 per hour, with monthly and quarterly bonuses on top of base pay. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer matching, short and long-term disability, life insurance, paid time off, an apartment rental allowance, educational assistance, and pet insurance.

What Olympus Looks For

  • At least two years of maintenance experience in residential, apartment, or commercial settings
  • Working knowledge of HVAC systems; an EPA 608 certification or HVAC license is a plus
  • Hands-on comfort with plumbing, electrical, carpentry, painting, and appliance repair
  • Ability to operate hand tools and power tools safely and independently
  • Willingness to be available for emergency calls outside regular hours

Olympus has earned a spot on the National Apartment Association's Top Employer list for 2023, 2024, and 2025. That kind of recognition tends to reflect how a company treats people day to day, and the benefit package and bonus structure here back it up.

From a career standpoint, a role like this builds the kind of documented, multi-trade experience that moves technicians toward Lead Technician and eventually Service Manager positions. Technicians who develop strong HVAC diagnostic skills in particular tend to have real leverage in the market, since that competency is consistently hard for operators to find. Two or three years of solid work order history, good resident interaction habits, and a growing EPA certification puts you in a strong position for the next step up in portfolio management.

job.title: Maintenance Porter - Part-Time
job.description:
Curb appeal is one of the first things a prospective resident notices, and one of the last things a departing resident remembers. At a student housing community, where high turnover is built into the calendar and first impressions drive leasing traffic, the porter role carries real weight in how a property presents itself day to day.

Redstone Residential operates more than 38,000 beds across 20 states, with a portfolio that spans student housing and conventional multifamily. This part-time porter position sits within their Statesboro, Georgia community and pays $16.00 per hour, with a 401(k) plan that includes up to 6% employer matching.

What This Role Requires

The core of this position is maintaining cleanliness and safety across the property. That means common areas, hallways, the clubhouse, office, and model unit all need consistent attention. Outdoor grounds require regular upkeep: trash and debris removal, landscaping maintenance, watering, and keeping walkways and parking areas clear. You'll also assist with basic repairs and general maintenance tasks as needed.

The qualifications Redstone is looking for reflect the practical nature of the work:

  • Prior janitorial or cleaning experience in a relevant setting
  • Ability to work independently and complete daily tasks without close supervision
  • Comfortable standing for 4 to 6 hour shifts and able to lift 50 or more pounds
  • A genuinely friendly, team-oriented approach to the work

What This Role Builds

Porters who pay attention tend to become valuable eyes on the property. Because you're moving through common areas and grounds regularly, you're often the first to spot a maintenance issue before it becomes a work order, a safety hazard before it becomes a liability, or a resident concern before it escalates. That awareness, once developed, is directly transferable to make-ready and maintenance technician roles.

In student housing specifically, the porter role sharpens your ability to maintain quality under real time pressure. Turn season at a student property compresses a significant volume of work into a short window, and team members who've built strong independent work habits and understand property presentation standards are the ones who tend to move into broader maintenance responsibilities when those opportunities open up.

If you're early in a property management career and want to learn the physical side of operations from the ground up, this is a practical entry point with a company that manages at genuine scale.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Fairstead operates at a scale that most affordable housing owners don't reach: 30,000-plus units across 28 states, with development, construction, and property management all running under one roof. At the site level in Columbia, Maryland, that integration means the maintenance team is held to a professional standard that matches what you'd expect at a market-rate operation. This Service Manager role sits at the center of that.

What the Work Looks Like Day to Day

The title says Service Manager, and that's accurate. This is a working supervisor position. You'll carry tools and you'll also direct people. On a given day that might mean pulling an HVAC diagnosis in the morning, reviewing a punch list from a turn unit midday, and coaching a tech through a repair they haven't done solo before in the afternoon. Fairstead uses Yardi and RealPage on the operational side, so comfort with work order software matters, even if you're not running reports all day.

Core responsibilities include:

  • Supervising maintenance staff and taking point on special projects
  • Performing skilled repairs across mechanical, electrical, and general building systems
  • Maintaining the property's physical condition in line with Fairstead's safety standards
  • Working independently on routine work, escalating or pulling in help on more complex jobs
  • Occasional overtime for emergencies or project-driven needs

The company is explicit that they want someone with depth in at least one trade, not a generalist who knows a little about everything. Three years of property maintenance experience is the floor. If you've got a background in HVAC, electrical, or plumbing with solid general skills layered on top, that's the profile that tends to fit well here.

The Affordable Housing Context

Working for an affordable housing operator means the resident population often has fewer alternatives when something breaks. That's not a minor detail. The maintenance function carries real weight here, and a Service Manager who understands that tends to run a tighter, more responsive operation than one who treats it like any other multifamily gig. Fairstead's tech-forward approach also means you'll likely encounter digital work order systems and data tracking tools that some smaller operators haven't adopted yet. That's a skill that transfers well if you eventually move toward a portfolio-level or regional maintenance role.

Compensation and Benefits

The pay range for this position runs $23 to $25 per hour, depending on experience and location factors. Benefits include employer-contributed medical coverage through Meritain Health, employer-paid vision and life insurance, a 401(k) with a dollar-for-dollar match on the first 3% and 50% match on the next 2%, 15 PTO days, 7 sick days, and 12 or more paid holidays. Flexible spending accounts, disability coverage, and pet insurance round out the package.

Fairstead is an equal opportunity employer and considers diversity in background and experience a genuine operational asset, not just a policy statement.

job.title: Leasing Manager
job.description:
A Role Built on Sales Skill and Market Awareness

Leasing at a mixed portfolio site takes more than a friendly tour. At Prentiss Pointe Apartments and The Reserve, a new construction single-family homes community in Harrison Township, you're working two distinct product types simultaneously. That means reading prospects quickly, matching them to the right option, and closing consistently. Paragon Properties is looking for a Leasing Manager who brings real closing discipline, a 40 to 50 percent closing ratio is the expectation, not an aspiration, along with the analytical habits to track traffic patterns, monitor renewal pipelines, and run competitive market surveys monthly.

The Macomb County rental market sits in an interesting spot. Harrison Township draws renters who often compare it against options further up the lakeshore corridor or back toward Eastpointe and Roseville. Knowing your comp set cold, running monthly phone shops and quarterly in-person shops, matters here because prospects in this submarket do their homework. The Leasing Manager owns that competitive intelligence function directly.

Day-to-Day Responsibilities

The core of this role covers the full leasing cycle: touring market-ready units and models, reviewing and processing applications, managing the CRM queue, coordinating move-in orientations, and verifying renters insurance compliance at move-in. Beyond individual leasing, you'll manage lease expiration timelines, prepare weekly occupancy reports for operations and the Regional Manager, and actively work the renewal process alongside the property manager.

Marketing ownership is a real part of this position. You'll plan and execute site-level advertising, manage Facebook and Instagram presence, send weekly eblasts, and conduct outreach to local businesses and employers. Resident event planning also falls here. On the operational side, you'll enter service requests into Yardi, assist with market-ready unit inspections, and flag deficiencies before they become liabilities.

You'll also lead the leasing staff directly: running marketing meetings, coaching closing ratios, and modeling the professional standards Paragon expects across prospect and resident interactions.

What Strong Candidates Bring

  • At least one year of on-site leasing or assistant manager experience, with demonstrated sales performance
  • Yardi proficiency or comfort picking it up quickly
  • Solid working knowledge of Fair Housing guidelines at the federal, state, and local level
  • Strong written communication for CRM follow-up, eblasts, and social content
  • Experience running comp shops and translating that data into pricing or marketing adjustments
