  • High school diploma required; college-level coursework strongly preferred

Candidates who stand out at this level typically combine consistent closing performance with genuine comfort in a coaching role. If you've only ever been an individual contributor in leasing, the shift to managing and motivating a team while still carrying your own closing expectations is the adjustment that trips most people up. Coming in with some experience leading peers, even informally, puts you ahead.

Compensation runs up to $24 per hour depending on experience, with monthly move-in bonuses, quarterly renewal bonuses, and a benefits package that includes medical, dental, and optical coverage with a short waiting period, company-paid life and disability insurance, a 401(k) with employer contribution, paid holidays, and a rent discount.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Technician
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role puts you at the center of daily property operations at a Fairstead affordable housing community in Virginia Beach. Your week will include scheduled preventative maintenance on building systems, responding to resident work orders, and handling the turns between move-out and move-in. Make-readies are a real part of the job: cleaning and prepping vacated units so they're genuinely ready for incoming residents, not just surface-clean. You'll inspect electrical systems for code compliance, test safety devices monthly, maintain a working inventory of tools and supplies, and participate in the on-call rotation for after-hours emergencies. That last part is worth taking seriously. On-call is a real responsibility here, and the role rewards technicians who stay calm and organized when the phone rings at 10pm.

Fairstead operates as an integrated owner, operator, and developer across more than 30,000 units in 28 states, which means the maintenance function connects directly to a larger platform. Work orders, inspections, and inventory aren't just local tasks; they feed into data systems that help the organization track asset performance at scale. Technicians who document carefully and communicate clearly make a measurable difference in how well that system works.

What You Bring

  • Hands-on experience in a service technician or general maintenance role
  • Working knowledge of electrical systems: diagnosis and minor repairs
  • Mechanical aptitude across plumbing, appliances, and building fixtures
  • Physical capability to stand for extended periods and lift up to 70 pounds unassisted
  • Clear written and verbal communication, because work order notes and handoff logs matter
  • HVAC certification (EPA 608, CMRP, or equivalent) is preferred and will strengthen your candidacy
  • Attention to detail, especially on punch list items during make-readies and safety inspections

Skills This Role Builds

If you're early in your maintenance career, this position develops real breadth. Affordable housing properties typically run leaner than Class A market-rate communities, which means technicians here handle a wider range of work rather than specializing narrowly. You'll build competency across electrical, plumbing, HVAC, and unit turns. That breadth is exactly what companies look for when promoting to Lead Technician or Maintenance Supervisor. Technicians who combine strong trade skills with solid documentation habits, and who treat resident communication as part of the job rather than an interruption, tend to move up quickly in organizations like Fairstead that operate at scale. If you want to grow into a supervisory role, the exposure you get here is genuinely useful.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
Maintenance supervisors in multifamily carry a split job. Part of the day is hands-on work. The other part is managing people, vendors, and schedules. PeakMade puts that split in writing: 60 to 70 percent of this role is direct repair and maintenance work, and the rest is supervision and coordination. If you want a pure desk job, this isn't it. If you want to stay in the field while building leadership experience, the structure fits.

What the Work Looks Like

This position covers a conventional apartment community in Olathe, Kansas. You'll own the service request queue: prioritizing, assigning, tracking completion, and stepping in to finish work when the team needs it. Daily property walks keep curb appeal and liability concerns in check. You'll also run the preventative maintenance program, manage shop inventory inside budget, and keep the maintenance space organized and OSHA-compliant.

Turn coordination is a real part of the job. You'll schedule and direct the team through make-ready cycles, supervise vendors and contractors during turns, and ensure vacant units are restored and ready for marketing. Unit inspections happen monthly. You'll also work with the Property Manager on budget performance and connect with the National Facilities Director when capital improvement bids are needed.

Technical scope includes HVAC, intermediate plumbing, intermediate electrical, appliances, carpentry, sheetrock, roofing, gutters, painting, irrigation, and landscaping. Pool care and small engine maintenance may apply depending on the community. EPA Type II certification is required before you start. CPO is preferred.

What PeakMade Needs From You

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • At least 2 years of maintenance supervisory experience, multifamily preferred
  • EPA Type II certification required; CPO preferred
  • Valid driver's license, current auto insurance, and your own reliable vehicle
  • Must live within 30 miles of the property
  • Basic hand tools supplied by you, not the community
  • Ability to lift up to 50 pounds, work at heights, and perform physical tasks in outdoor temperatures above 90 or below 32 degrees

PeakMade operates student housing, multifamily, and build-to-rent communities across the country. This role sits in their multifamily portfolio. Candidates who do well in this type of position tend to be strong diagnosticians who can also communicate clearly with residents and hold contractors accountable during turns. The leadership piece matters as much as the technical piece once you're in the supervisor seat.

Benefits include PTO, wellbeing days, 401(k) match, paid parental leave, technical certification support for HVAC and CPO, monthly renewal bonuses, and a facilities leadership development program for those who want to move up.

job.title: Leasing Consultant - Portland Oregon
job.description:
The leasing consultant role sits at the front edge of a property's revenue. Every lease signed, every prospect converted, every renewal retained flows through this position first. At Karya Property Management's Portland-area community, that responsibility belongs to you.

What You'll Actually Do

Your day centers on converting traffic into signed leases. That means greeting prospects, walking them through the property, and presenting the community's features in a way that connects to what they're actually looking for in a home. You'll explain lease terms clearly, including the TAA Lease Contract, so future residents understand exactly what they're signing before move-in day arrives.

Beyond the initial sale, you'll coordinate move-in packets, prepare units, and manage the day-of experience for incoming residents. You'll also do at least one full property walk daily to assess curb appeal and flag anything that needs attention before a prospect sees it. Resident events and marketing coordination fall into this role as well, so there's a creative side alongside the sales work.

Weekend and evening availability on a rotating schedule is part of the job. Leasing traffic doesn't follow a Monday-through-Friday pattern, and the strongest consultants treat weekend shifts as opportunities rather than inconveniences.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma or equivalent required; a college degree is preferred
  • Clear, confident verbal and written communication skills
  • Strong customer service instincts with residents, prospects, and vendors
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office, Word, and Outlook
  • A sense of urgency and the ability to manage competing deadlines
  • Physical ability to walk the property daily, climb stairs, and lift up to 15 pounds

Skills This Role Builds

A leasing consultant role is where most property management careers start, and for good reason. You'll develop a working command of lease administration, fair housing compliance, and the full prospect-to-resident lifecycle. The objection-handling and closing skills you build here translate directly into assistant manager and property manager roles, where leasing performance becomes one of several metrics you're responsible for rather than your primary focus. Consultants who learn to read traffic patterns, track their own closing ratios, and take ownership of curb appeal tend to move up faster because they're already thinking like operators.

What separates a strong candidate here is the ability to hold a genuine conversation with a prospect while staying accurate on lease terms and community details. The sales piece matters, but residents who feel well-informed at move-in create fewer headaches down the line and renew at higher rates. If you bring that combination of warmth and precision, this is a solid place to build the foundation of a property management career.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Technician - Verdant Peachtree Creek
job.description:
Maintenance work in multifamily housing covers a wide range of skill levels, and this role at AIR Communities' Verdant Peachtree Creek community in Atlanta sits squarely in the hands-on technical tier. You'll carry out resident service requests, complete turns to get units ready for incoming residents, and handle routine upkeep across plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliances, and carpentry. The expectation is that you're already proficient in at least two of those trades and can move through work orders independently with general direction rather than constant supervision.

What this role builds on top of that foundation is real breadth. Because community needs shift by season and by what mechanical systems are in play, you won't spend every week doing the same two tasks. One stretch might be weighted toward HVAC as summer leasing ramps up; another might call for more appliance work and punch list completion during a turn cycle. Technicians who stay curious about the trades they're weaker in tend to develop faster here than those who stay in their lane.

AIR uses technology to manage task flow and prioritization, which means you'll work with digital tools to track and close out work orders rather than relying on paper logs or verbal handoffs. That's worth knowing if you're coming from a smaller operation where systems were informal. The upside is that organized shops and stocked supplies are part of the model, so you spend less time hunting for parts and more time actually fixing things.

The role pays $23.00 to $26.00 per hour depending on your experience and trade skill level, and there's a quarterly customer service bonus structure that can add up to $250 per month for technicians who consistently earn strong resident satisfaction scores. A 50% rent discount at any AIR community is also available, which matters if you want to eliminate your commute by living onsite.

What you'll need coming in

  • At least two years of maintenance experience in a facilities or building environment
  • Proficiency in two or more trades: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliance repair, carpentry
  • Willingness to work flexible hours including evenings, weekends, and on-call shifts (roughly one week per month)
  • Reliable transportation for after-hours emergency response
  • Physical ability to move heavy equipment and machinery as needed

One thing worth understanding about on-call in multifamily: it's not decorative. Residents call when something fails, and that includes nights and weekends. If you've done on-call before, you already know how to triage what's urgent versus what can wait until morning. If you haven't, that judgment develops quickly and it's one of the more transferable skills this role gives you, applicable at any property type or ownership structure you work for later in your career.

AIR's internal development program, Ascend, is designed to map a path forward based on where you want to go, whether that's a lead technician role, a service manager position, or something more specialized. The company has a stated preference for internal promotion, so the ceiling here is higher than the job title suggests.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Prelude at the Park
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

Prelude at the Park is a 200-plus unit community in Henderson, and this role covers the full range of day-to-day maintenance operations. That means working through the service request queue, handling turns and make-readies, and keeping grounds, common areas, and office spaces clean and presentable. You'll do appliance repairs, plumbing, electrical, HVAC work, and painting. You're also on the on-call rotation, so after-hours emergencies are part of the deal. If you've done apartment maintenance before, none of this is a surprise.

Henderson runs hot. HVAC calls in summer aren't occasional, they're relentless. A technician who can diagnose and repair A/C units without waiting on a vendor is genuinely valuable here, and that skill will get used constantly from May through September.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of hands-on apartment maintenance experience, preferably on a property of 200 units or more
  • Working knowledge across trades: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliance repair, and general carpentry
  • A customer service orientation. Residents notice how you communicate, not just whether the work order got closed
  • Reliable transportation. This is a hard requirement, not a suggestion
  • Flexibility for on-call rotation and the ability to function well in a team setting

The Company and the Role in Context

MG Properties has been acquiring and managing apartment communities across the Western U.S. for over 30 years. They're a regional operator with real depth, which matters for a maintenance tech. You're not walking into a small outfit where the maintenance program is held together with good intentions. There's structure, there's process, and there's a benefits package that reflects a company that's been doing this long enough to know that retaining good maintenance staff requires more than a paycheck.

Compensation is experience-based, and the package includes monthly bonuses, company profit sharing, a 401k with employer match, and full medical, dental, and vision coverage. PTO, paid holidays, paid personal days, paid sick time, and a rental discount round it out.

For technicians thinking about where this role leads: solid multi-trade experience on a property this size is exactly the background that feeds into lead tech and maintenance supervisor positions. If you're consistent, organized, and residents actually like dealing with you, that path tends to open up faster than people expect.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager (Fetters, Celestina Gardens)
job.description:
A resident stops by the office to sort out a documentation issue before her annual recertification appointment. You pull her file, walk her through what's needed, and schedule a follow-up. That kind of interaction is the center of gravity for this role at Fetters and Celestina Gardens, two affordable communities in Sonoma managed by MidPen Housing.

What This Role Covers Day to Day

MidPen has operated affordable housing across Northern California since 1970, and their property management teams carry real weight in that mission. As Assistant Community Manager, you report to the Community Manager and share responsibility for keeping two properties running with care and precision.

The compliance side of this work is substantial. Affordable housing operates under layered regulatory requirements, and this role touches all of them: income verifications, lease preparation, waitlist management, and assistance with recertifications, welfare exemptions, MOR reviews, and TCAC compliance. If you've worked in affordable housing before, you already know how carefully these processes need to be tracked. If you're coming from general residential property management, expect a meaningful learning curve on the compliance side, and plan to invest time in it.

Beyond compliance, the role covers rent collection, security deposit processing, petty cash logs, and bank deposit preparation. You'll also schedule vacancies, prepare and monitor turn forms, coordinate maintenance inspections with facilities staff, and make sure work orders move through the system without stalling. Regular property inspections keep you connected to physical conditions on the ground, and you'll maintain resident and property files with appropriate confidentiality throughout.

Resident relations here go beyond collecting rent and issuing notices. MidPen's Resident Services team works alongside property management, which means the people living at these communities have real support structures around them. Your job includes communicating emergency preparedness procedures, coordinating resident meetings, and maintaining working relationships with local law enforcement and emergency agencies.

What MidPen Is Looking For

  • High school diploma or GED, plus at least one year of residential property management, customer service, or administrative experience (or an equivalent combination)
  • Proficiency in MS Office; experience with RealPage is a plus
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Organized, detail-oriented, and able to manage multiple tasks with minimal supervision
  • Genuine alignment with MidPen's mission of providing stable, dignified housing to people who need it

Candidates who stand out in affordable housing roles at this level tend to be people who take compliance seriously without losing warmth in their resident interactions. The recertification process can feel bureaucratic from the outside, but handled well, it's one of the most direct ways a property team keeps residents housed and stable. That dual focus, accuracy and relationship, is what separates strong candidates from those who struggle.

Pay ranges from $21.15 to $23.80 per hour based on experience. MidPen offers a benefits package that includes health, dental, vision, life and disability insurance, a 403(b) retirement plan, paid parental leave, employee education reimbursement, FSA options, an EAP, pet insurance, paid time off, company holidays, and wellness days.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - West Loop
job.description:
It's 10 a.m. on a Tuesday and the punch list already has six items: a resident reported low water pressure in 4B, the lobby trash needs a run, and a vendor is arriving at noon to rod a sewer line you scheduled last week. That's a normal start to this role.

The Work Itself

Reside Living manages roughly 3,000 apartments across Chicago, and this position supports one of their West Loop properties. You'll report directly to the Building Engineer and carry out the hands-on maintenance work that keeps the building operating and residents satisfied. That means completing service requests within agreed SLAs, performing janitorial and grounds work when needed, and assisting with apartment turns between residents. Seasonal responsibilities are real here: Chicago winters require snow removal equipment operation, and you'll be expected to handle that without being told twice.

Preventative maintenance is a core part of the schedule. You'll coordinate HVAC filter replacements, sewer line rodding, and other recurring tasks before they become emergencies. When water infiltration or mold appears, you treat it with urgency and escalate appropriately. You'll also coordinate vendor and contractor access, working alongside project management staff on larger capital work.

The schedule runs Tuesday through Saturday, 10 a.m. to 6:30 p.m., with on-call availability for after-hours emergencies. This is a full-time hourly position at $25.00 per hour. A $50 monthly phone stipend is included, since you'll use a mobile app to document completed work orders and inspections.

What This Role Requires and What It Builds

Coming in, you need between two and five years of maintenance experience in a residential, hospitality, or institutional setting. Mechanical aptitude across plumbing, electrical, HVAC, and hot water systems is preferred, and EPA certification is required (or must be obtained within 90 days). You'll need to be comfortable with hand and power tools, measuring devices, and mechanical equipment like pumps, compressors, and augers. A valid driver's license is preferred.

Strong candidates distinguish themselves through two things that don't appear on any tool list: communication and follow-through. You're interfacing with residents daily, coordinating with vendors, and keeping the Building Engineer informed. The technicians who advance in this kind of role are the ones who close the loop without being asked.

  • High school diploma or equivalent required
  • EPA certification required or obtained within 90 days of hire
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office and mobile work order systems
  • Ability to be on your feet 66 to 100 percent of the time; full physical demands apply
  • OSHA safety compliance required, including appropriate PPE for each task
  • Personal smartphone (iOS or Android) required; $50/month stipend provided

For a technician looking to grow, this role offers a clear path. Working directly under a Building Engineer gives you exposure to building systems at a scale that builds the diagnostic thinking you need to eventually move into an engineer or facilities manager role. Reside Living's expanding Chicago portfolio means internal mobility is a realistic outcome for performers who demonstrate reliability and technical range.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Santa Ana is a competitive submarket, and a 288-unit community doesn't run on autopilot. Property Management Associates is looking for a leasing consultant who can do more than hand out floor plan brochures: someone who closes, follows up, and understands that traffic converts when the experience is right from the first phone call through the lease signing.

PMA has been operating in the greater Los Angeles area for over 30 years, managing both residential and commercial assets across Southern California. They run a full-service shop, which means the infrastructure is there. This is an in-office, on-site role. One weekend day is part of the schedule.

The day-to-day looks like this: you're touring prospects, walking the community, handling applications, and pushing leases through to execution. You're also supporting marketing efforts, which in this market means social media and online platforms matter as much as signage. Yardi Voyager experience is a plus, and if you've already got time logged in Voyager, say so clearly on your resume.

Compensation runs $20 to $23 per hour, with lease commissions on top: $100 per new lease, $50 per renewal. For a 288-unit property with normal turnover, that commission structure adds up. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, life insurance with an employer contribution, 401(k) after one year, short- and long-term disability, and a PTO package covering vacation, holidays, and sick time.

What they're looking for

  • At least one year of leasing experience
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills
  • Comfort with the full application and lease signing process
  • Familiarity with online and social media marketing for rentals
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office; Yardi Voyager a plus
  • Availability to work one weekend day per week

What separates a good leasing consultant from a forgettable one at a property this size is follow-through. Plenty of people can give a decent tour. Fewer actually track their leads, re-engage cold prospects, and close the ones who "need to think about it." If your leasing history shows consistent occupancy contribution rather than just activity, that's the story worth telling here.

job.title: Leasing Manager
job.description:
Student housing leasing has its own rhythm. Lease-up cycles compress into short windows, renewals require early and consistent outreach, and traffic management demands both speed and warmth. The Leasing Manager role at Redstone Residential in Kent, Ohio sits squarely inside that rhythm, supporting the Community Manager across daily operations while owning the leasing function as its primary focus.

Redstone is one of the larger third-party student housing operators in the country, managing over 38,000 beds across 20 states. Their Kent property is part of a growing conventional portfolio alongside their student housing base, which means this role carries real operational weight at the community level.

What This Role Requires

The Leasing Manager handles the full leasing cycle: prospect calls, property tours, email follow-up, and renewal campaigns. You'll work inside Entrata's leasing workflow, manage online and social marketing touchpoints, and apply basic SEO thinking to the property's digital presence. Resident ledger accuracy falls under this role as well, so comfort with numbers and attention to detail on account balances matter. Customer service and sales skill aren't incidental here. They're the core of the job.

  • Strong customer service and sales instincts, especially under volume
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office, Gmail, Google Drive, and Dropbox
  • High school diploma or GED required; some college experience is preferred
  • Ability to stay organized and composed during high-traffic leasing periods

What This Role Builds

Leasing Manager is one of the clearest development paths in property management. The skills you'll sharpen here, running leasing strategy, motivating a team around occupancy goals, keeping delinquency in check, and reading what's working in your marketing mix, translate directly into Community Manager readiness. You'll also get exposure to budget performance and staff administration, which are disciplines most pure leasing consultant roles don't touch.

Working inside a large third-party management platform like Redstone's gives you something smaller operators can't: standardized systems, professional development programming, and a continued education benefit that rewards people who want to grow. The 401K match (up to 6%), paid parental leave, and 15 days of PTO round out a compensation structure that reflects a company building for retention, not just filling seats.

The position pays $18.00 per hour and is classified full-time, non-exempt. If you have a feel for leasing, enjoy working with people, and want to develop the operational skills that move careers forward in property management, this is a role worth taking seriously.

job.title: Maintenance Tech
job.description:
Maintenance work at a student housing or build-to-rent community is a different animal than a conventional apartment. Turnover is aggressive, resident expectations run high, and the technician on the ground sets the standard for how well the physical asset performs. PeakMade Real Estate is hiring a Maintenance Technician for their Indianapolis community, and the role sits at the center of daily operations.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Most of your days will involve completing service requests across mechanical, plumbing, electrical, and appliance systems. You'll follow a preventative maintenance schedule, keep chemical logs for the pool, and help coordinate turns when units flip between residents. Curb appeal, breezeway cleanliness, and the condition of common areas all fall within your scope. You'll also carry a share of the on-call rotation, which means after-hours calls are part of the job. That's worth stating plainly: this role requires flexibility with scheduling, including weekends and holidays.

Inventory management is part of the technician's responsibility here too. Working alongside the Maintenance Supervisor, you'll help track tools, parts, and supplies, and you'll be expected to flag shortages before they create delays. Budget awareness matters, not just wrench-turning.

What You Bring vs. What You'll Build

This role requires at least one year of maintenance experience, ideally in the apartment industry. You'll need the ability to troubleshoot and repair HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliances without supervision on routine calls. EPA Type I and II certification is preferred, and you'll need to supply your own hand tools. Reliable transportation and the ability to live within 30 miles of the property are non-negotiable given the on-call structure.

What the role builds is different. PeakMade offers HVAC and CPO certification support, a facilities leadership program, and ongoing technical training. For a technician who's solid on the fundamentals but wants a clear path toward a Maintenance Supervisor or Facilities Manager role, this structure gives you a visible track. The monthly renewal bonuses also reward quality work in a measurable way, which keeps skill-building tied directly to compensation.

Who Performs Well Here

  • Technicians who communicate proactively with residents and supervisors, not just complete the ticket and move on
  • People who treat make-ready turns with the same care as a standard service call
  • Anyone who's comfortable working outdoors in both summer heat and winter cold without cutting corners on safety
  • Candidates who understand that in student housing, occupancy and resident satisfaction are directly tied to how fast and how well maintenance responds

PeakMade is an Atlanta-based company with a portfolio spanning student housing, multifamily, and build-to-rent communities. Their culture leans collaborative and team-driven, and the Indianapolis position reflects that. If you've been doing solid maintenance work and want a company that invests in certifications and career structure, this is a role worth a close look.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - 50% Rent Discount
job.description:
Vaughan Place sits just off Wisconsin Avenue in the Cathedral Heights neighborhood, a 380-plus-unit luxury community within easy reach of Georgetown, Embassy Row, and Glover Archbold Park. AIR Communities operates it as part of a portfolio of Class A assets in major markets, and they run a tight ship on the maintenance side. This is a full-time technician role, not a light-duty position. You'll be doing turns, handling resident service requests, troubleshooting HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and appliances, and occasionally guiding less experienced techs on the team.

The pay range runs $24 to $27 an hour depending on your actual skill set, with the possibility of up to $250 per month in customer satisfaction bonuses tied to resident feedback. The 50% rent discount applies at any AIR community, so you can live on-site and eliminate your commute entirely, or pick a different AIR property nearby. That's a real benefit in a market like DC, where rent levels are what they are.

AIR has invested in technology to help technicians prioritize work orders and move through the day more efficiently. Shops are stocked and organized. They've also built out a maintenance development program called Ascend, which is designed around individual career paths rather than a generic training checklist. For a technician who wants a clear line toward a lead or maintenance supervisor role, that structure matters.

What They're Looking For

  • At least two years of maintenance experience in a facilities or building environment
  • Proficiency in at least two trades: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliance repair, or carpentry
  • Availability for evenings, weekends, and on-call shifts (roughly one week per month)
  • A reliable way to get to the property for after-hours emergency calls
  • Physical capability to handle heavy equipment and machinery

On-call is the part of this job that tends to separate people who last from people who don't. One week a month of after-hours availability is the stated expectation, and at a luxury community with residents who expect quick responses, that's a real commitment. If you've worked in multifamily before, you already know this. If you're coming from commercial facilities, the pace of resident-facing service requests is a different rhythm than scheduled PMs.

The technicians who perform well in roles like this one tend to be the people who genuinely close out a work order correctly the first time, document it properly, and communicate with the resident before and after. At a Class A property, the service standard is high and residents notice when it slips. The customer satisfaction bonus structure reflects exactly that expectation.

Benefits include a 401(k) with up to 6% employer match, medical, dental, and vision coverage, company-paid short and long-term disability, 14 paid holidays, paid parental leave up to 16 weeks, and tuition reimbursement up to 100% for job-related certifications and licenses. That last piece is worth noting if you're working toward an HVAC certification or EPA 608 and haven't finished it yet.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
A Role Built on Relationship Skills and Market Instincts

Student housing runs on a different rhythm than conventional multifamily. Lease-up cycles compress into a few intense months, traffic spikes around campus visit weekends, and your prospects are often making their first major housing decision without much experience. The Leasing Consultant role at The Reserve at Clemson puts you at the center of that dynamic, and the skills it develops compound quickly across a property management career.

The core of this position is sales, but the kind of sales that requires genuine relationship-building rather than a pitch script. You'll tour prospects through the community, field objections, and report back to management on what's actually stopping people from signing. That feedback loop matters. Consultants who can articulate why a prospect walked, and what messaging might have changed the outcome, develop market instincts that carry into leasing manager and assistant manager roles faster than those who just track traffic numbers.

Beyond the leasing floor, you'll handle property administration work: package management, office organization, maintenance request coordination, and after-hours lockout coverage. These aren't filler tasks. Understanding how a property runs operationally, from the front office through to maintenance follow-up, gives you a much clearer picture of NOI and resident satisfaction than leasing alone ever would.

What This Role Demands Week to Week

Student housing has defined pressure points, and availability during those periods is a real requirement here. Turn periods, when an entire community flips occupancy in a matter of days between academic terms, are intense and all-hands. Summer is peak leasing season. Holidays require coverage. If your schedule can flex to meet those demands, you'll get exposure to operational complexity that most entry-level roles never offer.

Marketing is also a meaningful part of this position. You'll contribute to social media, help plan and execute resident engagement events, and identify local outreach opportunities near the Clemson campus. Student housing communities compete hard for the same pool of prospects each year, and the consultants who understand both the digital and in-person sides of that effort tend to move up.

What Strong Candidates Bring to This Role

  • A customer-first mindset that stays consistent even on high-volume days
  • Strong verbal communication across a genuinely diverse resident and prospect population
  • Self-discipline and reliability, especially for on-call and after-hours responsibilities
  • Comfort with a schedule that shifts based on leasing season and campus calendar
  • Some familiarity with social media platforms used for community engagement

Scion operates specifically in the student housing segment, which means the institutional knowledge you'd build here is specialized and transferable to any university-adjacent market. For someone early in a property management career, that specialization is an asset worth developing.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Skills at the Center of This Role

Maintenance work at a residential property draws on a surprisingly wide skill set, and this position at Fairstead puts most of them to use. Electrical diagnosis, HVAC systems, preventative maintenance planning, make-ready prep for turns, and safety compliance all show up regularly. If you've spent time as a service technician and found yourself handling whatever came through the door, this role will feel familiar in the best way. The breadth is the point.

Fairstead manages more than 30,000 apartments across 28 states as an integrated owner and operator, which means the people maintaining their properties work within a system that connects development, construction, and property management under one roof. That structure matters for a technician because decisions move faster and resources tend to be more accessible than in third-party management environments.

What You'll Be Building Day to Day

The core of the role covers routine inspections of buildings and equipment, identifying what needs repair before it becomes an emergency. You'll carry out preventative maintenance on schedule, respond to work orders, and handle turns: cleaning and prepping vacated units so they're ready for incoming residents. Electrical checks, safety system testing, and maintaining inventory of tools and supplies round out the regular work. You'll also participate in an on-call rotation, which means some after-hours emergency response is part of the job. That's worth knowing upfront.

Preferred credentials include HVAC certification or a CMRP designation, and the physical demands are real: standing for extended periods and lifting up to 70 pounds unassisted. Attention to detail and solid communication skills matter too, especially when coordinating with property management staff or documenting completed work.

Where This Role Tends to Lead

For technicians thinking about trajectory, a role like this one builds a skill profile that translates directly into lead maintenance or maintenance supervisor positions. The combination of hands-on systems knowledge, preventative maintenance discipline, and experience working within a professionally managed affordable housing portfolio carries weight. Operators at Fairstead's scale run structured systems, so technicians who learn to work within those systems, and contribute to improving them, tend to move up faster than those in smaller, less formalized environments.

What separates strong candidates here is the blend of technical range and reliability. Electrical competence combined with HVAC knowledge is a meaningful differentiator in affordable housing maintenance. Operators at this scale can't afford single-skill technicians. The more systems you can confidently touch, the more valuable you become to the team and the more options you create for yourself down the road.

job.title: Experienced Field Maintenance Technician (3+ Years Required)
job.description:
What This Role Actually Involves

Field maintenance at a tech-enabled property services company operates differently than a traditional apartment maintenance role. Instead of being tied to a single asset or a handful of buildings, you're working across a portfolio, managing your own work orders through a platform that tracks scope, completion, and quality at scale. Lessen runs more than 3.5 million work orders annually across over one million properties, so the infrastructure around you is substantial. Your job is to show up as a skilled technician who can own the work from diagnosis to close-out without needing a supervisor to walk you through it.

Skills Required and Skills Built

Three years of verifiable, hands-on experience in property maintenance or a related trade is the floor here, not a soft suggestion. You need to arrive with working knowledge of general repairs, the ability to manage budgets tied to individual work orders, and the judgment to prioritize quality over volume. Lessen's model means your output directly reflects on a client relationship, so the ability to troubleshoot independently and communicate clearly with property owners and managers is part of the job, not a bonus trait.

What the role builds is equally worth naming. Working inside a technology platform that surfaces data on work order history, property condition, and vendor performance gives you exposure to how maintenance operations look at scale. Technicians who pay attention to that layer tend to develop a stronger instinct for cost management and scoping, skills that transfer directly into lead technician and field maintenance manager roles, which Lessen explicitly identifies as a growth path from this position.

Key qualifications and terms:

  • Minimum 3 years of hands-on property maintenance or trade experience, verifiable
  • Comfortable owning work orders independently, including budget accountability
  • Solution-oriented approach to repairs and property condition issues
  • Weekday schedule, no on-call rotation
  • Company fleet vehicle and fuel card provided
  • Tool and equipment allowance of $50 per month, plus $50 cell phone allowance
  • OSHA training provided
  • $1,500 sign-on bonus and quarterly discretionary bonus eligibility up to 5% of quarterly earnings
  • Pay range starting at $24 to $27 per hour, based on qualifications and experience

Where Strong Candidates Stand Out

The technicians who thrive in a portfolio model like this one tend to have strong time management habits and a clean track record on work order completion. Because you're not anchored to one property, you need to carry context about multiple sites and switch gears efficiently. The no on-call structure is a real quality-of-life benefit, but it also means the weekday hours need to count. If you've worked in third-party or fee management settings before, or handled maintenance across scattered single-family or small multifamily assets, that background translates well here. Atlanta's rental market continues to expand, and Lessen's national growth trajectory means this market will likely see increasing workload and opportunity for technicians who perform consistently.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Makowsky Ringel Greenberg has been a fixture in Memphis property management for decades, and this technician role sits inside that established operation. You'd be working across an apartment community with a full ticket load covering HVAC, plumbing, electrical, appliance repair, lock work, and make-ready prep. The Monday through Friday schedule is the baseline, but rotating on-call is part of the deal, and you should go in with that expectation set clearly.

The HVAC certification requirement signals where this role puts its weight. Universal EPA 608 is preferred, and if you hold that, you already know how to handle the full range of refrigerant work that comes with managing residential units. The rest of the scope, plumbing, electrical, lock rekeying, preventive maintenance, rounds out what a well-rounded technician handles at a mid-size apartment community. You'll also document your work daily, which keeps the property's maintenance history clean and matters more than most techs initially expect when deferred items start compounding.

From a career standpoint, this kind of role builds the foundation for a lead technician or service manager position. Two or more years in apartment maintenance teaches you how to triage competing priorities, manage your time across a property without someone standing over your shoulder, and handle resident-facing situations with professionalism. Those skills translate directly into supervisory roles where you're coordinating a team and owning the maintenance budget rather than just executing on it. MRG's structure, with quarterly and annual performance bonuses on top of a sign-on, suggests they're invested in retaining people who perform, which is worth factoring into how you think about the role's longer-term value.

What separates strong candidates here is the combination of genuine HVAC competency and the discipline to keep documentation current under a full work order load. Technicians who treat the paperwork as an afterthought create headaches for the whole operation. If you come in with your own tools, a reliable vehicle, a valid license, and the habit of closing tickets cleanly, you'll stand out.

What you'll need to qualify

  • HVAC certification required; Universal EPA 608 preferred
  • Two or more years of apartment maintenance experience
  • Working knowledge of plumbing, electrical, appliances, and general building systems
  • Physical ability to perform the assigned tasks
  • Familiarity with applicable building codes and safety standards, including OSHA
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Your own tools and a reliable vehicle for maintenance work
  • Valid driver's license and current auto insurance
  • Ability to pass a background check, credit check, and drug screening

The compensation package includes a $1,000 sign-on bonus, quarterly and annual performance bonuses, a fuel allowance, and a full benefits suite covering medical, dental, vision, disability, and life insurance, along with a 401(k) and profit-sharing plan.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - 3300 Tamarac
job.description:
Maintenance work at a 200-unit apartment community covers a lot of ground in a single shift. One morning you might be troubleshooting a tripped breaker in a resident's unit, running a make-ready punch list on a recently vacated apartment, and responding to a plumbing call before lunch. MG Properties is hiring a Maintenance Technician for 3300 Tamarac Apartments in Denver, and the role reflects exactly that kind of variety.

What You'll Actually Do

The day-to-day work spans the full range of apartment maintenance: service requests, appliance repairs, painting, grounds and common area upkeep, and unit turns. Turns deserve a specific mention because they're a real part of the workload at a property this size. Getting units make-ready on schedule directly affects occupancy, so the ability to move through a punch list efficiently matters. You'll also carry on-call rotation, which means after-hours calls are part of the deal. That's true of almost every apartment maintenance role, but it's worth stating plainly rather than burying it in the fine print.

What You Bring

  • At least 2 years of apartment maintenance experience, ideally at a property of 200 units or more
  • Working knowledge across trades: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, and general appliance repair
  • A straightforward, professional approach with residents when handling service requests
  • Reliable transportation (this one's non-negotiable given the on-call component)
  • Comfort working as part of a team and adapting when priorities shift mid-day

The Bigger Picture

MG Properties has been acquiring, developing, and managing apartment communities across the Western U.S. for over 30 years. That kind of track record usually means established systems, defined processes, and a maintenance operation that's had time to mature. For a technician, that often translates to clearer expectations and better support than you'd find at a smaller or newer operator.

Pay runs $24 to $25 per hour depending on experience, with monthly bonuses and company profit sharing on top of base. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, 401k with employer match, PTO, paid holidays, and rental discounts. One detail worth noting: this position is anticipated to close in September 2026, so it carries a defined end date. Factor that into your decision.

Strong candidates at this level tend to be the ones who can work independently without needing direction on every task, communicate honestly with residents even when a repair takes longer than expected, and treat turns with the same attention they give to occupied-unit service calls. Those habits are what separate a technician who's technically competent from one who's actually an asset to a maintenance team.

job.title: Associate, Asset Management
job.description:
Asset management at the property level requires two distinct skill sets working in parallel: financial modeling sharp enough to justify major capital decisions, and operational fluency to hold execution accountable. This role at The Scion Group uses both, consistently.

What This Role Actually Does

The Scion Group focuses on student housing, a sector with its own rhythms around lease-up cycles, annual turn seasons, and enrollment-driven demand. As an Asset Management Associate, you'll carry direct oversight of a portfolio of owned assets. That means building and owning the financial models that underpin capex decisions, tracking whether projected rent premiums are actually materializing post-renovation, and flagging performance gaps before they compound.

You'll also handle the retail side of mixed-use assets: negotiating letters of intent, working through TI scopes, CAM structures, insurance compliance, and concession terms. Quarterly investor reporting packages fall in your lane too, as does contributing to the annual budget process.

On-site inspections are part of the job. You're expected to develop a ground-level understanding of each asset and bring that context back into your analysis, not just model from a spreadsheet.

The Skills This Role Runs On

  • Advanced financial modeling in Excel. This is the core tool. You'll use it to justify repositioning strategies, project ROI on capital improvements, and build investor-facing packages.
  • Commercial real estate asset management experience, specifically. Prior exposure to operations, capital projects, and retail leasing is the baseline.
  • Communication that translates complex data into clear recommendations for both internal teams and external partners.
  • A proactive approach to identifying issues and repositioning opportunities, not waiting for problems to surface in reports.

A bachelor's degree in real estate, finance, economics, or a related STEM field is required. An MBA or advanced degree is a plus. Expect to travel up to 20% of the time, with some flexibility needed during peak periods.

What Makes This Role Specific to Scion

Student housing operates on a compressed annual cycle. Lease-up happens in a narrow window, turn costs are significant, and occupancy swings can be sharp. Asset managers here need to understand those dynamics and factor them into both underwriting assumptions and operational conversations. If your background is purely in conventional multifamily or office, there's a real learning curve on the demand-side drivers.

The role is based at Scion's Chicago corporate office. Compensation is targeted between $105,000 and $125,000 base, plus discretionary bonus and a full benefits package including 401k matching, health, dental, vision, parental leave, and learning reimbursement.

job.title: Cleaner - Part-Time
job.description:
Part-time cleaning roles at student housing properties get overlooked on job boards, but they're genuinely useful positions to hold early in a property management career. You're on the ground every day, moving through every corner of the community, which means you develop an eye for what a well-run property actually looks like from the inside out.

Redstone Residential operates over 38,000 beds across 20 states, making it one of the larger third-party student housing management companies in the country. Their Rexburg location is a student community, which comes with its own rhythm: high turnover seasons, move-in pushes, and the kind of cleaning checks that keep resident relations from becoming maintenance headaches. This role sits at the center of that.

Day to day, you'll handle scheduled cleaning checks of resident apartments, keep common areas like hallways, the clubhouse, and the leasing office in good shape, and manage exterior upkeep including trash, debris, landscaping, and snow and ice removal when the Idaho winters arrive. There's some light maintenance assistance involved as well. The shifts run four to six hours and the pay is $12.00 per hour, part-time and non-exempt.

What makes someone good at this role isn't just attention to detail, it's the ability to self-direct. You'll often be working without someone checking on you every hour, so the candidates who do well here are people who take ownership of their checklist and finish it without being prompted. A friendly demeanor matters too, since cleaning checks put you inside residents' living spaces, and how you carry yourself there affects how residents feel about the property overall.

From a career standpoint, this kind of role builds real fluency with property operations. Porters and cleaners who stay curious tend to move into maintenance tech roles or leasing support positions. You start to understand turn prep, punch list work, and curb appeal in a way that's hard to teach in a classroom. At a company managing a portfolio this size, there are also internal paths worth asking about during the interview.

What Redstone Is Looking For

  • Some background in janitorial or cleaning work
  • Ability to complete daily tasks independently, without close supervision
  • Comfortable with physical work: lifting 50-plus pounds and standing for a full shift
  • Friendly and professional when interacting with residents

Redstone offers a 401(k) with up to 6% matching, which is worth noting for a part-time hourly position. If you're based in Rexburg and want a foothold in property management, this is a practical place to start building one.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
PeakMade Real Estate manages off-campus student housing across the country, and their College Station property sits in one of the more demanding student housing markets in Texas. With Texas A&M enrollment consistently above 70,000, the Bryan/College Station market runs high occupancy most of the year and compresses turn windows considerably. A Maintenance Supervisor here needs to be comfortable executing fast, clean turns while keeping daily service levels high during the academic year.

What You'll Actually Do

This role splits roughly 60 to 70 percent hands-on work and the remainder on supervision, vendor oversight, and coordination with the property manager. On any given day that means completing service requests alongside your team, walking the grounds to catch issues before residents do, and making sure the maintenance shop stays organized and OSHA-compliant. You'll own the preventative maintenance program, manage supply inventory within budget, and keep the hazard communications program current.

Turn season is where this role gets tested. You'll schedule and direct all make-ready activity, supervise contractors throughout the process, and push vacant units through restoration and cleaning so they're ready to market on time. The pace during turn can be relentless, and your ability to keep the team coordinated and the punch list moving is what determines whether the property hits its lease-up deadlines. Outside of turn, you'll conduct monthly unit inspections, assist with move-ins and move-outs, manage key control, and work with the National Facilities Director when capital improvement bids are needed.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • At least 2 years of maintenance supervisory experience; multifamily background strongly preferred
  • EPA Type II certification required; CPO preferred (PeakMade offers technical certifications if you're not yet certified)
  • Valid driver's license, current auto insurance, and a reliable personal vehicle (required for the role)
  • Must live within 30 miles of the property
  • Your own basic hand tools
  • Hands-on repair ability across HVAC, intermediate plumbing, intermediate electrical, appliances, sheetrock, carpentry, painting, pool care, roofing, irrigation, and landscaping
  • Physical ability to lift up to 50 pounds, work at heights on ladders, and work outdoors in Texas heat or cold

Context Worth Knowing

Student housing maintenance supervision differs from conventional multifamily in a few specific ways. Resident turnover is annual and largely synchronized, which means the turn window is compressed and high-volume. Wear and tear patterns in student communities also tend to run heavier than in conventional properties, so your diagnostic speed and carpentry and appliance skills will get consistent use. Supervisors who thrive here are the ones who can execute at the technician level without losing track of their team's workload or the broader property condition. The path from this role often leads to regional facilities roles or community director positions for candidates who develop both the technical depth and the management fundamentals PeakMade's leadership program is designed to build.

PeakMade's benefits package includes paid parental leave, 15 days of PTO plus two additional wellbeing days, 401(k) match, monthly renewal bonuses, and a ten-year milestone trip. The company is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Fairstead operates a portfolio of more than 30,000 apartments across 28 states, and the work that keeps those units occupied and those residents housed happens at the property level, one work order at a time. This Maintenance Technician role in Newark is a direct contributor to that mission. Fairstead builds and manages affordable housing, and the physical condition of each unit directly affects occupancy, resident retention, and NOI. A well-run maintenance program keeps turns tight, punch lists short, and emergency calls manageable. That's the operational reality this role lives in every day.

Day to day, you're moving between scheduled preventative maintenance, unit inspections, and responding to resident service requests. Make-readies are a core part of the rhythm: cleaning and prepping vacated units so the next resident can move in without delay. Deferred turns cost money and drag down occupancy. You'll also check electrical systems for code compliance, test safety devices monthly, and keep a working inventory of tools and supplies so nothing slows you down mid-job.

On-call rotation is part of the role. After-hours emergencies happen in multifamily, and Fairstead expects a prompt response when they do. That's a real commitment worth acknowledging upfront.

Strong candidates come in with hands-on experience across general maintenance trades, a working knowledge of electrical systems, and an HVAC certification or equivalent. The ability to lift 70 pounds and stay on your feet for extended periods is a physical requirement of the work, not a formality. What separates a good technician from a great one at a property like this is attention to detail during inspections and the discipline to follow preventative maintenance schedules before problems compound into capex issues.

What Fairstead is looking for

  • Prior experience as a maintenance technician or in a comparable service role
  • Mechanical aptitude for minor repairs across plumbing, electrical, and general fixtures
  • HVAC, CMRP, or equivalent certification (preferred)
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills
  • Physical ability to lift up to 70 pounds and stand for extended periods
  • Availability for on-call rotation and after-hours emergency response

Compensation runs $24 to $26 per hour depending on experience and qualifications. Benefits include medical coverage through Meritain Health with a generous employer contribution, employer-paid vision and life insurance, a 401(k) with company match (100% on the first 3%, 50% on the next 2%), 15 days of PTO, 7 sick days, and 12 or more paid holidays. Flexible spending accounts, disability coverage, and pet insurance round out the package.

Fairstead takes a tech-forward approach to affordable housing operations, which means technicians here work within systems built around data and efficiency. If you're used to paper logs and informal processes, expect a more structured environment with digital tools supporting maintenance tracking and resident communication.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor - Multi site
job.description:
It's 7 a.m. and you're already mapping out which of the three San Diego properties needs you first: a vacated unit at Melrose Canyon that has to be market-ready by end of week, a pool chemical check at Park Diplomat, and a work order backlog at 445 West University. That's the rhythm of this role.

What This Job Covers

Sunrise Management is hiring a multi-site Maintenance Supervisor to oversee physical operations across three residential properties in San Diego. You'll rotate between locations based on project needs, so a valid driver's license is a hard requirement, not a formality.

The core of the job is keeping units turning and common areas clean and functional. Make-ready timelines here run three to five days after vacancy. You'll handle the painting, coordinate carpet cleaning, run through punch list items, and make sure each unit passes inspection before it goes back on the market. On top of turns, you'll manage the full preventive maintenance calendar: HVAC, water heaters, pool and spa systems, lighting, fire safety checks, and life-safety walkthroughs.

Day-to-day work orders need to close within 24 hours. When parts delays push that window, you communicate directly with site management and keep residents informed. You'll also be on call for after-hours emergencies, which is standard for a supervisor role at this level.

This is a team leadership position. You'll supervise maintenance staff across sites, assign schedules, run monthly safety meetings, maintain MSDS records, and make sure PPE protocols are followed. You'll also have a hand in interviewing and training new maintenance hires, and you'll submit timesheets for your team.

Budget awareness matters here. You control supply purchases, get manager approval on expenditures, and flag capital improvement needs or repair recommendations up the chain. Sunrise wants someone who can identify a problem before it becomes expensive.

What You Bring

  • At least 2 years of hands-on property maintenance experience
  • Prior supervisory experience, managing a team and holding people accountable
  • Working knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, electrical, appliances, carpentry, and pool systems
  • Familiarity with Entrata or AppFolio is a plus
  • Valid driver's license with reliable transportation between sites
  • Understanding of Fair Housing laws
  • Comfort with PPE requirements and adherence to safety and hazardous materials policies

Pay runs $27 to $32 per hour depending on experience. Candidates who stand out tend to bring pool certifications, HVAC experience, and a track record of keeping turns tight without cutting corners on quality. Multi-site experience is a genuine advantage here because managing your time across three addresses with competing priorities is a skill in itself.

job.title: Service Technician
job.description:
Affordable housing maintenance operates on tighter margins and higher expectations than most people assume. At a community like Harbor House on Saratoga in Corpus Christi, a Service Technician isn't just fixing things. They're directly protecting the quality of homes for working families who depend on the property running well. Dream Live Prosper Communities, a subsidiary of DLP Capital, is staffing this full-time role at their Corpus Christi location.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

The job centers on two rhythms: reactive and planned. On the reactive side, you're responding to resident service requests within 24 hours, handling the full range of plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliance, and drywall work that comes up in any occupied community. On the planned side, you're running apartment turns, with a five-day target from vacancy to move-in ready. That turnaround window is tight, and hitting it consistently requires you to walk a unit, build a punch list quickly, sequence the work, and execute without a lot of hand-holding.

HVAC certification is required here, not preferred. That signals how central mechanical systems are to this community's operations. Beyond the technical work, this role includes some team coordination: assigning service requests, mentoring other technicians, managing the on-call schedule, and keeping the maintenance shop stocked without overspending. If you've only ever worked as a solo tech, the team leadership piece is worth taking seriously as part of the job description.

The role also involves grounds maintenance, emergency on-call rotation, and working in South Texas weather conditions year-round. After-hours calls are real, and consistent availability matters.

Where This Role Leads

A Service Technician position at a growing affordable housing operator is one of the cleaner paths into a Maintenance Supervisor or Maintenance Director role in property management. The skills that compound fastest here are turn management and vendor coordination. Techs who understand how a five-day turn affects occupancy, and who can manage cost-per-unit on make-readies, become genuinely valuable to regional operations teams. Add HVAC certification, some capex project exposure, and a track record of low delinquency-related damage disputes (through solid move-out documentation), and you've built a profile that carries weight across the industry.

What separates strong candidates in this specific role is the combination of technical range and communication. The job requires talking to residents professionally, coordinating with vendors, and reporting up to property management. Technicians who treat resident interaction as secondary to the wrenches tend to struggle here. The ones who move up treat both as equally important parts of the job.

  • HVAC certification required
  • Proficiency in electrical, plumbing, appliance repair, painting, and drywall
  • Ability to complete apartment turns within five days
  • Experience with turnovers in both newer and older building stock
  • Valid driver's license with a clean driving record and reliable transportation
  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs and work in varied physical conditions including roofs, crawl spaces, and attics
  • Availability for after-hours emergencies and on-call rotation
  • Your own basic tools
  • Familiarity with property management operations and basic budgeting (preferred)

This is a full-time position with a schedule that includes weekends. Benefits include PTO, health, dental, vision, and life insurance, 401(k) matching, and learning and educational incentives.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Leasing consultants carry the front door of any residential community. They're the first real conversation a prospective resident has with a property, and in a market like Los Angeles County, where competition for qualified tenants is constant, the quality of that conversation determines occupancy. Property Management Associates is building its pipeline for this role at a Carson property and wants someone who can convert traffic into signed leases consistently.

What the Work Looks Like

You'll conduct tours, walk prospects through the application process, and handle lease signings. Marketing is part of the job too: PMA expects you to support vacancy promotion through online platforms and social media, not just wait for leads to arrive. This is an in-office, on-site role with one weekend day required each week. That's standard for leasing; weekend traffic is often the heaviest.

Compensation runs $19.50 to $23.00 per hour for 40 hours per week, with a leasing bonus structure on top: $100 per new lease signed and $50 per renewal. Full-time employees receive medical, dental, vision, and life insurance with an employer contribution, a 401(k) with discretionary company match after one year, short and long-term disability, and a PTO package covering vacation, holidays, and sick time.

What PMA Is Looking For

  • Strong verbal and written communication, especially with prospects who are still deciding
  • Hands-on experience with rental applications and lease execution
  • Comfort with Microsoft Office and property management software; Yardi Voyager and Rent Cafe experience is a plus
  • Demonstrated use of social media and online platforms to market vacancies
  • A personality that reads well in person: you're talking to people at a significant decision point in their lives

PMA has operated in the Southern California market for over 30 years, managing both residential and commercial properties across greater LA County. For a leasing consultant, that kind of organizational depth means established processes, training resources, and real room to grow inside the company.

One thing that separates strong leasing consultants from average ones in this market: follow-through. Most prospects tour multiple properties before deciding. The consultant who follows up promptly, answers questions clearly, and moves the application process forward without friction closes more leases. Familiarity with Yardi and Rent Cafe helps because slow processing loses applicants who are ready to commit.

job.title: Providence at McDowell Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
It's 9 a.m. on the first of the month at Providence at McDowell, and your morning is already shaped by the ledger. Which residents posted overnight, who still owes, and which accounts are moving toward a late notice. That rhythm, financial accountability layered underneath everything else you do, defines what this role actually is.

What This Role Covers

Karya Property Management is hiring an Assistant Community Manager for Providence at McDowell, a full-time, hourly, on-site position in Phoenix. The role sits at the intersection of collections, leasing, and community operations, and you'll carry real ownership across all three.

On the financial side, you'll post payments, process deposits, and maintain resident ledgers daily. Delinquency management is yours end to end: late notices, statutory notices under the Arizona Residential Landlord and Tenant Act, payment plan negotiations, and coordination with legal counsel when matters escalate to eviction. You'll also handle move-in and move-out accounting, security deposit dispositions within Arizona's statutory window, and contribute to weekly and monthly reporting on occupancy, budget variance, and collections.

Leasing is a real part of the job, not secondary to the admin work. You'll carry an individual leasing and renewal goal, conduct tours, work leads through to close, and manage the full application pipeline from screening through lease execution. Renewal campaigns, rent increases, and resident retention outreach are also part of your workload, alongside competitor surveys and occasional social media support.

When the Community Manager is off-site, you're running the property. That includes resident escalations, vendor coordination, unit turns, punch walks, and whatever the day brings. You'll also participate in the on-call rotation for after-hours emergencies.

What You'll Need and What You'll Build

This role requires at least one year in a customer-facing field, strong comfort with numbers and spreadsheet-level detail, and the communication skills to handle a frustrated resident and a vendor call in the same hour without losing composure. A high school diploma or equivalent is required. Weekend availability and flexibility during peak leasing and turn seasons are both expected.

Prior multifamily experience, especially collections and evictions, gives candidates a real advantage. Familiarity with Yardi, Entrata, or RealPage is preferred, as is working knowledge of Arizona landlord-tenant law, Fair Housing requirements, and bilingual ability in English and Spanish.

What the role builds is worth naming directly. Candidates who come from leasing or hospitality will develop serious financial fluency here: delinquency management, ledger accuracy, and budget-variance thinking are skills that carry directly into Community Manager roles. Candidates who come from an admin or accounting background will develop the leasing confidence and resident-relations judgment that rounds out a full property management skill set. Either path leads somewhere.

One honest note: Phoenix summers are real, and this role includes outdoor property walks during turns and outreach events. Physical stamina during peak season is part of the job description, not a footnote.

Compensation includes an hourly rate, leasing commissions, renewal bonuses, quarterly and annual performance bonuses tied to occupancy and delinquency targets, medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401(k) with company match, paid time off, and a potential housing discount.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
FLATS operates urban apartment communities in Chicago with a design-forward identity and a tech-integrated approach to property operations. This Maintenance Technician role sits at the center of the day-to-day physical plant: work orders, make-readies, grounds, life safety systems, and everything in between.

What You'll Actually Do

Your day starts with the work order queue. You'll triage, prioritize, and close out resident service requests, keeping response times tight. Make-ready work is a regular part of the job: prepping vacant units to company standards before a new resident takes possession. Beyond turns, you'll handle common area cleaning, exterior grounds upkeep, and seasonal duties including pool maintenance. Property walk-throughs are part of your routine, and when something's off, you document it and move toward a fix.

Annual inspections don't manage themselves. Fire extinguishers, life safety systems, elevators, and any other city or state-mandated checks fall within your scope. When outside contractors are needed for larger projects, you'll help coordinate that under the direction of the Maintenance Engineer or Property Manager. Inspection prep is part of the job too.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of residential maintenance experience
  • HVAC experience is required; certification is a plus
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Comfortable with Microsoft Office for basic documentation and communication
  • Strong time management and the ability to shift priorities without losing track of open items
  • Good resident-facing communication skills, which matter more than people expect in this role
  • Physical readiness: this job involves lifting up to 100 pounds, working in varying weather, and spending most of the day on your feet, crawling, climbing, or crouching
  • Safety-conscious habits around electrical, mechanical, and airborne hazard exposure

A Few Honest Notes

Urban mid-rise maintenance in Chicago carries its own rhythm. Winters push HVAC and exterior work hard, and the life safety inspection calendar in the city is thorough. If you've worked a Chicago property before, you already know the pace. If you haven't, expect to learn it quickly. The coordination side of this role, managing contractors and inspection schedules, tends to separate the technicians who stay and grow from the ones who burn out. Good documentation habits and a methodical approach to work order management go further here than raw technical speed.

FLATS offers medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with employer match, paid time off, sick leave, and paid holidays.

job.title: Regional Property Manager - Northern Colorado
job.description:
It's a Tuesday morning and you're standing in the leasing office of a new-build community in Thornton, walking through traffic numbers with a Community Manager before heading north to check on a stabilized asset in Fort Collins. By noon, you'll be reviewing a punch list with a maintenance lead. That's the rhythm of this role.

The Scope

AIR Communities operates apartment communities across major U.S. markets, and this position covers a Northern Colorado portfolio that spans both lease-up assets and mature, stabilized properties. The two types demand different thinking. A new-build community needs aggressive leasing strategy, concession discipline, and close attention to early occupancy trends. A stabilized asset needs operational consistency, retention focus, and tight expense management to protect NOI. You'll be doing both, often in the same week.

This is a field-based role by design. Four to five days per week, you're at properties, not working remotely. You'll lead Community Managers and their onsite teams, which means coaching on sales process and leasing metrics, addressing delinquency, managing budgets, and keeping resident satisfaction scores where they need to be. You'll also partner closely with maintenance to make sure make-ready timelines stay on track and community standards hold up across the portfolio.

Financial accountability is real here. You're responsible for budget oversight, revenue growth, and expense management across multiple assets. A general understanding of property financials isn't enough; you need to be comfortable reading a T-12, identifying where performance is slipping, and adjusting strategy accordingly.

What AIR Is Looking For

  • At least five years leading multifamily teams across multiple communities, with measurable results in occupancy, leasing performance, and resident retention
  • Experience managing a portfolio that includes lease-up or new construction alongside stabilized assets
  • Strong financial acumen: budgets, expense control, and revenue growth strategies
  • Hands-on, present leadership style. This role doesn't work for someone who manages from a distance
  • Familiarity with property management platforms such as OneSite, SmartRent, or Salesforce
  • A background in competitive, metrics-driven sales environments, whether in multifamily, hospitality, or similar fields

Compensation is $120,000 to $140,000 annually, plus an annual target bonus. AIR also offers medical, dental, vision, and life insurance, HSA/FSA options, company-paid short and long-term disability, a 401(k) with up to 6% employer contribution, paid parental leave up to 16 weeks, tuition assistance, and a 25% rent discount at any AIR community. The application deadline is August 3, 2026, though AIR will continue reviewing submissions on a rolling basis after that date.

Northern Colorado's multifamily market has added significant supply over the past few years, particularly in the Greeley and Fort Collins corridors. That means the leasing environment is more competitive than it was even three years ago, and concession strategy matters more at the community level. Candidates who have managed through a lease-up in a supply-heavy submarket will have a real advantage here.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

Copper Beech Statesboro serves the Georgia Southern University market, which means your leasing calendar runs on an academic rhythm. The biggest stretch of the year is Turn, when hundreds of residents cycle in and out within a compressed window and every task from touring to package retrieval to maintenance follow-up runs simultaneously.
