Outside of Turn, the role stays active: you'll lead property tours, field prospect inquiries, help execute resident engagement events, and keep the leasing office and common areas presentation-ready. You'll also support social media content and flag local marketing opportunities to the management team.

After-hours on-call rotation is part of the job. Lockouts happen, and you'll be expected to cover your share of them. That's a real commitment worth knowing upfront.

The title at Scion is Experience Team Member, which reflects what the company actually wants from this position: someone who treats every touchpoint, the first tour, a maintenance follow-up call, a package hand-off, as a customer service moment. Sales and hospitality are genuinely intertwined here.

What You Bring

  • Strong interpersonal skills and comfort communicating with a wide range of people, including prospective residents, current residents, and university-adjacent partners
  • Flexibility with a schedule that shifts across weekdays, weekends, holidays, and peak Turn periods
  • Self-discipline and reliability in a role that blends independent tasks with team coordination
  • Comfort with social media platforms used for resident communication and community promotion
  • Eligibility to work in the United States (visa sponsorship is not available)

Context Worth Knowing

Student housing operates differently from conventional multifamily. Occupancy at properties like Copper Beech Statesboro is tied directly to enrollment cycles, so traffic patterns are predictable in one sense but extremely compressed in another. Strong ETMs learn to read objections early in the leasing season, communicate them clearly to the management team, and adjust their approach as availability tightens. That feedback loop between the leasing floor and management is something Scion builds into this role deliberately.

For someone early in a property management career, this position builds a foundation that transfers well. The combination of leasing, marketing, administration, and resident relations gives you exposure to most of the functions you'd need to move into an assistant manager or property manager role down the road, particularly within the student housing sector where operators like Scion, CA Student Living, and Greystar Student run at scale.

job.title: Assistant Property Manager
job.description:
Cottonwood Residential is filling an Assistant Property Manager position at Morgan Ridge Apartments in Winston-Salem. If you've spent time on the leasing floor or front desk and you're ready to take on more of the operational side, this is a natural next step.

The day-to-day here covers the full range of what an APM does at a conventional multifamily community. You're handling rent collection, managing delinquency, keeping resident files current, and processing the paperwork that comes with notices and formal correspondence. You'll coordinate with vendors and support leasing activity alongside the property manager. When the PM is out, you run the site. That's not a footnote; it's worth understanding upfront, because it means you need to be comfortable making judgment calls on your own.

Cottonwood has been an early adopter of self-guided tours, which reflects how they approach the leasing process generally. If you've only worked at communities where everything runs through a leasing agent, expect a slightly different rhythm here around prospect traffic and how tours convert.

Weekend availability is required. That's standard for this industry, but it bears saying plainly.

What Cottonwood is Looking For

  • Background in leasing, sales, or customer-facing service
  • Comfort with basic accounting concepts, especially around rent ledgers and delinquency tracking
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Entrata Core experience is a plus, not a requirement
  • Working knowledge of Fair Housing law
  • Weekend availability

The compensation package includes a competitive base with quarterly bonuses, full medical, dental, vision, life, and disability coverage (available within the first month), a 401k with company match, HSA matching, three weeks of PTO in the first year, and 10.5 paid holidays. That's a solid benefits structure for a site-level role.

APMs who do this job well tend to move into property manager roles within a couple of years. The skills that carry over are the ones that matter most at that level: delinquency management, vendor coordination, and the ability to hold a community together when the person above you is unavailable. If you treat this as a training ground and pay attention to the financials, the path forward is pretty clear.

job.title: Maintenance Technician-Cortland Armour Yards
job.description:
It's 7:15 a.m. and there's already a work order flagged urgent: a resident's AC stopped cooling overnight, and Atlanta in July doesn't forgive slow response times. That's the rhythm of this role at Cortland Armour Yards.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Cortland is a vertically integrated operator with a sizable footprint, which means their maintenance teams carry real responsibility. At Armour Yards, you're handling the full range of building systems: electrical, plumbing, HVAC, appliances, flooring, railings, and everything in between. You'll run work orders, support the preventative maintenance schedule, and keep an eye on building systems like automatic doors and surveillance equipment so small issues don't become capex problems. Inventory management matters here too. Running out of a common part mid-turn is the kind of thing that slows down a make-ready and nobody wants that conversation.

On-call rotation is part of the job. Emergencies don't schedule themselves, and Cortland expects you to respond when they happen. Resident interactions come with the territory, and handling them professionally is just as much a part of the job as the technical work itself.

What You Bring

  • EPA certification (Type I, II, or Universal) required before you start
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • One to three or more years in maintenance, facilities, or multifamily housing
  • Solid working knowledge of electrical, plumbing, HVAC, and appliance repair
  • Ability to prioritize a shifting work order queue without losing track of the details
  • Comfortable with ladders, tools, and working outdoors in Georgia heat
  • Willingness to participate in on-call rotation and respond to after-hours emergencies
  • Clear communication with both residents and teammates

What separates a strong candidate from an average one at a property like this: the ability to diagnose accurately on the first visit. Repeat trips on the same work order signal either a parts problem or a diagnostic problem, and Cortland tracks that. Technicians who close tickets cleanly and document recurring issues before they escalate tend to build credibility fast with site leadership.

Cortland operates as a recognized top-10 multifamily owner and operator nationally, with in-house design, construction, and management functions. For a maintenance technician, that structure can open doors. Techs who develop strong HVAC and electrical skills at a platform like this often move into lead tech or maintenance supervisor roles as the portfolio grows, and Cortland's growth trajectory has been consistent.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.description:
Skills That Drive This Role

Maintenance work at a residential community runs on a specific combination of hands-on trade knowledge and people skills. At Stonebriar of Frisco Apartments, a Cottonwood Residential community in Frisco, TX, you'll use both every day. The technical side covers plumbing repairs, electrical troubleshooting, general carpentry, and HVAC diagnostics. The human side means showing up to a resident's door, explaining what you're doing, and leaving the unit better than you found it. If you hold EPA Type II or Universal certification, or a CPO cert, those credentials give you a head start. HVAC troubleshooting experience is genuinely useful here, not just a checkbox.

This is an entry-level position, which means Cottonwood isn't expecting a seasoned maintenance supervisor. They're looking for someone who learns quickly, communicates clearly in English (written and verbal), and can handle the physical demands of the job: lifting up to 50 lbs., working on ladders and scaffolding, and spending most of the day on your feet. A valid driver's license is required.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

A typical day moves between work orders and whatever comes up unexpectedly. You might start the morning running a make-ready punch list on a vacated unit, then shift to a plumbing call in the afternoon, then help with a grounds issue before the end of your shift. Evenings and weekends are part of the schedule, and on-call rotation means you'll occasionally respond to after-hours emergencies. You won't be handling those calls alone. The Service Manager provides backup and guidance, especially while you're still learning the property and the company's standards.

That on-call piece is worth being honest about. It's a real commitment, and it affects your schedule in ways that a standard 9-to-5 doesn't. For the right person, it's also where you build trust with residents fast. Showing up reliably during a leak or a lockout leaves a stronger impression than a dozen routine work orders.

What Makes Cottonwood a Particular Fit

Cottonwood Residential has positioned itself as a company that moves early on technology adoption. Their rollout of Self-Guided Tours is one example of how they approach the resident experience differently. For a maintenance tech, that context matters because it signals a company culture that values service delivery as a differentiator, not just a checkbox. Your work directly supports the experience residents have, from the condition of their units to how quickly problems get resolved.

The benefits package is worth noting for an entry-level role. Health, vision, dental, life, and disability coverage becomes available within the first 30 days. The company also offers a 401(k) with a match, an HSA match, 120 hours of paid time off in year one, and 10.5 paid holidays. That's a meaningful package at this level of the career path.

For technicians looking at where this role leads: strong performers in entry-level maintenance positions typically move into lead tech or Service Manager roles as they build certifications and property-specific experience. EPA Universal and CPO certifications, in particular, open doors across the industry and increase your value on any property, regardless of where your career takes you.

job.title: Leasing Consultant
job.description:
Student housing runs on a different clock than conventional multifamily. Leasing isn't spread across twelve months of steady traffic. It compresses, it surges, and then Turn arrives and everything happens at once. The Experience Team Member role at Ion at the Ballpark exists because Scion understands that in student living, the leasing relationship doesn't end at the signed lease. It continues through move-in, through the academic year, and right up to renewal season.

What the Role Actually Covers

This is a full-cycle customer-facing position, not a pure leasing role. You'll conduct community and amenity tours, field prospect and resident inquiries, and assist with social media and local marketing outreach. On the administrative side, expect package logging, office and amenity upkeep, maintenance request coordination, and after-hours lockout coverage on rotation. The job description notes the responsibilities aren't exhaustive, which in student housing means you should assume the list will expand during peak periods.

Availability during summer and Turn is a real requirement here, not a formality. Turn at a student property is controlled chaos at best. If you haven't worked one before, it's worth knowing what you're signing up for: compressed timelines, high unit volume, and residents moving in and out on the same weekend.

What Scion Is Looking For

  • Genuine comfort working with a college-aged resident base and their parents
  • Strong communication skills across in-person, phone, and digital channels
  • Reliability and self-discipline, particularly for the on-call rotation
  • Flexibility in a leasing calendar that shifts with academic cycles
  • A customer-first instinct, not just a sales instinct

The candidates who do well in this kind of role tend to be organized enough to manage admin tasks without losing their energy on the floor. Student residents notice when the person giving them a tour is distracted or going through the motions. The ones who build real rapport, who actually know the neighborhood and can speak to the Birmingham market around the Ballpark District, tend to drive better close rates and better renewal conversations.

Scion offers health, dental, and vision coverage, 401k matching, paid time off, paid parental and maternal leave, learning reimbursement, and a discretionary annual bonus. This is a non-exempt hourly position. Work authorization is required. Visa sponsorship is not available.

job.title: Porter
job.description:
A resident flags a piece of litter near the building entrance at 8 a.m. By the time the morning is underway, the walkway is clear, the common areas are checked, and the property looks the way it should. That's the rhythm of this role.

What the Job Involves

Fairstead is an affordable housing owner and operator with a portfolio of more than 30,000 apartments across 28 states. This Porter position is based at one of their Newark properties. The work is hands-on and exterior-focused: daily property walks, trash and debris removal, maintaining curb appeal, and keeping common areas clean and safe for residents.

You'll also assist with light maintenance and repairs to community features as needed. Resident interactions happen regularly, so basic customer service skills matter. The job requires weekend availability and on-call flexibility.

What You Bring

  • An interest in custodial or maintenance work, with some mechanical aptitude
  • Ability to work a flexible schedule, including weekends and occasional on-call shifts
  • Reliability and attention to detail on daily rounds

Pay runs $16 to $19 per hour depending on experience and location. Benefits include medical insurance through Meritain Health with a strong employer contribution, employer-paid vision and life insurance, a 401(k) with company match (100% on the first 3%, 50% on the next 2%), 15 days of PTO, 7 sick days, and 12 or more paid holidays.

One thing worth knowing: Porter roles at affordable housing properties tend to carry more resident-facing responsibility than similar positions at market-rate sites. Fairstead's residents rely on well-kept common spaces and responsive staff. Showing up consistently and communicating issues quickly carries real weight here.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - Brockford Place
job.description:
Multifamily maintenance is where technical skill and resident experience intersect most directly. A leaking faucet at 11pm, a unit that needs to be rent-ready in three days, a pool that has to pass inspection by Friday: the maintenance technician is the person the whole operation depends on to keep those things from becoming bigger problems. Sunrise Management is hiring for that role at Brockford Place in Sacramento, and the position suits someone who takes real ownership of a property rather than just working through a ticket queue.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

The core of the role covers the full range of hands-on maintenance: plumbing, basic electrical, HVAC, appliance repair, carpentry, painting, and pool upkeep. You'll keep common areas clean and presentable, manage curb appeal, and handle the make-ready process for vacant units with a target of three to five days from vacancy to rent-ready. Service requests need resolution within 24 hours, which means you'll need to prioritize quickly and communicate clearly when parts or scheduling push a timeline out.

Beyond reactive repairs, you'll work through monthly preventive maintenance checks covering lighting, fire safety, pool and spa systems, and life-safety hazards. You'll know where every shutoff lives on the property. You'll track tool and supply inventory, document vacant unit status, and assist with move-in and move-out inspections. On-call emergency coverage is part of the schedule, so flexibility on evenings and weekends is a real requirement, not a footnote.

What You Bring and Where This Can Lead

Sunrise is looking for one to two years of hands-on experience across the core trades, plus solid computer and mobile device skills since work orders and documentation run through software. Strong communication matters here: you're the face of the property for residents when something goes wrong, and how you handle a frustrated tenant during a repair visit shapes retention as much as the fix itself does.

  • 1 to 2 years of experience in plumbing, electrical, HVAC, carpentry, or painting
  • Comfortable using a mobile device for work order management
  • Able to work a flexible schedule including on-call emergency response
  • Familiarity with MSDS documentation and safety compliance practices
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to work independently with minimal supervision

Technicians who build depth across trades and develop strong documentation habits tend to move into lead tech or maintenance supervisor roles within two to three years. From there, the path to a regional maintenance director position or facilities management role opens up, especially at a company with a growing portfolio. The skills you compound here, specifically preventive maintenance planning, resident communication, and compliance documentation, are exactly what separates candidates for those senior roles. The pay range is $22 to $24 per hour depending on experience, with medical, dental, and vision coverage, FSA, company-paid life insurance, and paid time off.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
This role covers five apartment communities across two Pittsburgh-area submarkets: four properties totaling 198 units in Greensburg and one 97-unit community in New Kensington. Multi-site portfolios at this scale demand someone who can move fluidly between hands-on skilled trades work and the logistical side of managing people, vendors, and budgets. Birgo is looking for a maintenance supervisor who does both well.

The day-to-day splits roughly into two modes. Some of it is field work: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, drywall, turns, punch lists, and groundskeeping across properties that aren't all in the same zip code. The rest is coordination: leading a two-person tech team, sourcing and managing contractors when the scope exceeds what the crew can handle, tracking expenditures against budget, and serving as the operational link between maintenance and property management. AppFolio handles work orders in a paperless workflow, so comfort with mobile tools matters here.

The Greensburg and New Kensington markets sit in the older housing stock belt east and northeast of Pittsburgh. Properties in these corridors tend to be garden-style or low-rise buildings with aging mechanical systems, which means HVAC and plumbing calls come with some frequency. A supervisor who can personally handle high-skill repairs keeps vendor costs down and reduces unit downtime on turns. That's a real budget lever at this portfolio size.

Birgo emphasizes servant leadership internally, and that framing is worth taking seriously in the context of this role. Managing two techs means coaching and developing them, not just directing work. Strong candidates will have experience building a team's technical capability over time, not just assigning jobs and checking completions. Emotional intelligence in conflict resolution, which comes up in any maintenance team eventually, matters as much as trade credentials here.

What Birgo is Looking For

  • 5 or more years of multifamily maintenance experience
  • 3 or more years in a supervisory capacity
  • Hands-on expertise across plumbing, electrical, HVAC, and drywall
  • Experience managing a multi-site portfolio
  • Comfort with mobile work order platforms (AppFolio experience is a plus)
  • Budget awareness and cost control discipline
  • Active driver's license, reliable insured vehicle, and ability to lift 50 pounds unassisted

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM, with participation in an on-call rotation. Compensation is $31 per hour. Birgo offers medical, dental, vision, life, and short-term disability insurance with a company contribution, a 401(k) with employer match, paid time off, paid holidays, sick time, mileage and boot reimbursements, uniforms, a professional development reimbursement program, profit-sharing, and a discount at Birgo properties.

job.title: Maintenance Technician (The Reserve)
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

Maintenance technicians at The Reserve handle the full range of day-to-day upkeep: HVAC service and repairs, plumbing, electrical work, and structural fixes across the property's interior and exterior. You're also responsible for preventative maintenance, which means staying ahead of issues before they turn into emergency calls. Speaking of which, after-hours emergencies are part of this role. When a resident loses heat in January or has a water leak at midnight, someone has to respond. That's you sometimes.

On a typical day, you'll work through a queue of resident service requests, document what you find, complete the work, and move on to the next one. Keeping accurate records matters here, both for accountability and for spotting recurring problems on the property. The job keeps you moving physically, so expect time on your feet, climbing, bending, and lifting throughout your shift.

What You Bring

  • 2 to 3 years of maintenance experience in a residential or comparable setting
  • Working knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, and electrical systems
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Valid driver's license
  • EPA Type 2 or Universal certification (preferred but not required)
  • Ability to communicate clearly with residents and teammates, even when the situation is frustrating

The EPA certification is worth mentioning separately. If you have it, you're more useful on HVAC work from day one. If you don't, it's a credential worth pursuing early and one that adds real value to your skill set across any property you work on in the future.

The Role in Context

BAM Companies has been operating since 2010 and manages properties across multiple markets. The Reserve in Evansville is part of that portfolio. Pay for this position ranges from $17 to $19 per hour depending on experience and qualifications. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage with BAM covering a significant share of the cost, paid life insurance, rent discounts at BAM properties, and a PTO structure that gives you 88 hours after 90 days and 120 hours after your first year, plus 14.5 paid holidays.

One honest note for anyone weighing this against other maintenance roles: the difference between a solid technician and an exceptional one at a property like this usually comes down to how they handle resident interactions, not just the technical work. You can fix a unit perfectly, but if you leave a resident feeling dismissed or uninformed, the job isn't really done. The technical skills get you hired. The communication habits are what build a reputation on site.

job.title: Leasing Manager
job.description:
Leasing skills sit at the center of this role, and they show up in concrete, measurable ways. At Redstone Residential's Rexburg community, a Leasing Manager's effectiveness gets measured in occupancy trends, renewal rates, and the quality of every prospect interaction from the first phone call to the signed lease. This is a hands-on leasing position with real operational responsibility layered in.

Skills This Role Puts to Work Daily

Sales and customer service aren't background skills here. They drive the core function of the job. You'll conduct prospect tours, manage phone and email pipelines, and run renewal campaigns designed to hold occupancy. Redstone uses Entrata as its leasing platform, so comfort with structured software workflows matters. You'll also work within their online and social marketing systems, which means basic SEO awareness and digital communication skills translate directly into leasing performance.

On the administrative side, you'll maintain resident ledgers and keep balances accurate. That requires attention to detail and a working comfort with cloud-based tools like Google Drive and Dropbox. Mistakes in ledger management create downstream problems for collections and delinquency tracking, so accuracy carries real weight.

The Operational Layer

Beyond leasing, this role supports the Community Manager across broader operations. That includes budget performance awareness, rent collections, and some staff administration. You're not just filling units. You're helping keep the property running day to day, which gives you visibility into how leasing activity connects to NOI and overall community health.

Rexburg is a student-market town built largely around BYU-Idaho's enrollment calendar. That means leasing cycles here follow a rhythm that differs from conventional multifamily. Traffic peaks and lease-up pressure align with academic timelines, and renewal campaigns need to account for the transient nature of a student population. Experience in or awareness of student housing dynamics is a genuine advantage in this market.

What Separates Strong Candidates

  • Demonstrated ability to hit leasing goals without waiting to be directed, especially during peak traffic periods
  • Comfort using Entrata or a comparable leasing CRM, not just basic office software
  • A communication style that works equally well with prospects, current residents, and teammates
  • Enough composure to handle a high-volume leasing season without letting service quality slip

Redstone operates at scale, managing over 38,000 beds across 20 states as a third-party manager. That structure means their systems, reporting standards, and leasing processes are well-developed. For someone early in a property management career, working inside that kind of operational framework builds transferable skills quickly. The Leasing Manager role is a natural stepping stone toward a Community Manager position, particularly for candidates who develop both the leasing and administrative sides of the job.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This role sits at the center of daily operations at a Fairstead affordable housing property in Dallas. You'll work alongside the Property Manager to keep the property compliant, occupied, and financially sound. A good portion of your time goes toward HUD compliance: executing the 4350.3 Handbook requirements, coordinating annual and interim recertification reviews, and helping prepare the property for REAC inspections, Management and Occupancy Reviews, LIHTC reviews, and investor site visits. When EHS violations surface, you help get them cleared.

On the financial side, you'll track arrears daily, ensure rents are collected, posted, and deposited, and create purchase orders in Yardi. You'll work with the in-house legal team to monitor rent payment status and coordinate evictions when lease violations escalate past intervention. On the resident-facing side, you're responding to calls, emails, and complaints within a few hours, alerting staff to move-ins and move-outs, and making sure the maintenance team closes out service requests. You also manage the lease renewal program to protect retention.

What You Bring

  • At least two years of experience in affordable housing leasing or property management (required)
  • Working knowledge of EIV, Yardi, and RealPage
  • Familiarity with HUD 4350.3 compliance requirements and LIHTC recertification processes
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, specifically for resident relations and documentation
  • Knowledge of the Dallas residential market

What This Role Builds

Affordable housing compliance is a distinct discipline within property management, and this position develops real depth in it. Candidates who come from conventional multifamily often underestimate how different the regulatory cadence is. You'll sharpen your ability to read and apply HUD guidance, manage recertification timelines, and prepare a property for formal review cycles. Those skills transfer directly into Community Manager roles at affordable properties, compliance specialist positions, or regional roles within affordable housing portfolios. Fairstead operates across 28 states with more than 30,000 units, so internal advancement for people who prove themselves operationally is a realistic path.

The candidates who thrive here combine genuine attention to detail on the compliance and financial side with the interpersonal steadiness that resident-facing work requires. Affordable housing residents often face real housing instability, so the ability to handle difficult conversations with patience and professionalism matters as much as knowing your way around Yardi. If you've worked affordable housing and already understand the distinction between market-rate delinquency follow-up and the specific protocols required under HUD guidelines, you'll hit the ground running.

job.title: Maintenance Technician - San Diego, CA
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

At The Rey in San Diego, the Maintenance Technician role touches nearly every corner of daily community life. You're the person residents call when something goes wrong, and you're also the one quietly keeping things from going wrong in the first place. That balance between reactive repairs and proactive upkeep is really what defines this position.

Day to day, you'll handle the full range of general maintenance needs: plumbing fixes, electrical troubleshooting, appliance repairs, carpentry work, and general building upkeep. You'll help manage the shop, keep inventory organized, and make sure equipment and keys are properly secured. Curb appeal matters here. If something looks off walking through the property, you notice it and you address it. Management leans on you to uphold community standards, and that means being thorough on make-readies and punch list items so units are genuinely ready for new residents, not just technically turned.

You'll interact with residents regularly, which means your communication style matters as much as your technical skills. A friendly, calm presence when someone's frustrated about a maintenance issue goes a long way toward resident retention. That's not a soft skill, it's a real part of the job.

What You Bring

  • At least one year of hands-on maintenance experience in a residential community setting
  • Working knowledge across appliances, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, and general building systems
  • Comfortable with computers and basic software for work order management or communication
  • Strong written and spoken English communication skills
  • A detail-oriented approach to property inspections and safety compliance

The Fit and the Context

Berkshire Residential owns and manages its own properties, which means decisions get made closer to the ground than at a typical third-party management shop. Maintenance staff here tend to have a real voice in how things run at the property level. That's worth something if you're someone who takes ownership of your work and wants to be heard when you flag a recurring issue.

The pay range for this role in California runs from $24 to $28 per hour, depending on experience, with benefits that include health coverage, retirement, paid time off, and a meaningful rent discount for employees who live on-site or at a Berkshire community.

One thing that separates strong candidates in this type of role: the ability to prioritize well under pressure. On a busy day you might have a handful of open work orders, a unit turn in progress, and a resident standing at the office with an urgent request. The technicians who thrive here are the ones who can triage calmly, communicate honestly about timelines, and follow through without needing to be chased. That combination of technical competence and personal accountability is what makes the difference between a good hire and a great one.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Technician
job.description:
It's 9 PM on a Tuesday and a resident's heat is out. That call comes to you. That's the job, honestly, and knowing that upfront is more useful than a list of perks.

Fairstead is a vertically integrated affordable housing owner and operator with more than 30,000 units across 28 states. They develop, build, and manage their own properties, which means maintenance staff work within a single unified system rather than bouncing between ownership and a third-party management company. This Euclid, Ohio position carries a $2,000 signing bonus and sits at the core of keeping a residential property functional and safe for the people who live there.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Day to day, you're handling make-ready turns on vacated units, running preventative maintenance rounds, checking safety systems monthly, and working through resident work orders as they come in. Electrical diagnostics, HVAC checks, appliance repairs, and general building upkeep are all part of the rotation. You'll maintain a working inventory of supplies and tools, and you'll help enforce maintenance standards that protect the property's physical assets from misuse or premature wear. On-call rotation is part of the position, which means after-hours emergency calls are real and expected. The paperwork and communication side matters too. You'll need to document work clearly and coordinate effectively with property staff.

Fairstead operates with a tech-forward approach for an affordable housing company, including data-driven systems and digital tools. That doesn't eliminate the physical demands of the role, but it does mean you'll likely use software to log and track work orders rather than relying on paper-based processes.

What You Bring

  • Prior experience as a maintenance or service technician in a residential or commercial setting
  • Working knowledge of electrical systems sufficient to diagnose issues and complete minor repairs
  • General mechanical aptitude across plumbing, HVAC, appliances, and building systems
  • HVAC certification, CMRP, or equivalent credential (preferred, not required)
  • Ability to lift up to 70 pounds unassisted and stand for extended periods
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills
  • Attention to detail, especially on punch list items and unit inspections

The candidates who do well in roles like this one tend to be self-starters who can triage a work order list without constant direction. In affordable housing specifically, the resident population often depends on quick, reliable service in ways that are more immediate than in market-rate communities. That's not pressure meant to discourage anyone. It's just context for why responsiveness and follow-through matter here more than in some other settings.

Fairstead offers medical coverage through Meritain Health with a generous employer contribution, employer-paid vision and life insurance, a 401(k) with company match, 15 days of PTO, 7 sick days, 12 or more paid holidays, and a flexible spending account among other benefits.

job.title: Leasing Manager
job.description:
Student housing leasing management operates on a different calendar than conventional multifamily. You're selling beds a year out, managing a lease-up cycle tied to academic schedules, and working with a resident demographic that expects a social experience alongside a place to sleep. PeakMade Real Estate specializes in exactly this space, managing off-campus student communities across the country from their Atlanta headquarters. This Leasing Manager role sits onsite in Ithaca, New York, which puts you in a college market with real seasonal intensity.

What the Role Actually Covers

This is a dual-track position: half leasing leadership, half marketing execution. You'll hire, train, and manage a leasing staff while also owning the property's social media presence, digital content, and community programming. That combination is specific to student housing. Conventional multifamily rarely asks a leasing manager to shoot and edit content in Canva, manage online reputation across platforms like Reputation.com and JTurner, and still hit closing ratios. Here, that's the full job description.

On the leasing side, you'll conduct tours, sign leases (beds and apartments), support move-in and move-out events, and keep prospect traffic data current. Renewal programming falls under your scope as well, including lease renewal events and resident retention campaigns. On the marketing side, you'll develop and execute the annual marketing plan within budget, using social platforms, creative tools, and campus-specific outreach to drive traffic and conversions.

What PeakMade Is Looking For

  • 2 or more years of leasing experience specifically in off-campus student housing
  • Prior leadership experience, formal or informal
  • Hands-on comfort with Instagram, Facebook, Canva, Lightroom, VSCO, and property management software
  • Strong communication skills across in-person, phone, and online leasing channels
  • Flexibility for some evenings and weekends, especially during peak leasing season
  • High school diploma or equivalent required

The pay range runs $52,000 to $57,000 annually, with monthly, quarterly, and annual commission layered on top. PeakMade also offers a housing discount, 401(k) match, 15 days of PTO plus two additional wellbeing days, up to 12 weeks of paid parental leave, and a mentorship program.

A Note on What Separates Strong Candidates

In student housing, the leasing cycle is unforgiving. Pre-leasing for the following academic year typically starts in the fall, which means you're selling apartments to people who won't move in for another nine to twelve months. Candidates who've managed that timeline, kept traffic moving in the off-peak months, and still hit occupancy targets before the summer rush tend to do well in roles like this. If your background is conventional multifamily without student housing exposure, the calendar alone will be an adjustment. Two-plus years in the student space is a real requirement here, not a preference dressed up as one.

job.title: Maintenance Porter - Full-Time
job.description:
Porter roles at student housing communities carry more daily variability than most people expect. You're covering a lot of ground, often literally, and the standard of presentation matters because curb appeal and common area cleanliness directly affect leasing traffic and resident retention.

What the Work Actually Looks Like

Redstone Residential operates over 38,000 beds across 20 states, making them one of the larger third-party student housing operators in the country. This Eugene property is part of their broader conventional multi-family portfolio. The Porter role here is full-time at $18.00 per hour, and the core of the job is keeping the community clean, safe, and presentable every day.

That means common areas, hallways, parking structures, and outdoor grounds. Snow and ice clearing when the season calls for it. Trash and debris removal, including pet waste. Lawn and landscaping upkeep, watering, and general grounds care. You'll also assist the maintenance team with basic repairs and general tasks as needed, so some mechanical comfort helps even if this isn't a tech-heavy position. The expectation is that you manage your daily rounds with minimal supervision and bring a genuinely decent attitude when you cross paths with residents.

Qualifications

  • Prior janitorial or cleaning experience preferred
  • Ability to work independently and stay on task without constant direction
  • Physical capability to lift 50+ lbs. and remain on your feet for 4 to 6 hour shifts
  • Friendly, professional demeanor with residents and coworkers

Benefits and Growth

Redstone offers a solid benefits package for a full-time hourly role: health, vision, and dental coverage, 15 days of PTO plus 10 paid holidays, paid parental leave, three paid service days, short-term disability, and a 401(k) with up to 6% employer match. They also include a continued education program and professional development support, which matters more than it sounds for someone who wants to move into a maintenance technician role down the road.

Porter positions are a legitimate entry point into property maintenance careers. The people who advance from here tend to be the ones who treat the grounds like they own them, notice things before they become work orders, and build trust with the maintenance team. That track record opens doors to make-ready work, tech roles, and eventually lead maintenance. Redstone's scale means those opportunities exist internally if you want them.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager - WOODLEA ELDERLY
job.description:
It's Monday morning. A tenant's recertification deadline is two weeks out, her income documentation is incomplete, and the HUD 4350.3 clock is running. That's the kind of moment that defines this role at Woodlea Elderly in Wilmington.

Fairstead is a vertically integrated affordable housing owner and operator with more than 30,000 units across 28 states. The company brings development, construction, and property management under one roof, and it runs a tech-forward operation that includes Yardi, digital compliance workflows, and data-driven decision-making at the property level. Woodlea Elderly is part of that portfolio, serving residents in the HUD-subsidized, elderly housing space where compliance precision and genuine resident care carry equal weight.

What This Role Covers Day to Day

The Assistant Community Manager supports the Property Manager across the full spectrum of site operations. On the compliance side, you'll work within the HUD 4350.3 Handbook framework, assist with preparation for REAC reviews, Management and Occupancy Reviews (MORs), LIHTC reviews, and investor site visits. Annual and interim recertifications are part of your regular rhythm, and you'll use EIV to verify income data and flag discrepancies before they become findings.

On the financial side, you'll track arrears consistently, follow up with tenants per company policy, post and deposit rents daily, and create purchase orders in Yardi. Delinquency management at an elderly affordable property requires a particular combination of firmness and empathy. Many residents are on fixed incomes, and your follow-up approach will reflect that reality while still protecting the property's financial performance.

Resident relations are central to this position. You'll respond to questions, complaints, and service requests promptly (same day where possible, never beyond 24 hours), coordinate with maintenance on open work orders, and manage communication around move-ins, move-outs, and any on-site emergencies. You'll also support lease renewal efforts to maintain healthy occupancy and reduce costly turn activity.

When a compliance review is approaching, you'll be in the weeds: pulling files, confirming EHS violations are cleared, and making sure documentation is airtight. The property's audit readiness is a direct reflection of how well this role is executed.

Qualifications

  • Minimum two years of experience in affordable housing leasing or property management
  • Working knowledge of HUD programs and the 4350.3 Handbook
  • Hands-on experience with EIV, Yardi, and RealPage
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, especially for sensitive resident interactions
  • Familiarity with the Wilmington residential market is a plus

Candidates who stand out in this type of role tend to be detail-oriented enough to catch a certification error before it becomes a finding, and people-skilled enough to handle a frustrated elderly resident with patience. Both matter equally here. The compliance side can be learned and refined, but genuine care for residents in this demographic is harder to teach.

Fairstead offers medical insurance through Meritain Health, employer-paid vision and life insurance, a 401(k) with company match (100% of the first 3%, 50% of the next 2%), 15 days of PTO, 12 paid holidays, 7 sick days, and a flexible spending account, among other benefits.

job.title: Maintenance Supervisor
job.description:
What You'll Actually Do

This is a full-time, on-site maintenance role at a 202-unit apartment community in Pilsen. The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 7:30am to 3:30pm, with rotating on-call coverage for after-hours emergencies. Most of your day involves working through assigned work orders, keeping common areas clean and functional, and turning vacant units so they're ready for incoming residents.

Unit turns are a consistent part of the workload. That means punch list repairs, paint touch-ups, drywall patching, and general make-ready tasks that get a unit back to rentable condition. Beyond turns, you'll handle routine preventive maintenance on building systems, resolve minor plumbing and electrical issues, and do light carpentry and appliance repairs as needed.

Exterior upkeep is part of the job too. Trash pickup, snow removal, and seasonal amenity maintenance (including pool cleaning and basic equipment checks) all fall under this role. You'll work closely with the property manager to stay on top of priorities and make sure residents get responsive, courteous service when you're in their home.

What You Bring

  • Hands-on apartment or building maintenance experience
  • Working knowledge of electrical, plumbing, HVAC, carpentry, and appliance repair
  • Comfortable with hand and power tools
  • Physically able to lift up to 50 lbs, climb ladders, kneel, and bend as needed
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • Self-directed and reliable. You don't need someone checking in on every task
  • High school diploma or equivalent preferred

A Few Things Worth Knowing

Pilsen is a dense, active Chicago neighborhood. A 202-unit building in that area sees real daily wear, so the work order volume is steady. Technicians who do well in roles like this tend to be fast at diagnosing problems accurately on the first visit rather than returning multiple times. Residents notice the difference, and so does your manager.

The on-call rotation is real. If after-hours emergency response doesn't fit your life right now, that's worth weighing before you apply. For candidates who are fine with it, the Monday-through-Friday daytime schedule is otherwise predictable, which is a genuine advantage over some maintenance roles that run irregular hours throughout the week.

Benefits include health, dental, and vision insurance, a 401(k), paid time off, and a referral program.

job.title: Assistant Community Manager
job.description:
Student housing operates on a different clock than conventional multifamily. Lease-up happens in the fall for the following academic year, the turn is compressed into a few brutal weeks in August, and your residents' parents are often just as involved as the residents themselves. The Assistant Community Manager role at The Domain at Waco exists inside that specific rhythm, and the person who thrives here understands that the financial office and the leasing floor aren't separate jobs , they're the same job.

The financial responsibilities here are real and central. You own the delinquency process from first notice through payment plan negotiations to guarantor outreach to coordinating with legal on evictions when it comes to that. You're posting payments, reconciling ledgers, preparing weekly and monthly reporting on occupancy and variance, handling security deposit dispositions, and coding invoices against budget. Clean books aren't a bonus , they're the baseline expectation. If spreadsheets make you anxious, this isn't the right fit.

At the same time, you carry an individual leasing and renewal goal during pre-lease season. By-the-bed leasing has its own mechanics: roommate matching, unit assignments, guarantor verification, and the particular patience required when you're explaining a joint-and-several lease structure to a parent in Houston who's never rented an apartment. You'll work the full pipeline from lead to signed lease, support renewal campaigns, and participate in on-campus outreach. Baylor's student population is the market , knowing that calendar matters.

When the Community Manager is off-site, you run the property. That means you need to already understand how the pieces connect: what a delinquency spike does to NOI, why curb appeal on move-in day matters to retention, how a botched punch list during turn creates maintenance headaches for twelve months. You'll also help hire and train leasing staff and Community Assistants, participate in the on-call rotation, and assist with annual turn inspections, punch walks, and move-in readiness.

What separates strong candidates in this role isn't leasing charisma. It's follow-through. Student housing offices get loud in August and quiet in October, and the people who struggle are usually the ones who can close a lease but let the ledger slide, or who handle the front desk well but disappear when a parent calls upset about a damage charge. The job rewards people who close every loop, document every outcome, and treat the delinquency number as their own.

What Karya is looking for

  • At least one year in property management, leasing, hospitality, or a comparable customer-facing role
  • Comfort with ledgers, reconciliation, and spreadsheet-level math
  • Ability to work weekends and extended hours during pre-lease season, turn, and move-in
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation
  • Prior student housing or by-the-bed leasing experience is preferred, as is familiarity with Entrata or RealPage
  • Bilingual English/Spanish is a plus

Compensation includes an hourly rate, leasing commissions, renewal bonuses, and quarterly or annual performance bonuses tied to occupancy and delinquency targets. Medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with company match, and paid time off are included. A housing discount or on-site apartment may be available depending on circumstances.

job.title: Leasing Agent
job.description:
Urban lease-up shops live and die by first impressions, and at FLATS, the leasing agent is that impression. This Chicago-based lifestyle brand operates with a design-forward identity and a tech-integrated approach to apartment living, which means the leasing role here carries more brand weight than a typical Class B shop where you're just filling units.

What the Day-to-Day Looks Like

You'll own the full leasing cycle: fielding inquiries, conducting tailored tours, following up on leads through calls, texts, and email, and closing leases while hitting monthly targets. The follow-up cadence is where most leasing agents either earn their keep or fall behind. Traffic without conversion is just noise. Beyond closing, you'll handle applications, prepare lease documents, and keep records clean and compliant, which matters in Illinois where leasing activity is regulated and your license status is a real requirement. Either an Illinois Leasing Agent or Broker's License, or the ability to get a 120-day Student Permit before your start date, is non-negotiable here.

Move-in coordination is part of the role too. You'll make sure units are market-ready and that the move-in experience matches the brand promise. Resident concerns that surface early in a tenancy often land on the leasing agent's desk before anyone else's. How you handle those moments affects retention as much as it affects your own reputation on the team.

Weekend and evening availability is part of the job. That's true at most lease-up focused properties, and FLATS is direct about it.

What FLATS Is Looking For

  • Illinois Leasing Agent or Broker's License, or eligibility for a 120-day Student Permit
  • Prior leasing or sales experience, with a track record of closing
  • Strong written and verbal communication, the kind that works across email threads, phone calls, and face-to-face tours
  • Organized enough to manage multiple leads, applications, and move-in timelines simultaneously
  • Flexible schedule that covers evenings and weekends when prospect traffic peaks

Where This Role Can Take You

Leasing agents who develop genuine sales instincts and operational fluency tend to move into assistant manager or property manager roles within a few years. At a company like FLATS that runs multiple urban properties, internal mobility is realistic for people who demonstrate both closing ability and the kind of ownership mentality the company explicitly values. The skills that transfer are real ones: lead management, lease compliance, market comp knowledge, and resident relations. Those carry weight at virtually any multifamily operator.

What separates strong candidates here from average ones is the ability to sell the lifestyle authentically without it feeling like a script. FLATS leans hard into brand identity. Prospects who tour these properties are often choosing between a FLATS unit and several other well-appointed options in the same neighborhood. The agent who can articulate what makes the community distinct, and back it up with genuine product knowledge and a polished follow-up process, is the one who closes.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance
job.description:
Birgo operates a portfolio of residential properties across Cleveland, with this opening focused on Shaker Heights and Edgewater. The technician hired here will carry a broad scope: make-readies, preventative maintenance, and the full range of trade repairs that keep occupied units functional and turned units rent-ready on schedule.

What You'll Actually Do

Turns are the rhythm of this role. Drywall patches, paint, plumbing fixes, electrical troubleshooting, carpentry, HVAC checks , you'll move through make-ready punch lists and get units back online. Beyond turns, you'll handle day-to-day repair requests across multiple properties and run a preventative maintenance program that keeps deferred costs from compounding. Shaker Heights in particular has older housing stock, which means boiler systems show up frequently. Comfort with boiler operation and maintenance is a genuine advantage here, not a nice-to-have on paper.

The schedule runs Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., with participation in an on-call rotation for after-hours emergencies. That rotation is worth understanding before you apply: after-hours calls are real, and being prepared for them mentally is part of doing this job well.

You'll need your own reliable, insured transportation to move between properties, a valid driver's license, and the physical capacity to lift 50 pounds unassisted, work in confined spaces, and safely use power tools and ladders.

What You Bring

  • Hands-on experience across multiple trades: plumbing, electrical, drywall, painting, carpentry, and HVAC
  • Ability to work through a make-ready punch list efficiently and independently
  • Boiler experience (helpful, given the property locations)
  • Valid driver's license and personal, insured transportation
  • Eligibility to work in the United States
  • Physical ability to lift 50 pounds, use power tools safely, and work in confined spaces

The Bigger Picture

Birgo pays $23 to $26 per hour, weekly. Benefits include medical, dental, vision, and life coverage with employer contribution, paid time off, paid holidays, sick time, a 401(k) match, professional development reimbursement, and discounted rent at Birgo properties. The company describes itself as mission-driven, and its stated values include integrity, teamwork, and a genuine investment in staff development. For a technician who wants to sharpen skills across trade disciplines while working a predictable weekday schedule with a company that tracks professional growth, this is a solid setup.

What separates strong candidates here is range. Single-trade specialists will struggle with the variety this role demands. The technician who can close out a plumbing ticket, pivot to a drywall repair, and still troubleshoot a boiler issue before the end of the day is the one who'll thrive across Birgo's Cleveland portfolio.

job.title: Apartment Maintenance Manager
job.description:
Fairstead runs a portfolio of more than 30,000 apartments across 28 states, and they operate as a fully integrated owner, operator, and developer. That means maintenance leadership at their sites isn't just about fixing things. It's about holding a standard across a professionally managed affordable housing portfolio where operational consistency matters at scale.

This Service Manager role is based in Cleveland and puts you in charge of the day-to-day maintenance operation at the property. You'll supervise maintenance staff, manage special projects, and perform skilled hands-on work yourself when needed. The expectation is that you bring real trade depth, whether that's electrical, plumbing, HVAC, or another core discipline, plus the general maintenance range to handle what comes up between those specialties.

You'll own the condition of the building systems and the cleanliness and safety of the property's common areas and facilities. That means regular inspection of mechanical and electrical equipment, timely repairs, and keeping everything running in line with Fairstead's safety standards. When a complex project comes up, you won't be left alone to figure it out, but routine work is yours to manage independently. Overtime comes with the territory when emergencies or special projects demand it.

On the administrative side, Fairstead uses Yardi, and familiarity with that platform is a plus. You'll also work within Microsoft Office for documentation and reporting. The ability to implement and refine procedures matters here. Fairstead takes a tech-forward approach to operations, so a manager who can adapt to systems and data-driven workflows will fit better than someone who prefers to keep everything informal.

Qualifications

  • At least three years of property maintenance experience
  • Proficiency in a specific trade plus broad general maintenance skills
  • Solid knowledge of building and mechanical trade tools, techniques, and terminology
  • Strong grasp of safety protocols and accident prevention
  • Ability to supervise staff and lead projects
  • Comfort with Microsoft Office; Yardi experience is a bonus

Strong candidates for this role tend to have more than just technical skill. The ones who stand out can also communicate clearly with residents, hold their team accountable without micromanaging, and keep a punch list moving even when priorities shift mid-week. Affordable housing properties often have longer-tenured residents with higher service expectations than people assume. The manager who earns trust on the ground floor of the building earns it across the whole community.
